docs.title: Who reads the stores today
docs.text:
7.7 is the map from a frontend to the part of the chapter it depends on, with the Qt Source tab described in full. In short: the Qt debugger draws the source; GDB prints it (monitor src); ZRCP's smartload reaches the sidecars; scripts subscribe to FILE:LINE; the loop owners attach --source-map; DZRP has no source surface at all (DeZog reads the SLD or map itself).

The facade verbs themselves (load_map(), source_map(), source_location(), source_step(), subscribe_source_line()) are listed in 3.9.1.

docs.title: 7.1 Which memory supplied the instruction
docs.text:
A source map says "the bytes at $8C95 came from main.c:17". On a Next that sentence is incomplete, because $8C95 is a logical address and the logical address space is a window onto many memories: the MMU maps RAM pages into eight slots, and over them a ROM, the DivMMC's ROM or RAM, the Multiface, the alternate ROM or Layer 2 can be mapped. A program built for RAM page 20 and a ROM routine at the same logical address are different code with different source. So every range, label and line breakpoint carries the memory it belongs to, and every lookup supplies the memory that is mapped now.

That memory is a MemSpace (src/debug/mem_space.h, std headers only). When it names what supplied a read or an opcode fetch it is called a FetchSource, an alias of the same type (using FetchSource = MemSpace;) so that a grep finds the role.

One arbiter body answers every question. The record is taken after an instruction and goes into the trace and the call frames; the prediction is asked before one and feeds every lookup. The Execute filter has one predicate, used in three places.

docs.title: The kinds
docs.text:
A MemSpace is a Kind and a 16-bit index. Equality is by decode path, not by physical store: Layer2{p} and Page{p} share external SRAM for every p outside {0x0A, 0x0B, 0x0E}, and DivMmcRam{b}, Config{b}, the Multiface and the alternate-ROM windows all alias SRAM pages some Page{} also reaches. They stay distinct because the VHDL arbiter reaches them by different routes, and a debugger that shows which one answered must not collapse them. Cpu compares equal whatever its index (operator== in mem_space.h).

Kind index Store The VHDL (zxnext.vhd unless named) Cpu unused The live CPU mapping, overlays included. Never an arbiter result: it is the peek side's "whatever the CPU would see" Page NR 0x50-0x57 page number, 0..223 An 8 KB page. On the Next it is SRAM page n + 0x20, except n = 0x0A/0x0B (the bank-5 BRAM) and 0x0E (the bank-7 BRAM) mem_active_page zxnext.vhd:2952; slots 0/1 zxnext.vhd:3037-3043, slots 2-7 zxnext.vhd:3059-3065; zxnext.vhd:2961-2964 Rom 0..3 A 16 KB ROM image; the half is cpu_a(13) sram_rom, zxnext.vhd:3052-3057 BootRom 0 The 8 KB boot ROM (bootrom_en), mirrored through 0..0x3FFF; it sits above the whole SRAM arbiter zxnext.vhd:1856-1857, zxnext.vhd:3199-3204 MultifaceRom 0 0..0x1FFF while mf_mem_en: SRAM page 0x0A zxnext.vhd:2923, zxnext.vhd:3030-3035 MultifaceRam 0 0x2000..0x3FFF while mf_mem_en: SRAM page 0x0B zxnext.vhd:3030-3035 DivMmcRom 0 The 8 KB DivMMC ROM: SRAM page 0x08 zxnext.vhd:2921, zxnext.vhd:3084-3090; divmmc.vhd:94, divmmc.vhd:98 DivMmcRam bank 0..15 A DivMMC RAM bank: SRAM page 0x10 + bank zxnext.vhd:2926, zxnext.vhd:3092-3098; divmmc.vhd:95-96, divmmc.vhd:99 AltRom sram_alt_128_n (0 = Alt ROM0 128k, 1 = Alt ROM1 48k) The alternate-ROM read override, a 16 KB store: SRAM pages 0x0C + 2*index + cpu_a(13) zxnext.vhd:2924-2925, zxnext.vhd:3116-3122, selector zxnext.vhd:2981-3008 Layer2 layer2_active_page The Layer 2 CPU read mapping: SRAM page index + 0x20, never the BRAMs zxnext.vhd:2966-2969, zxnext.vhd:2971, zxnext.vhd:3100-3107 Config NR 0x04 The config-mode window, a 16 KB store: SRAM pages 2*index + cpu_a(13) zxnext.vhd:3044-3050 Floating 0 Nothing answers; the read returns the floating bus (0xFF in JNEXT) zxnext.vhd:3060-3061, zxnext.vhd:3101-3102

Three facts the table does not show:

  • The packing is bounded. Every value the arbiter produces fits 12 bits: kind <= 15 and index <= 0xFF. A static_assert in debug_types_check.cpp pins kind <= 15, and row FSRC-09 (mmu_integration_test) pins index <= 0xFF. MemCoverage relies on both (below).
  • Store size depends on the kind. space_size() is 0x4000 for Rom, AltRom and Config and 0x2000 for every other kind, and space_offset(s, logical) is logical & (size - 1). Every route the arbiter produces has exactly this offset.
  • Only some kinds are accessible to a verb. Debugger::peek() and poke() take Cpu, Page and Rom. DivMmcRam{b} can be read (the dot commands run from DivMMC bank 2, so their bytes must be checkable): bank b is DivMmc::ram_page(b) (SRAM page 0x10 + b, zxnext.vhd:3092-3098), a bank past DivMmc::kRamPages is InvalidPage (debugger_inspect.cpp:310-317), and poke of it stays Unsupported. Every other kind is identity-only: the arbiter names it, and peek and poke refuse it with Result::Unsupported (identity_only(), debugger_inspect.cpp:98, one total switch with no default, so a new kind is a compile error there). Rom is read-only (RefusedReadOnly). Coverage is the exception: mem_coverage() accepts the identity-only kinds.

docs.title: One arbiter
docs.text:
Mmu::route(addr) and Mmu::route_with(addr, divmmc_active, mf_active) (src/memory/mmu.h) are the single body that decides which memory answers a read, and they return a Route { space, offset, ptr }. The read, the opcode fetch, the debugger's prediction and the instruction-fetch record all come from it, in the VHDL's order, so they cannot disagree. 3.2 owns that body and its priority order; this page does not restate it. What this chapter needs from it is the space field.

route() uses the overlays as they are now. route_with() is the same body with the two overlays that an M1 fetch itself can switch, DivMMC's automap and the Multiface's $0066 latch, given as they will be for that fetch.

docs.title: The prediction and the record
docs.text:
A lookup happens before the instruction runs (the Source tab follows a PC that has not yet executed it, and a line breakpoint must match the fetch about to happen), but a fetch can change which memory supplies it. The system therefore has two views of one function.

The prediction. Emulator::predict_fetch(pc) (core/emulator.cpp) asks the overlay predictors, then the arbiter:

  1. predict_m1_overlays_(pc) mirrors the on_m1_prefetch hook in init(), but asks const predictors instead of the state machines. The DivMMC decision comes first (DivMmc::automap_m1_may_react() gates it; m1_automap_gates_() supplies the arbiter inputs; DivMmc::active_on_m1() is the answer and hold_after_m1() the hold for the next fetch), then the Multiface's (Multiface::would_latch_on_m1(), the $0066 fetch). m1_automap_gates_() is called by both the real hook and the predictor, so there is one copy of the inputs.
  2. Mmu::route_with(pc, o.divmmc, o.mf).space is the result.

Debugger::source_page(addr) (debugger_source.cpp) is predict_fetch(addr), and it is what every lookup passes: source_location(addr), the symbol lookup, the gutter, mem_coverage_fetch(). A DivMMC entry shows the idea: a delayed entry at RST $08 (NR 0xBA bit 1 clear) maps at the next M1, so the fetch at $0008 is still the RAM page and the one at $0009 comes from the DivMMC ROM, and the prediction at $0008 has to say RAM (row SRCDBG-ID-09).

The record. Mmu::read_m1() keeps last_m1_ = route.space for the first opcode byte of every instruction fetch; Mmu::last_m1() returns it, and MemSpace::cpu() ("none recorded") after construction, reset() and load_state() until the next fetch. Emulator::step_one_instruction() reads it once per instruction, after cpu_.execute(), and only if the CPU says it fetched an opcode (Z80Cpu::fetched_opcode_last_execute()):

  • The trace. TraceEntry::fetch_space() (debug/trace.h, stored as fetch_kind and fetch_index) is set by TraceLog::set_newest_fetch(). The entry is recorded before execution with cpu() provisionally and patched after; it stays 56 bytes.
  • The call frames. CallFrame::caller_space is the CALL's or RST's own fetch. target_space is recorded by the first fetch at target_pc and stays cpu() until then (and forever if none happens: a debugger moved the PC, or the esxDOS shim serviced the call). An INT or NMI frame has no fetch to record: its caller_space is the prediction at the interrupted PC, captured by CallStack::on_instruction_pre().
  • Slots that fetch nothing. An accepted INT, an accepted NMI and the esxDOS shim fetch no opcode, so last_m1() still holds the previous instruction's. Such a slot keeps no_fetch_space, the prediction for its PC, in its trace entry.

Because prediction and record are one function evaluated at two moments, they must agree for every instruction that fetches. The rows SRCDBG-ID-* in source_debug_test step instructions across DivMMC, Multiface, boot-ROM and NMI paths and compare the two; FSRC-* in mmu_test and mmu_integration_test pin the arbiter's order and identities against the VHDL.

docs.title: Spelling a space: the long address
docs.text:
One place spells a MemSpace for a human or a file: src/debug/long_address.* (std headers and mem_space.h only). Every Qt view, the trace export and the remote protocols that name a memory go through it (7.7).

  • The tag. space_tag() (long_address.cpp:46) is the stable name: Page{n} is P%02X (P04, P0E), Rom{i} ROM%u, BootRom BOOT, MultifaceRom MFROM, MultifaceRam MFRAM, DivMmcRom DIVROM, DivMmcRam{b} DIVRAM%u (decimal), AltRom{i} ALTROM%u, Layer2{p} L2P%02X, Config{b} CFG%02X, Floating FLOAT, Cpu CPU. The charset is [A-Z0-9]: no whitespace and no :.
  • The inverse. parse_space_tag() (long_address.cpp:64) is strict: digits only, any case, no leading zero on a decimal index, the hardware's ranges (a page 0..0xDF, ROM 0..3, DivMMC bank 0..15, alt ROM 0..1). It refuses PE5: a slot 2-7 that holds NR >= 0xE0 reads nothing, so SlotInfo::now is Floating while SlotInfo::space is Page{0xE5}. A view therefore names a slot by now, no protocol output tags space, and a view that shows the slot's own source shows FLOAT for a page >= 0xE0.
  • The tags are a stable format. The project file and the ghidra and skoolkit exports key on them, so changing a spelling is a format break, not a tidy-up (the header says so, in the comment on parse_space_tag, long_address.h:9-11). The trace export's FETCH= column is space_tag(fetch_space()) (trace.cpp:324), never the GUI's style (3.9.1).
  • The Next layout. physical_text(space, addr) (long_address.cpp:111) says where the byte sits in the Next's memory: $ and six hex digits of the SRAM address (Page{n} and Layer2{n} are (n + 0x20) << 13 | offset, zxnext.vhd:2964, zxnext.vhd:2971; Rom{i} i << 14 | offset, zxnext.vhd:3052-3057; alt ROM 0x018000 + 0x4000 * i, zxnext.vhd:2924-2925; Multiface 0x014000 / 0x016000; DivMMC ROM 0x010000 (SRAM page 8) and DivMMC RAM 0x020000 + 0x2000 * b (page 0x10 + b), zxnext.vhd:2921, zxnext.vhd:2926, zxnext.vhd:3085, zxnext.vhd:3093), or BRAM5+$XXXX (pages 0x0A, 0x0B), BRAM7+$XXXX (page 0x0E), BOOT+$XXXX, FLOAT. Banks 5 and 7 are block RAM, not SRAM, apart from page 0x0F; Layer 2 always sees the SRAM copy.
  • The style. space_text() and long_address() ($C000 P0E) choose by AddressStyle: Friendly prints the tag, Physical the physical text, and Physical falls back to Friendly wherever next_layout is false (a non-Next machine: memtext::next_layout(), memory_text.h:20).

The instruction at the PC is a special read. Debugger::memory_reader() (debugger_inspect.cpp:838) returns the bytes the CPU will fetch for that one instruction (Emulator::predict_instruction_bytes(), at most four) and Mmu::peek() for everything else, because at a DivMMC instant entry the M1 itself maps DivMMC. That is the prediction half of this page applied to the bytes instead of the identity.

docs.title: Two ways to name a memory in an Execute filter
docs.text:
An Execute subscription has two memory qualifiers (EventFilter in debug/events.h):

  • EventFilter::space is the canonical one: the FetchSource that must supply the opcode, compared exactly (kind and index) with Event::space. MemSpace::cpu() means no qualifier, since Cpu is never a fetch source. A source-line breakpoint names the memory its location was compiled into.
  • EventFilter::page is the legacy protocol qualifier. It compares Mmu::get_effective_page(slot) and nothing more, so it also matches a ROM or an overlay that carries that page number. DZRP's bank+1 (dzrp_server.cpp, sub.filter.page = page) and the DSL's page filter (script_engine.cpp) use it, because those protocols know pages and nothing else. dzrp-frontend.md stays a frozen design record of that meaning.

EventFilter::matches(ev) (event_table.cpp) applies both, after the kind and the range, and it is the only copy of the predicate. EventTable::filter_matches() calls it for the live gate and the boundary drain, probe_execute() calls it for the pure "what is armed at this PC" question (the step-off arm, and ZRCP), and history_stop_at() (debugger_source.cpp) calls it for Reverse Continue with an Event built from a trace entry. The gate's Event::space is the prediction; history_stop_at()'s is the record. 7.5 uses this.

docs.title: Coverage is keyed by the same identity
docs.text:
MemCoverage (debug/mem_coverage.h) records which bytes of which memory the guest executed, read and wrote: one flag byte per byte, COVERAGE_EXEC for the first opcode byte of an executed instruction (the M1), COVERAGE_READ for any other read (operands, data, DMA) and COVERAGE_WRITE for a write that landed. It is keyed by MemSpace, the decode path the arbiter named, so Page{p}, Layer2{p}, DivMmcRam{b} and Config{b} that alias one SRAM page stay distinct. Floating and Cpu are never recorded.

  • Storage. Lazily allocated 8 KB chunks in a flat table of 16 * 256 * 2 pointers: the key is (kind, index, offset >> 13), which is why the kind and index bounds above matter. A 16 KB store is two chunks.
  • A set, not counts. Setting a bit twice changes nothing, so a rewind's replay does not double count, and the set survives a rewind, a reset, a state load and a cold boot. Only mem_coverage_clear() and switching it off empty it.
  • Recording. Mmu::cov_note_() (memory/mmu.cpp) asks the arbiter again (it is pure) with the right direction and fetch view, and marks only a write that landed. Guest accesses only: a debugger peek or poke, a trace capture, video and a loader never count. Switched off, it costs a pointer test.
  • The source view. Debugger::mem_coverage_fetch(addr) is get(source_page(addr), space_offset(...)), the Disassembly's view. Debugger::executed_source_lines(file) walks SourceMap::file_ranges(file) and reports a line as executed when any byte of any of its ranges carries COVERAGE_EXEC, with each range's own space and space_offset().

This is a store, not a file format: nothing reads or writes a coverage file, and no DZRP, ZRCP, GDB or DSL verb exposes it. Its readers are the Qt Disassembly and Memory panels (disasm_panel.cpp, memory_panel.cpp), the Source tab, and --coverage (EmulatorConfig::coverage, applied by the three loop owners through apply_startup_coverage(), platform/coverage_startup.h), which switches it on at startup and logs a summary at exit. The separate logical-PC set of the INS-20 coverage verbs is described with the trace in 3.9.1.

docs.title: 7.2 The source map
docs.text:
SourceMap (src/debug/source_map.h, source_map.cpp) is the store for source positions. It knows no file format: an adapter (7.3) hands it a vector of ranges, and it builds the two indexes that answer the two questions the rest of the system asks. Which source line is this address? is a lookup by (memory, address). Where is this source line? is a resolve by file:line. It lives in a header with standard includes and debug/mem_space.h, so the adapters and their tests build without Qt or the emulator.

The same ranges, indexed twice. The example is main.c in the z88dk 2.4 sccz80 fixture: lines 16 and 17 share $8C95, line 14 shares $8C92 with line 15 but belongs to another function, and util.h:7 has three starts.

docs.title: What an adapter emits
docs.text:
struct SourceLocation { std::string file; int line; int column; };  // one-based; column 0 = absent
struct SourceRange    { FetchSource space; uint16_t lo; uint32_t hi_excl; SourceLocation location; };
struct SourceAlias    { std::string file; int line; size_t range; };

A SourceRange says that the bytes [lo, hi_excl) of one memory space came from location. The location has no address and no page: where the code is belongs to the range. hi_excl runs to 0x10000; a range with hi_excl == lo is zero-width. No adapter in this tree emits one, because every extent rule yields at least one byte (7.4); the type allows it and the store handles it: it is counted by size() and kept out of both indexes. A SourceAlias names a (file, line) that has no bytes of its own and the index of a range (in the vector given to replace()) it resolves through.

docs.title: replace(): one transaction
docs.text:
SourceMap::replace(ranges, aliases, identity, loaded_file, format, texts, dot) builds a complete new map and move-assigns it over *this as its last step, so an observer never sees a half-built store. The order of ranges is emission order and matters: it is the tie-break below.

  1. Normalise. A file name has \ turned into / and leading ./ removed (normalized_file()). Equal (file, line, column) triples share one entry in locations_.
  2. The line index. by_line_ maps (file, line) to the indices of the non-zero-width ranges of that line, in emission order. An alias whose range index is out of bounds is dropped; the rest go to aliases_.
  3. The address index. Take every edge (lo and hi) of every non-zero-width range, per memory, and sort them. The intervals between consecutive edges are segments; each segment lists, in cover_, every range that covers it. The segment's key is (space_key << 20) | lo, where space_key is kind << 16 | index (and Cpu always has index 0).
  4. The primary. The ranges of a segment are sorted shortest first and, on a tie, the one emitted later first (primary_first). The first is the segment's primary location.

loaded_file is the adapter's absolute, lexically normalised path (built as the local loaded: sld_loader.cpp:328, z88dk_source_map.cpp:1210), which is also where the search for a source file starts (7.7). identity, loaded_file, format ("SLD" or "z88dk"; clear() resets it to "SLD"), texts and dot (SourceMap::dot(): the map is a z88dk dot command's, so the backend never judges it from memory at a load, 7.6; clear() resets it) are stored as given. Every const SourceLocation* the class returns points into locations_ and is valid until the next replace() or clear(); code that keeps a location copies it. The backend does so before it calls anything that might load a map.

docs.title: Looking up an address
docs.text:
lookup(space, address) finds the segment by binary search and returns the primary location, or null when no range of that memory covers the address. It allocates nothing. Because the key is the memory and the address, code from a ROM slot or an overlay has a location only if a record names that memory; there are no unqualified records.

lookup_all(space, address) returns every covering location in the segment's order: the primary, then ascending length, then later-emitted first. That is the case of nested ranges: an adapter that emits a long range for a function and a short one for a statement inside it gets both, the statement first.

SourceMap::same_position(a, b) compares file, line and column, since one statement can emit several ranges. The source steps use it (7.5).

docs.title: Resolving a line
docs.text:
resolve("file:line") splits at the last :. The text before it is the file, the rest must be a decimal line number of at least 1; otherwise the result is empty with no error. The file is matched in two steps: an exact match against the files of the map, else the unique file whose path ends in "/" + text, a suffix on a component boundary. Two candidates make it ambiguous and the result is empty. A file that is not in the map is empty too, so a typo is silent at this level; the caller turns an empty result into its own message.

For a known file:

  • The starts are the line's entries. Every non-zero-width range of the line is a start at (space, lo), except a continuation: a range that begins exactly where another range of the same line in the same memory ends. A line that the compiler emitted as two adjacent ranges has one place to put a breakpoint, not two. The starts are sorted by (space, address) and unique.
  • An alias answers only when there are no starts. The line's alias, if any, gives the start of the range it points at.
  • No code. With neither, error is "no code at <expression>". That text appears only for a file the map names, which is how a caller tells "this line has no code" from "this file is unknown".

file_ranges(file) is the reverse listing for one file, with the path exactly as the map holds it (SourceLocation::file, no suffix matching): every non-zero-width range as {line, space, lo, hi_excl}, ordered by line. Coverage uses it (7.1).

files() is the set of every file the map names (ranges, zero-width ones included, and aliases), under the same exact names, in byte order; the Source tab's File list shows it (7.7).

docs.title: Embedded texts
docs.text: SourceText { origin, lines } is the text of a source file the toolchain did not keep: lines[i] is line i + 1, empty where the listing shows nothing, and origin names the listing it came from. The only producer is the z88dk listing adapter, which keeps the text of z88dk's generated start-up code (the .m4 files) from prog.lis (7.4.4). embedded_text(file) looks up the exact normalised name. Every replace() drops the previous texts, since they came with the previous map.

docs.title: The C variable store
docs.text: A z88dk map also carries the program's C variables. The adapter reads the __CDBINFO__ records into a VariableStore and hands it to replace(), which keeps it like the embedded texts: variables() returns that one shared, immutable object, a copy of the map shares it, and clear() and every replace() without one drop it. What it holds, and how it is joined to the map's symbols, is 7.9.

docs.title: Program identity
docs.text:
A map can carry a statement of what the program's bytes looked like when it was built, so a map for another build is not trusted. SourceProgramIdentity has two forms, either or both:

  • A hash (sha256, org, size): the SHA-256 of size bytes of logical memory from org, as they were right after the load. This is the SLD form (7.4.1). sha_matches() refuses size > 0x10000 - org.
  • Byte checks (bytes, a list of SourceByteCheck { space, lo, bytes }): bytes as they must read from one named memory at lo, lo + 1, and so on. This is the z88dk form, built from the section binaries beside the map (7.4.3).

has_identity() is true when either is present. verify_program(read, read_space) returns nullopt when there is no identity, otherwise whether it all still matches: the hash through read (logical memory), then each byte check through read_space for its own memory. A missing read_space, an unreadable byte or a different byte fails the whole check.

The backend supplies the two readers in Debugger::Impl::verify_identity() (debugger_source.cpp). The logical reader is Mmu::peek(). The space reader is Debugger::peek(Page{n}, addr & 0x1FFF) and accepts only Page: a byte check in any other memory reads nothing and so fails. It reads through Debugger::peek, not through the CPU's view, so a page is read whatever the MMU has mapped over it, and a debugger read touches no watchpoint and no latch.

docs.title: Units and spans, for programs that are not in memory yet
docs.text: A tape's program is not in memory when its map is attached. verify_spans() splits the identity into units, the things that can be judged separately: one per memory a byte check lies in, and, for the SLD hash (which hashes logical memory as one block), the single unit MemSpace::cpu(). A VerifySpan is the code the CPU is about to run, [lo, hi_excl) of space, which triggers the judgement of its unit; spans of one unit and space that touch or overlap are merged, and the list is empty for a map with no identity. For the hash form there is one span per non-zero-width range. verify_unit(unit, read, read_space) judges one unit: the hash for Cpu, the byte checks of that memory otherwise, and nullopt if the map has nothing to check there. 7.6 shows how the backend uses them.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• Where the ranges come from and what extent each adapter gives them: 7.4.
  • The FetchSource that qualifies every range: 7.1.
  • The facade verbs over this store (source_map(), source_location(), load_source_map()): 3.9.1.

docs.title: 7.3 Loading: the adapter contract, sidecars and ownership
docs.text:
Four entry points put data into the stores, and they differ in who asks and in what the result is filed under. This page is the contract the adapters keep, the dispatch that picks one, the search for the files that sit beside a program, and the ownership rule that decides which load may replace which.

A program load searches for sidecars and files what it finds as the program's (Sidecar). A hand load, from --source-map, Load Source Map or --map, is the user's (User) and is never touched by a sidecar.

docs.title: The adapter contract
docs.text:
Every adapter keeps the same promises, and a new one must too (7.8 has the checklist).

  • Parse the whole input before touching a store. load_sld() reads every line and calls map.replace() once, at the end; load_z88dk_source_map() places every record first and calls map.replace() last. A refusal returns before that, with the store untouched. The symbol loaders clear() their table only once the file has opened.
  • A source half is strict; a symbol half is lenient. A record the source half cannot place refuses the half, with a reason that names the line ("line 12: ...", "malformed SLD record at line N"). The symbol half skips what it cannot place and counts the rest: parse_label() in sld_loader.cpp returns false for a record that names nothing, and SymbolTable::read_z88dk_map() continues past a symbol no rule places. A bad source record must not cost the user their labels, and a label that does not fit 16 bits must not cost them their lines. The C variable records are lenient like the symbols: one the decoder refuses is kept in the store's refused() with its reason, one that cannot be joined stays unresolved with its reason, and neither refuses the lines (7.9).
  • One file can be two transactions. A z88dk map is read twice (SymbolTable::load_z88dk_map() for the symbols, load_z88dk_source_map() for the lines, which fills the C variable store in the same pass and hands it to the same map.replace(), 7.9). An SLD is read once and yields both: load_sld(map, path, &labels). A file refused as a whole (a missing header, a bad device or identity record) loads neither half and leaves both stores as they were; a bad trace record refuses only the source half, and the labels still load (SourceMapLoadResult::labels >= 0).
  • A listing is dropped alone. A z88dk .lis that does not hold up is left out with a note (SourceMapLoadResult::listing_notes), and its module keeps the map's records (7.4.4). It never refuses the map. The count reaches the frontends as SourceMapLoad::listings and the notes as SourceMapLoad::listing_note; the sidecar log says and N listings and one Warn per note.
  • Look before opening. source_file_problem(path) (debug/source_file.h) returns a reason, or empty. It refuses anything that is not a regular file (a FIFO or device would block or never end) and a file over SOURCE_FILE_MAX_BYTES, 64 MiB; a missing file is left to the open, which reports it. load_sld(), load_z88dk_source_map() (and the section binaries and .lis files it reads), load_z88dk_map(), load_simple_map() and load_nextbuild_memory() call it. The two sjasmplus-capable symbol loaders differ from the others as follows. load_z88dk_or_sjasmplus(), which serves --map, must open --map <(cmd), a pipe and so not a regular file, so it cannot ask first: it reads the file exactly once into memory, in chunks, and refuses the load when more than SOURCE_FILE_MAX_BYTES arrive ("input is over the 67108864-byte limit", table untouched), a pipe included. load_sjasmplus_equ() (MapFormat::SjasmplusEqu, the Qt Map menu's sjasmplus load) is a path the user picked, so it does call source_file_problem(), like the Map menu's other loaders; the menu shows the reason in its "Load Failed" box. load_z88dk_map() and load_simple_map() refuse such a file with the table untouched and say why through their optional why argument; the cap refusal is row Z88MAP-27. A file that merely fails to open returns -1 with why left empty (load_nextbuild_memory() alone sets "could not open Memory.txt file"), and the table is untouched there too (if (!file.is_open()) return -1; comes before clear()).
  • Emit only qualified ranges. Every SourceRange carries a FetchSource (7.1); the adapter decides it, and SourceMap never invents one.

A format is supported only once its extent rule (how far a record's range extends) and its space rule (which memory a record belongs to) are written down; those are the first two parts of every 7.4 page.

docs.title: Dispatch by content
docs.text:
Debugger::load_source_map(path, accept_identity_mismatch, verify_at_first_execution, dot_only) (debugger_source.cpp:452) is the hand load. After source_file_problem() it tells the format by content, never by extension: looks_like_sld() is true when the first line starts |SLD.data.version|, or when the file cannot be opened at all, so that the SLD loader's own error names it. Anything else is read as a z88dk map. A UTF-8 byte-order mark (EF BB BF) at the very start of the file is skipped first, by skip_utf8_bom() (source_file.cpp), in the router and again by load_sld() before it requires the first line to be exactly |SLD.data.version|1 (only a trailing CR dropped): a BOM'd SLD loads exactly as the same file without the BOM (owner decision, 2026-11-01; rows SRCDBG-Z88-30 and -33). Only the very first three bytes count: a second BOM, or a BOM after a leading blank line, is ordinary text, so such a file is not an SLD and goes to the z88dk adapter, which refuses it (SRCDBG-Z88-34). Every text loader skips it the same way: the z88dk source adapter, the --list listing reader (whose first header names a source and carries rows, so a BOM left in it would break the anchors and the file names), and the five symbol loaders behind --map and Debug > Map (z88dk, sjasmplus EQU, Simple, NextBuild Memory.txt, and the choose-by-content one, which erases one leading BOM from the bytes it read, as a pipe cannot be rewound). Rows: SRCDBG-Z88-35, MAPBOM-01..06, Z88LIS-44.

  • An SLD goes to load_sld(candidate, path, &labels).
  • A z88dk map goes to load_z88dk_source_map(..., Z88dkListings::Beside); its symbols stay with load_map() and --map. A map whose load returns count == 0 (built without -debug, no usable listing) is refused with "no source lines in '<path>' ..." and the listing notes appended.

Before the map is filed as the user's, load_source_map() checks the program identity (7.2): a mismatch is refused unless accept_identity_mismatch, and for a program that is not in memory yet (verify_at_first_execution, used for tapes) a map with an identity attaches pending (7.6). Only then does the user's store take it. SourceMapLoad::identity_note is the suffix a frontend appends to its report: verified, not verified for lack of section binaries, or verified for the code the binaries cover with N ranges unchecked (identity_note() in debugger_source.cpp).

Debugger::load_map(path, MapFormat) (debugger.cpp) is the symbol-file load. MapFormat has five values: Z88dk, Simple (SYMBOL = $ADDR), NextBuild, SjasmplusEqu and Z88dkOrSjasmplus. The last is the one --map uses (ScriptHost, script_host.cpp): SymbolTable::load_z88dk_or_sjasmplus() reads the file once into memory and lets its first line pick the loader (an sjasmplus EQU line, whatever its value, or anything else, an empty file included, taken as a z88dk map). It is by content because sjasmplus names its files freely and z88dk's assembler writes a .sym of its own, in the map format. On success the symbols become the user's and a rule-4 z88dk symbol takes the RAM page predict_fetch says is mapped (SymbolTable::bind(), 7.4.3); on failure (-1) the table and its owner are as they were.

docs.title: --source-map
docs.text:
EmulatorConfig::source_map_file is set from --source-map FILE (EmulatorConfig::source_map_file, src/main.cpp:878, :2193). EmulatorConfig::source_map_no_program (emulator_config.h:298), set at src/main.cpp:2207, says which of three cases it is: 0 a program loads and the map follows it; 1 there is no --load; 2 an RZX replay is the program (--rzx-play, or --load R.rzx, told by the extension).

With a program (0). Each loop owner (headless_app.cpp, sdl_app.cpp, gui/qt_app.cpp) calls load_program_sidecars() after its first successful --load and then emulator_attach_cli_source_map() (platform/emulator_boot.h:112), the same call as a hand Load Source Map with a mismatch refused. A refusal logs an error and the run exits 1. When the program is a tape (program_loads_later()) the helper passes deferred, the map attaches pending, and the loop owner watches it once per tick with emulator_poll_cli_source_map() (source_map_watch_): a map dropped by the check logs --source-map: dropped: <reason> and exits 1.

Without one (1 and 2). There is no program to judge a map by, so only the map of a z88dk dot command is accepted. Each loop owner makes the load once, at start-up, before ScriptHost::start(), so a file:line rule in a script resolves (the guard is source_map_no_program: headless_app.cpp:77-91, sdl_app.cpp:252, gui/qt_app.cpp:353). The call is emulator_attach_cli_source_map(dbg, file, deferred = false, dot_only = true, rzx = (case 2)), which passes dot_only to load_source_map(). After the adapter has parsed the file, dot_only && !candidate.dot() returns SourceMapLoad::not_dot with the error "it is not the map of a z88dk dot command" (SourceMapLoad::not_dot, debugger_source.cpp:494), and the helper words it for the frontend: --source-map requires --load FILE, or the map of a z88dk dot command: '<file>' is not one, or, for case 2, --source-map with an RZX replay accepts only the map of a z88dk dot command (SourceMapLoad::not_dot, emulator_boot.h:120-125). The refusal makes the start-up fail (exit 1). A dot map is deferred whatever verify_at_first_execution says: defer = (verify_at_first_execution || candidate.dot()) && !verify_spans().empty() (verify_at_first_execution, debugger_source.cpp:502), so it attaches pending with the note "identity check pending: the dot command loads when it runs", and source_map_watch_ is set from the result. How it is then judged is 7.6; how its sections are placed is 7.4.3, rule 5.

docs.title: The sidecars of a program
docs.text:
Debugger::load_program_sidecars(path) is called after every successful --load in the three loop owners (headless_app.cpp, sdl_app.cpp, gui/qt_app.cpp) and by Debugger::load() (debugger_reconstruct.cpp), which is what a remote client's load verb runs. It looks beside the program for three kinds of file, using the non-throwing std::filesystem calls and accepting only a regular file (a FIFO would block the load; a broken or looping link is "no sidecar"):

Sidecar Search Applies to NextBuild symbols <stem>.Memory.txt, then Memory.txt in the program's directory (nextbuild_sidecar()) a .nex only SLD <stem>.sld, then <stem>.sld.txt (load_sld_sidecar()) any program z88dk map <stem>.map (z88dk_map_sidecar(), program_has_z88dk_map()) .nex, .tap, .sna

source_file.cpp holds the one table of program formats: .nex and .sna load at once, .tap, .tzx and .wav load later (program_loads_later(): the machine reads them over the following frames), and only .nex, .sna and .tap have a z88dk map.

Symbols. The user's symbols are never touched (logged as "Kept the loaded symbols ... not loading ..."); their rule-4 symbols are re-bound to the pages mapped now at every program load. Otherwise the program's store is assembled in one block, in this order, first wins on every key (SymbolTable::merge()):

  1. Memory.txt;
  2. the SLD's L labels, when the SLD file is not refused as a whole, its identity does not mismatch and the user's source map is not kept (an SLD with no label is not a symbol source);
  3. the z88dk map's symbols, last, and only when no Memory.txt exists and its identity does not mismatch.

The log says what was attached, by log->info(): Loaded N SLD labels from '<file>' (log->info(), debugger_source.cpp:780) and Loaded N z88dk symbols from '<file>' (log->info(), :786).

If nothing attached, a previous program's Sidecar symbols are cleared, also when the new Memory.txt cannot be read (SidecarLoad::symbols_unreadable): a previous program's data never survives into one it does not describe.

Sources. The user's source map is kept if there is one (logged). Otherwise a previous Sidecar map is cleared, then: the SLD's source half if an SLD file exists, even a refused one, whose refusal is reported; only if there is no SLD file at all, the z88dk map's source half. A z88dk map with neither symbols nor line records is not a map: ignored without a word. A map whose section binaries or hash do not match memory is rejected whole, its symbols included. A tape program's identity cannot be judged at the load call, so its map attaches pending.

Ownership. Each store has an owner, Impl::StoreOwner: None, Sidecar or User, tracked explicitly because an empty-looking store can still be the user's (a map of ; const lines only). The rules, all in debugger_source.cpp and debugger.cpp:

  • Ownership changes only on a successful load.
  • A sidecar load never touches a User store. A user's source map is carried into the new load generation without a second verification (the machine has not changed since the load call).
  • A hand SLD's labels become the user's symbols (Impl::attach_hand_labels(), symbols_from_sld), unless the user loaded a MAP (then the count is -1, the MAP kept). A hand SLD with no labels clears only an earlier hand SLD's labels.
  • Debugger::clear_source_map() and clear_symbols() set the owner to None.

What was refused. SidecarLoad::problem is the one-line account of what was found and refused: NextBuild symbols '<file>' rejected: <reason> and/or source map '<file>' rejected: <reason>, joined by "; ", empty when nothing was refused. The file is named, not the program. load_program_sidecars() fills it and logs each refusal as well. The headless loop warns --load: <problem>, the SDL loop load: <problem>, the Qt loop hands it to DebuggerManager::report_sidecars() in a debugger build (the log and the main window's status bar for ten seconds) and warns otherwise, and a remote Debugger::load() logs load: <problem> at Warn to every client. The Source tab reads the reason for the source half from source_map_status().reason, which the next load or drop replaces.

For a program that is not in memory when the load call returns, see 7.6.

docs.title: 7.4.1 sjasmplus SLD
docs.text: SLD, "Source Level Debugging data", is the only format here that carries a machine's memory model, one record per instruction and the labels in one file. It is the format JNEXT likes best, because it names the page of every instruction.

docs.title: 1. The producer
docs.text:
sjasmplus, option --sld[=FILE]. The fixtures were made with sjasmplus v1.23.1 (z00m128/sjasmplus commit 46aae3fa784cae903345b87bd6b9db16a77c4bea):

sjasmplus --sld=equlabels.sld equlabels.asm

Without a file name the default is the first source's name with the extension sld.txt (OpenSld_buildDefaultNameIfNeeded(), sjasmplus sjasm/sjio.cpp:1605), which is why the sidecar search tries both <stem>.sld and <stem>.sld.txt (7.3). Records are written only for code assembled inside a DEVICE (IsSldExportActive() needs a device id; the sjasmplus manual, docs/documentation.xml chapter c_sld_data, line 5479).

docs.title: 2. The writer
docs.text:
All in sjasmplus:

  • sjasm/sjio.cpp:1587 writes the first line, |SLD.data.version|1. An optional ||K|KEYWORDS|... line follows (sjasm/sjio.cpp:1588-1597).
  • sjasm/sjio.cpp:1629-1687, WriteToSldFile(), writes every record. Its own comment (sjasm/sjio.cpp:1630-1666) documents the layout; the snprintf is at sjasm/sjio.cpp:1683: "%s|%s|%s|%s|%d|%d|%c|%s\n". The position is line[:colBegin[:colEnd]] (WriteToSldFile_TextFilePos(), sjasm/sjio.cpp:1573-1578).
  • The device record: sjasm/devices.cpp:275-291 builds pages.size:%d,pages.count:%d,slots.count:%d,slots.adr:A,B,... and writes it as a Z record with page and value -1.
  • The L record's data, module,main,local[,+trait...], is built by ExportLabelToSld() (sjasm/tables.cpp:135-185); the module markers module,,,+module and module,,,+endmod by ExportModuleToSld() (sjasm/tables.cpp:187). The traits written are +local, +equ, +macro, +smc, +reloc, +reloc_high, +used, +struct_def, +struct_data and +sizeof (sjasm/tables.cpp:174-183).

docs.title: 3. The grammar
docs.text:
A line is either the version line, a comment, or a record of eight |-separated fields:

|SLD.data.version|1
||<anything>
<file>|<line>[:<col>[:<endcol>]]|<deffile>|<defline>|<page>|<value>|<type>|<data>
Field Meaning file Source file, never empty in a record line The source position: the line, then optionally the start and end column deffile, defline Where the instruction was defined, when that differs (inside a macro); 0 otherwise page The device page of value; -1 where the value is not an address in a page value A 16-bit address, or a full 32-bit value for an EQU type T instruction trace (data empty), D an EQU symbol, F a function label, L a label, Z a device (memory model) change data By type: empty, the name, the name, module,main,local[,+traits], pages.size:...

docs.title: 4. The parser's rules
docs.text:
load_sld() in src/debug/sld_loader.cpp applies these, in file order.

  1. Header. Line 1 must equal |SLD.data.version|1 (a trailing CR is dropped), else "missing SLD.data.version 1 header" and the whole file is refused.
  2. || lines are comments, except ||program.name, ||program.sha256, ||program.org and ||program.size, which are the identity (below). A || line without a : is ignored.
  3. Eight fields. Any other line is split on | and must have exactly 8 fields, else "malformed SLD record at line N".
  4. Z, the device. Page and value must be -1. parse_device() requires pages.size:, ,pages.count:, ,slots.count:, ,slots.adr: in that order; a page size of exactly 8192; 1 to 224 pages (the Next's 224 8 KB RAM pages) and at least one slot; as many slot addresses as slots.count, each in 0..0xFFFF, strictly ascending, none that would run past 0x10000, none overlapping. Exactly one device record is allowed ("SLD contains multiple device records", "SLD must contain one device record"). Every device error refuses the whole file.
  5. T, a trace (source half). A trace before the device record is an error; so is an empty file field, a non-empty data field, a position that is not line[:col[:endcol]] with each number at least 1 (parse_position()), a page outside [0, pages.count) or above 0xFF, or an address outside 0..0xFFFF. The line and the start column are kept; the end column and the definition fields (deffile, defline) are ignored, so a macro's instructions map to the line that invoked it. The range is {Page{page}, address, hi, {file, line, column}}.
  6. L, a label (symbol half, only if a label table was given). parse_label(): the data is split on ,; at least three parts and a non-empty main are needed (so module markers name nothing and are skipped). The name is module.main.local with the empty parts and their dots left out, as sjasmplus --sym spells it. The address must be 0..0xFFFF. A record whose traits include +struct_def is a struct's size or a field offset, not an address: it goes to the name-only values (add_value()). +sizeof only says that SIZEOF(label) was used somewhere, and the record is an ordinary label (sjasmplus sjasm/tables.h LABEL_HAS_SIZE). A page of -1 makes an unpaged label; any other page must be in [0, pages.count) (and at most 0xFF), else the record is skipped.
  7. Failures of the source half. Without a label table the first bad record returns an error at once. With one, the scan goes on and the first error is kept (source_error) so the labels still load: the source half is refused (count == -1, labels >= 0), the label half is not. The device and identity errors are never recoverable this way.
  8. No traces. With no trace record and no earlier error: "SLD contains no source traces".

docs.title: 5. Space and extent
docs.text:
Space. A trace in page p belongs to MemSpace::page(p): the SLD page number is the device's 8 KB page number, which for DEVICE ZXSPECTRUMNEXT is the NR 0x50-0x57 number, so a record is exactly the memory it names (7.1). value is the CPU's logical address and is kept as the range's lo.

Extent. A trace has a start and no end, so the adapter gives it one (sld_loader.cpp, near the end of load_sld()): the range covers its instruction up to the next distinct start in the same page, and never past the end of the 8 KB window it starts in, (lo & 0xE000) + 0x2000. Records that share a start share the extent. A zero-width range cannot result.

docs.title: 6. Identity
docs.text:
sjasmplus writes no program identity. ||program.name, ||program.sha256, ||program.org and ||program.size are a jnext convention that a build script appends (introduced with the SLD identity check); grep -rn program.sha256 ~/src/spectrum/sjasmplus finds nothing. They are all or none:

  • the SHA-256 must be exactly 64 lowercase hex digits (valid_sha256()), else "invalid SHA-256 in SLD program identity";
  • all four must be present, program.name non-empty, org at most 0xFFFF, size at most 0x10000 and org + size at most 0x10000, else "invalid or incomplete SLD program identity".

The identity then is SourceProgramIdentity { sha256, org, size }; the name is only checked. It is the hash form of 7.2: the SHA-256 of size bytes of logical memory from org, as they were right after the load. A bad identity refuses the whole file, labels included.

docs.title: 7. What is skipped
docs.text: D (EQU symbols) and F (function labels) records are well-formed records the loader does not use (the same names arrive as L records). The ||K|KEYWORDS| line is a || line. A +struct_def record, a module marker, a label whose value is past 0xFFFF or negative (an EQU of 0x10000 or -1), and a label in a page the device does not have are skipped as labels. The definition position is ignored (rule 5).

docs.title: 8. Excerpt
docs.text:
From test/fixtures/sjasmequ/equlabels.sld, produced by sjasmplus v1.23.1 from equlabels.asm (unmodified, 50 lines; lines 1-4 and 13-22 shown):

|SLD.data.version|1
equlabels.asm|3||0|-1|-1|Z|pages.size:8192,pages.count:224,slots.count:8,slots.adr:0,8192,16384,24576,32768,40960,49152,57344
equlabels.asm|5||0|-1|16384|D|SCREEN
equlabels.asm|5||0|-1|16384|L|,SCREEN,,+equ,+used

equlabels.asm|18||0|-1|2|L|,point,,+struct_def
equlabels.asm|18||0|-1|0|L|,point.x,,+struct_def
equlabels.asm|18||0|-1|1|L|,point.y,,+struct_def
equlabels.asm|21||0|4|32768|F|main
equlabels.asm|21||0|4|32768|L|,main,
equlabels.asm|21||0|4|32768|T|
equlabels.asm|22||0|4|32771|T|
equlabels.asm|23||0|4|32774|F|main.loop
equlabels.asm|23||0|4|32774|L|,main,loop,+local,+used
equlabels.asm|23||0|4|32774|T|

main at 32768 ($8000) is page 4. The two T records at 32768 and 32771 become the ranges Page{4}:[$8000, $8003) for line 21 and [$8003, $8006) for line 22 (the next distinct start in the page is 32774, which is line 23's). point, point.x and point.y are name-only values (sizes and offsets), and SCREEN is unpaged (page -1).

The identity records are synthetic: no public producer writes them, and there is no committed fixture. This is the SLD that write_text builds in code in test/debug/source_map_test.cpp:144-154, to exercise the identity check; kNextDevice is the Z record's tail (kNextDevice, source_map_test.cpp:85-87):

|SLD.data.version|1
||program.name:game.bin
||program.sha256:9f64a747e1b97f131fabb6b447296c9b6f0201e79fb3c5356e6c77e89b6a806a
||program.org:32768
||program.size:4
main.bas|6||0|-1|-1|Z|pages.size:8192,pages.count:224,slots.count:8,slots.adr:0,8192,16384,24576,32768,40960,49152,57344
main.bas|6||0|4|32790|T|
...

The hash is of the four bytes 01 02 03 04 at $8000.

docs.title: 9. The rows
docs.text:
• source_map_test: SLD-* (the parser's refusals and acceptances), SLDL-* (labels, with equlabels.sym as the oracle for names and values), SRCRNG-* (extents and resolution), SRCMAP-*, SRCPATH-*, SYMPG-*.
  • source_debug_test: SRCDBG-SIDE-* (the sidecar), SRCDBG-SYM-*, SRCLIFE-* (7.6).
  • Functional: sld-labels-func and source-map-func.
  • test/fixtures/sjasmequ/README.md records how equlabels.sld and sizeof.sld were made.

docs.title: 7.4.2 sjasmplus --sym and --exp
docs.text: Two plain files sjasmplus writes for a different purpose than debugging, which JNEXT reads as a list of labels. They carry a name and a value and nothing else: no source line, no page, no type.

docs.title: 1. The producer
docs.text:
sjasmplus options --sym=FILE (every label) and --exp=FILE (only the names a source EXPORTs). The fixtures were made with v1.23.1 (commit 46aae3f):

sjasmplus --sym=equlabels.sym --exp=equlabels.exp equlabels.asm

An older sjasmplus wrote --sym differently. Up to v1.17.0 CLabelTable::DumpSymbols() wrote NAME: equ 0x%08X, with the keyword in lower case and the labels in definition order; from v1.18.0 --sym shares the writer of --exp (test/fixtures/sjasmequ/README.md, "equlabels-v1.17.sym"). --exp has always said EQU.

docs.title: 2. The writer
docs.text:
In sjasmplus v1.23.1:

  • WriteLabelEquValue(), sjasm/sjio.cpp:1433-1443, writes NAME: EQU 0x and the value as 8 upper-case hex digits (PrintHex32).
  • --sym: CLabelTable::DumpSymbols(), sjasm/tables.cpp:610-624, calls it for every symbol in name order, skipping a name that starts with a digit (a temporary label) and a keyword (sjasm/tables.cpp:619-620; the call is at sjasm/tables.cpp:621).
  • --exp: WriteExp(), sjasm/sjio.cpp:1445-1447, called by the EXPORT directive (sjasm/directives.cpp:1707). A name exported twice is written twice (the fixture has counter at both of its values).
  • Both files are opened in text mode (SJ_fopen(), sjasm/support.cpp:47-50), so a Windows build ends every line with CR LF.

docs.title: 3. The grammar
docs.text:
<name>: EQU 0x<hex>

<name> is the label as sjasmplus spells it: module-qualified (gfx.draw), with a local label's parent (main.loop), a struct's fields (pos.x), and for --exp the name the EXPORT gave (draw). The value is the full 32-bit aint: a label or EQU above 0xFFFF is written as it is, and a negative one as 0xFFFFFFFF.

docs.title: 4. The parser's rules
docs.text:
parse_equ_line() in src/debug/symbol_table.cpp is the one definition of an EQU line. The loader and the first-line check that picks it both use it, so they cannot disagree about what a line is.

  1. A trailing CR is dropped.
  2. The line must contain ": EQU 0x" or ": equ 0x", exactly, found with find(); a separator at column 0 is not one. The two spellings are the current and the pre-v1.18.0 writers; no other case or spacing counts.
  3. The name is everything before the separator and must contain no space, tab or :.
  4. The value is the whole rest of the line: at least one hex digit and nothing else, fitting 32 bits (std::from_chars).

SymbolTable::read_sjasmplus_equ() then keeps the line when the value is at most 0xFFFF (so 0x00010000 and 0xFFFFFFFF are skipped) and adds an unpaged label. The first line at an address wins for the address and, apart, the first for a name (add_label()); the count it returns is the lines accepted, duplicates included.

Every entry is a label, whatever the source declared it with: a code label, an EQU, a DEFL, a struct's size or a field offset. The file has no type to tell them apart.

SymbolTable::load_sjasmplus_equ(path, why) first asks source_file_problem() (7.3): a file that is not a regular file, or is over the size cap, is refused with that reason before it is opened. It then opens the file, returns -1 if it cannot (the table untouched), clear()s and reads.

SymbolTable::load_z88dk_or_sjasmplus(path, why) is what --map uses: it reads the file once into memory (at most SOURCE_FILE_MAX_BYTES of what arrives; more is refused, 7.3), asks parse_equ_line() of its first line, and passes the whole text to read_sjasmplus_equ() or read_z88dk_map(). The first line is enough because a real --sym may open with a negative or oversized value, so the test is "is it an EQU line", whatever its value.

docs.title: 5. Space and extent
docs.text: None. A label from these files is unpaged: it names its address in every memory. Two labels at $C000 in different DEVICE ZXSPECTRUMNEXT pages (banked and other_bank in the fixture) are therefore the same address with two names: both names resolve to it, and the address is displayed by the first one the file lists. For per-page labels use the SLD (7.4.1), which carries the page.

docs.title: 6. Identity
docs.text: None.

docs.title: 7. What is skipped
docs.text: Any line that is not an EQU line; values above 0xFFFF and negative values; temporary labels (sjasmplus does not write them).

test/fixtures/sjasmequ/equlabels.sym, written by sjasmplus v1.23.1 (all 18 lines, byte for byte; NEG and PASTTOP are the two the loader skips):

PASTTOP: EQU 0x00010000

SCRSIZE: EQU 0x00001B00

The --sym of v1.17.0 for the same source is test/fixtures/sjasmequ/equlabels-v1.17.sym; its first lines are SCREEN: equ 0x00004000 and SCRSIZE: equ 0x00001B00 (lower-case equ, and definition order, so NEG is no longer first). equlabels-win.sym is the Windows build's: the same bytes with a CR before every line feed.

docs.title: 9. The rows
docs.text:
• debugger_backend_test: SYM-19 to SYM-32, including two rows that glue equlabels.sym to a comment, a blank line or to a z88dk map to prove that the first line picks the loader.
  • script_events_test: SCRIPT-HOST-MAP-SJASM, -EXP, -V117, -CONTENT.
  • debugger_verbs_test (Qt): QMAP-05, QMAP-06.
  • Functional: script-map-pipe-func feeds equlabels.sym to --map through a pipe.
  • test/fixtures/sjasmequ/README.md has the commands, the commit and the sha256 of every file.

docs.title: 7.4.3 The z88dk map
docs.text: The z88dk linker map is the one file that feeds both stores, by two separate loads. Its addr lines are the symbols. A build with -debug adds two kinds of marker symbol, __C_LINE_ and __ASM_LINE_, whose names and addresses are the source lines, and a third kind, __CDBINFO__, the C debug information, which the variable store reads (7.9). The map carries no length for a line and no page for an address: both have to be derived from the section a symbol lives in.

docs.title: 1. The producer
docs.text:
z88dk's assembler, z80asm, writes the map when zcc is given -m; the line markers appear only with -debug. The fixtures were made with two installs, built for the Next with zcc +zxn ... -m --list -subtype=nex -o prog -create-app (the exact commands are the + zcc ... lines of each build.log):

Fixtures Tree Commit test/fixtures/z88dk/v2.4/ z88dk 2.4, ~/src/spectrum/z88dk-original-2.4 4d530b6eb779ad0f2a1d13c0bb670cf717477501 (v2.4) test/fixtures/z88dk/master/ z88dk master before the debug-record fixes, ~/src/spectrum/z88dk-original-97731e4e29 97731e4e2988543e2c849cd1ae1d0aeddf372fcd (v2.4-2883-g97731e4e29) test/fixtures/z88dk/master-fixed/, master-fixed-zsdcc/ z88dk master after them, ~/src/spectrum/z88dk-original-latest 0f0a1cf70e48856af8191af6f86096d2e1362482 (v2.4-2954-g0f0a1cf70e) test/fixtures/z88dk/nightly/ the nightly z88dk-20261107-965fd0e628-26852, ~/src/spectrum/z88dk-original-965fd0e628: the float-format symbols of every C module (__fp_mode, __fp_exponent_bias, __fp_mantissa_size) 965fd0e628 (master, 2026-11-06) test/fixtures/z88dk/v2.4-fp/ the same float program as nightly/, built by 2.4 (no such symbols) 4d530b6eb779ad0f2a1d13c0bb670cf717477501 (v2.4)

A map built without -debug has symbols and no source lines. Several -debug builds do not exist: 2.4's sdcc -debug fails to assemble (defc Gcounter0_00==. syntax errors, fixed on z88dk master) and the classic +zxn banked -debug is not producible on 2.4 (Unknown option2 --hardware-keyboard; master builds it since v2.4-2883). test/fixtures/z88dk/README.md records both.

docs.title: 2. The producer's writer
docs.text:
In z88dk:

  • The map line. z80asm src/z80asm/src/c/symtab1.c:598-616 (master; the same line is src/z80asm/src/c/symtab1.c:641 in 2.4): name padded, then = $%04lX, then ; type, scope, def, module, section, file:line, then strstrip(). The def field is the word def or empty. An empty section shows as , ,, and a symbol with no file ends after the section: the trailing blanks are stripped (const, public, def, , ,).
  • __C_LINE_<n>_<enc>. Preproc::do_c_line(), src/z80asm/src/cpp/preproc.cpp (master src/z80asm/src/cpp/preproc.cpp:1721-1755, the symbol built at src/z80asm/src/cpp/preproc.cpp:1746-1747; 2.4 src/z80asm/src/cpp/preproc.cpp:1309-1310). Only if (g_options.debug). <n> is the directive's line operand (C_LINE 17,... gives __C_LINE_17_) and <enc> is url_encode() of the string operand (main.c::main::1::3): master preproc.cpp:1706, 2.4 preproc.cpp:1272. It keeps isalnum() characters and writes every other byte as _ and two lower-case hex digits.
  • One symbol per (line, scope). if (!find_local_symbol(...)) (master preproc.cpp:1748, 2.4 preproc.cpp:1311): only the first occurrence of an identical name is defined. That is why sccz80 emits one __C_LINE_18_ where main.c.lis has four C_LINE 18, (README finding G1).
  • __ASM_LINE_<n>_<enc>. asm_cond_LABEL(), src/z80asm/src/c/directives.c (master src/z80asm/src/c/directives.c:76-95; the encoder url_encode() is at src/z80asm/src/c/directives.c:35-53; 2.4 src/z80asm/src/c/directives.c:88 and src/z80asm/src/c/directives.c:35). Defined at a label, if (option_debug() && !sfile_is_c_source()), so a label in assembler that came from C gets no ASM_LINE. In sdcc builds these numbers are lines of the generated assembly, not of main.c (README G14).

docs.title: 3. The grammar
docs.text:
NAME = $HEX ; type, scope, def, module, section, location
Field Values type addr (a place in memory) or const (a number: a size, a section bound, a defc); the parser recognises only these two scope local or public in the fixtures; not interpreted def def or empty module The module name; for a .c file <file>_c (zcc heads each file with MODULE <file, non-alphanumerics to _>) section The section the symbol lives in, empty for a symbol in none location file:line, the rest of the line (it can hold commas and a TAB)

The location in a -debug line record takes one of three forms: file:line (assembler), file::func::level::block:line (sccz80, 80cc), and sdcc's file::x::<level><TAB>:line, where the TAB marks a function it did not give.

docs.title: 4. The parser's rules
docs.text: parse_z88dk_map_line() (debug/z88dk_space.cpp) is the one tokenizer. A line needs an =, then a ; after it; the value is $ and hex digits up to 64 bits (__clib_malloc_heap_size = $FFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF exists); the fields after the ; are split at the first five commas and the sixth is taken whole. A line that does not parse is not a symbol record; the caller decides if that is fatal.

docs.title: The symbol half
docs.text:
SymbolTable::read_z88dk_map() (debug/symbol_table.cpp) reads the whole file first, because the map is sorted by name and a section's head may come after its symbols.

  1. Names starting __C_LINE_, __ASM_LINE_ or __CDBINFO__ are skipped: they are not symbols, and sorted by name they would otherwise win the address of the function label.
  2. A const line goes to a table of constants (first wins, 64-bit; the page heads come from it) and, when the value fits 16 bits, becomes a name-only value (add_value()): lookup_name() and @name resolve it, but it never names an address, so a size or a section bound is never shown in a disassembly.
  3. An addr line is placed in the second pass, in file order, first occurrence wins. A value above 0xFFFFFF is skipped. Otherwise z88dk_section_space() (below) decides: a paged label; a label bound at load; an unpaged label (only if the value fits 16 bits); or nothing.
  4. C symbols. An addr symbol whose name starts with _ and a second character other than _, and whose module ends in _c, is a C symbol: zcc's compilers write every C identifier with a leading _, and __x names are runtime internals. add_label(..., c_symbol=true) records its key under the C name (the name without the first _, c_name_to_key_) with the first C symbol winning. find_name() tries that after every exact name and constant, so a real counter always wins; lookup() and nearest() show the C name only when nothing else holds it and the label's own key is the one it resolves to (otherwise the assembler name, which is the case of a second C module's local _util_inc); lookup_assembler() keeps the assembler name for text that must assemble.

docs.title: The source half
docs.text:
load_z88dk_source_map() (debug/z88dk_source_map.cpp) is strict and reads the file twice over: pass 1 collects line records, symbols, and the __<group>_head and _tail constants; pass 2 places the line records in file order, so the first refusal is the first bad line.

  1. A line record whose section is empty is dropped: = $0000 ; addr, local, , main_c, , is "no code" (README G2; the 2.4 sccz80 -debug map has 80 of them).
  2. A record whose location is line 0 is dropped (is_line_zero()): sccz80 and 80cc write C_LINE 0,"<file>::<func>::0::1" on entering a file, and "no source line is numbered 0" (G22).
  3. A value above 0xFFFFFF refuses the half ("address $... does not fit 24 bits").
  4. The location is parsed (parse_location(): the text after the last : is the line, at least 1; a TAB before it marks an unknown function); an unparsable one refuses the half.
  5. The space is decided by z88dk_section_space() (with the dot verdict, rule 5 of the space rules below); Unpaged and Refused refuse the half with a reason naming the map line; a bind-at-load record asks the space_of function the caller supplies (Emulator::predict_fetch), and an address that is not in a RAM page refuses it too ("address $... of section '...' is not in a RAM page").
  6. The records are grouped by (space, address) for ownership and extent, below.

docs.title: Space
docs.text:
z88dk_section_space(section, value, page_head, dot) (debug/z88dk_space.cpp) maps a section name and a (possibly 24-bit) value to a Z88dkSpace. Page numbers are 0..223, banks 0..111; the numbers in a section name are 1 to 3 decimal digits.

The block first. Since z88dk nightly 2026-10-21 z80asm writes the block, the top-level section, of each section in its __<section>_head line (__game_const_head = $103546 ; const, public, def, , BANK_8_CODE,). appmake puts the section's code in the bank its block names, so a user section such as game_const is in bank 8 although its own name says nothing. Both halves fill a Z88dkBlocks table from those lines (first wins) and pass it as a fifth argument; when the section has a block and the block names a bank by appmake's rule (mb_enumerate_banks(): the first of BANK, DIV, PAGE, in zxn's order, found anywhere in the block name and followed by _<n>; what follows the number is free), the section is placed by its block: BANK_<n> as rule 2, with _L / _H right after the number fixing the half; PAGE_<n> as rule 1 with the head __<block>_head; DIV_<n>, the ranges and the dot rules as below. Messages then name the section and its block. A section with no block (an older map) or whose block names no bank (CODE) takes the rules below on its own name, unchanged.

The rules, in order of the section name:

  1. PAGE_<n> and <KIND>_PAGE_<n> (KIND is CODE, RODATA, DATA or BSS): a section that starts in page n and may run into the next ones. The head is z88dk_page_head(): the low 16 bits of the constant __PAGE_<n>_head (newlib puts the page in bits 16-23, which are not read). The page is n + (((head & 0x1FFF) + (addr16 - head)) >> 13). With no such constant, an address below the head, or a result past page 223, the value is unpaged.
  2. BANK_<n> and <KIND>_<n>, with _L or _H, and for RODATA/DATA also <n>_align_<m>: a 16 KB bank, which is the two pages 2n and 2n + 1. _L is page 2n, _H is 2n + 1, and a plain or aligned name uses bit 13 of the low 16 bits of the address.
  3. An unnumbered section with a value above 0xFFFF is refused: nothing says which bank it is in.

  4. Any other section, and a value of 16 bits: bind at load. The memory is the RAM page the MMU maps at that address with the program in memory, found with the same predict_fetch the source lookups use. In the symbol half this is the lenient form: SymbolTable::bind(space_of) gives the page only when space_of(addr) is a RAM Page; ROM, DivMMC and the other overlays leave the symbol unpaged; an empty function unbinds all. It runs at load_map(), at the sidecar <stem>.map (a tape's too, at the attach) and for the user's store at every program load.

  5. A dot command. NextZXOS copies a dot command's file into a DivMMC RAM bank and runs it from $2000 there; the map names no bank. z88dk_dot_command(consts, &why) (z88dk_space.cpp:275) says whether a map is one: the constant startupoffset is $0100 (dot), $0200 (dotx) or $0300 (dotn) and __CODE_head is $2000. No startupoffset, or another value, is not a dot and has no reason; a dot whose __CODE_head is not $2000 is not a dot and its reason ("a dot command's CODE must start at $2000") refuses the source half (dot_why, z88dk_source_map.cpp:777-779), while the symbol half places the map as any other (z88dk_dot_command(), symbol_table.cpp:84, no reason asked). Both halves read the __<s>_head/_tail constants and startupoffset (z88dk_source_map.cpp:757; the symbol half keeps every constant). For a dot, z88dk_section_space() takes it as a last argument, after rules 1 to 3 (a value above 0xFFFF in an unnumbered section is still refused) and before rule 4, for unnumbered sections only:

    • an unnumbered section at $2000-$3FFF is DivMmcRam{kNextZxosDotBank}, bank 2 (kNextZxosDotBank, z88dk_space.cpp:192-197), whatever the MMU maps there when the map is loaded;
    • a dotx's other unnumbered sections are rule 4: its main part (PROG.X, prog_MAIN.bin at CRT_ORG_MAIN $8000) is main RAM;
    • in a dotn those sections, and every PAGE_<n> / DIV_<n> section, are refused (refused_dotn(): NextZXOS allocates those pages when the command runs, __z_page_table; the reason says to build it as a dotx to debug it);
    • a dot's or dotx's PAGE/DIV sections follow the rules above, and DIV_<n> stays unpaged.

    The bank is measured, not documented: booting NextZXOS in JNEXT and typing a dot, a dotx and a dotn, the file lands in bank 2, E3 becomes $82 (conmem and bank 2) and the CPU executes $2000 (fixtures README, G24; kNextZxosDotBank, z88dk_space.h:46). SourceMap::replace(..., dot) remembers the verdict (SourceMap::dot()), which 7.6 uses for the identity.

A number above the limit of its family (223 for a page, 111 for a bank, 15 for DivMMC) makes the value unpaged when it fits 16 bits and refused otherwise.

A DIV_<n> or <KIND>_DIV_<n> section (DivMMC memory) is unpaged with the reason "a DIV_n bank is the one the program, or a dotn command's allocator, chooses when it runs": the bank is the program's to choose, so the map cannot say it. The symbol half keeps a 16-bit symbol of it as an unpaged label, and the source half refuses a line record in it.

In a numbered section the bits of value above 15 are not read.

docs.title: Extent and ownership
docs.text:
A line record has a start and no end. extent() in load_z88dk_source_map() gives a record the first of:

  • the next line start in the same memory (any placed record, owners and aliases);
  • the next addr symbol of another module in that memory;
  • the section's __<section>_tail (the distance tail - value, when the tail is above the value and under 0x10000);
  • the start plus 0x400 (kMaxLineSize, DeZog's MAX_C_LINE_SIZE);
  • the end of the 8 KB window, (lo & 0xE000) + 0x2000.

Records at the same (memory, address) are a group: the highest line owns the range. A lower line of the group is an alias (it resolves through the owner's range) if it is in the same module and the same function: both functions are known and equal (the ::func:: part of the location), or, when either is unknown (sdcc), when no _-prefixed symbol of that module at that address is located at a later line of the same file (later_function_entry(): a function whose entry is at that address and whose line is after the lower line's). A duplicate (file, line) in a group is dropped. Any other lower line has no code: resolve() says so (7.2). In the fixture, main.c:16 is the alias of main.c:17 at $8C95 and main.c:14 (in square) has no code at the $8C92 that main.c:15 (in main) owns.

docs.title: 6. Identity
docs.text: The section binaries z88dk writes beside the map, <map stem>_<GROUP>.bin, are the identity. A group comes from a constant __<GROUP>_head and must have no lower-case letter (__code_compiler_head is a section, not a group; on a case-insensitive file system it would name the same file). The file must be a regular file under the size cap, and unreadable ones refuse the half. For each range of a section that is not data (data*, bss*, smc*, case-insensitive), the binary that holds both its first and last byte, with both ends in the range's memory, supplies a SourceByteCheck { space, lo, bytes }. A range no binary covers is counted in SourceMapLoadResult::unchecked, and no binary at all means no identity. This is the byte-check form of 7.2.

docs.title: 7. What is skipped
docs.text: __C_LINE_, __ASM_LINE_ and __CDBINFO__ symbols in the symbol half; line records in an empty section and line-0 records in the source half; any symbol a space rule refuses or leaves unpaged beyond 16 bits; const values wider than 16 bits as names; lines that do not parse as map lines.

docs.title: __CDBINFO__
docs.text:
These records are z88dk's C debug information, in a different encoding from the line markers:

  • Encoding. Only isalpha() characters are kept; every other character, digits included, is _ and two lower-case hex digits. Writers: sccz80 src/sccz80/cdbfile.c:13-24 (both trees, defc __CDBINFO__<enc> = 1 at src/sccz80/cdbfile.c:85-87), 80cc src/80cc/cdbfile.c:7-18 (master only). For sdcc, zcc folds the temporary .adb file into the assembly (zsdcc_embed_adb(), master src/zcc/zcc.c:2041-2072, called when peepholeopt is non-zero: zcc's -O, src/zcc/zcc.c:588, src/zcc/zcc.c:1551), with a variant encoder that also keeps whitespace (zcc.c:2026-2038). The value is always 1, so the line is const.
  • Content. After decoding _hh, a record starts M: (module), F: (function), S: (symbol) or T: (type). The reference decoder is z88dk's own debug_add_info_encoded() (src/ticks/debug.c:656), called from src/ticks/syms.c:173.
  • Duplicates. z80asm ignores a second definition (symtab1.c:117).
  • In JNEXT. The symbol loader skips them (symbol_table.cpp, rule 1 above). The source half keeps the const lines that start __CDBINFO__ and decodes them into the C variable store (7.9); it takes no symbol from them. A test also decodes the names of the C identifiers to check the C names above (Z88CN-01).
