docs.title: 7.4.4 z88dk listings
docs.text: A z88dk map says where a C line starts. A listing says what every line of a source file compiled to, byte by byte. JNEXT reads the listings that sit beside a map to fill what the map cannot: every assembly line (the map has only the first __ASM_LINE_ of a label), sdcc's C lines on z88dk 2.4 (whose map has no __C_LINE_ at all), and the text of the generated start-up code. The listing adapter is src/debug/z88dk_lis.*; z88dk_source_map.cpp calls it.

docs.title: 1. The producer
docs.text: z80asm --list, requested through zcc --list. It writes <file>.lis for every user source (main.c.lis, asmfn.asm.lis) and <program>.lis for zcc's start-up code (prog.lis, 12 to 18 thousand lines; the fixtures keep it for four builds only). A listing is the assembler's view: addresses are section-relative, and a module is listed under its own name, not the path the map uses (MODULE util_c in game/util.c.lis, module game_util_c in the map; README finding G18).

docs.title: 2. The producer's writer
docs.text: z80asm src/z80asm/src/cpp/lstfile.cpp (list_open(): 2.4 src/z80asm/src/cpp/lstfile.cpp:202, master src/z80asm/src/cpp/lstfile.cpp:213). The layout is LstFile::out_line() (master src/z80asm/src/cpp/lstfile.cpp:131-177, 2.4 src/z80asm/src/cpp/lstfile.cpp:126-168) with the widths at src/z80asm/src/cpp/lstfile.cpp:26-29 (identical in both trees): a 6-wide line-number column, 2 blanks, a 4-digit hex address (the section-relative or phased pc), 2 blanks, 16 characters for at most 8 bytes, 2 blanks, and the source text from column 32. Bytes beyond the eighth continue on rows that repeat only the bytes. LstFile::out_filename() (master src/z80asm/src/cpp/lstfile.cpp:122-129, 2.4 src/z80asm/src/cpp/lstfile.cpp:117-124) writes <name>: on its own line whenever the file changes, which includes the files z80asm is reading through INCLUDE, a C_LINE's file operand and a macro's source (the .m4 text of the start-up code).

docs.title: 3. The grammar
docs.text:
<file>:                                 a file header, no leading blank
nnnnnn  AAAA  bb bb ...   <text>        a row: line number, address, bytes, text
                    bb bb               continuation of the bytes of the row above
nnnnnn                    <text>        a row with no bytes (a label, a directive, a comment)

The line-number column holds the line of the file the header names (for a C module, the C line a C_LINE set). Row texts that matter here:

  • MODULE name, LINE n,"file", C_LINE n,"file::func::level::block" and SECTION name, PHASE, DEPHASE, REPT...ENDR, MACRO...ENDM.
  • For sdcc with --c-code-in-asm, comments ;file:line: text.
  • Labels, either name: or sccz80's .name.

docs.title: Reading a listing: parse_z88dk_listing()
docs.text: A strict tokenizer. It refuses, naming the physical line ("line N: ..."), a file that is not a z80asm listing: a header not ending in :, a row before the first header, a line-number column holding something other than digits and blanks, columns 6-7 not blank, a malformed address or byte field, and a byte continuation with no row to continue. The result is a list of rows (phys, col, header, has_addr, addr, bytes, text) and the headers.

docs.title: Placing it: place_z88dk_listing()
docs.text:
It interprets one parsed listing against the map, seen through a Z88dkMapView (the map's symbols and line records, its __<group>_head/_tail constants, a place function that is z88dk_section_space(), and the section binaries' bytes). In order:

  1. Macros. A MACRO definition (MACRO name, name MACRO, name: MACRO, to ENDM) is listed once, at its definition, and not assembled there, so its rows are ignored in the walk (README G20). A macro whose body, transitively, switches section (SECTION, PHASE, DEPHASE), or a SECTION/PHASE inside a REPT body, makes the bytes of its expansion impossible to attribute: the whole listing is dropped with a note.
  2. The module. The last MODULE directive wins (z80asm keeps the last one; zcc's own MODULE zxn_crt0_asm comes first, README G19). With none, the stem of the first LINE operand, else the listing's own file name without .lis. If the caller named the modules this listing may declare (accepted, built from the map's module symbols: a file game/util.c is game_util_c in the map and util_c in its listing), a listing of another is dropped; the module must also be one the map has.
  3. The mode. If any C_LINE directive is present the listing is CLine (sccz80, 80cc, and master's sdcc): the source lines are the C_LINE markers. Otherwise, if the LINE operand names a .c file, Comment (sdcc on 2.4): the ;file:line: comments. Otherwise Asm: the listing's own file and line-number column. A Comment listing without a single such comment is dropped ("it has no line information (sdcc writes it with --c-code-in-asm)").
  4. The walk. Per row: SECTION sets the current section, PHASE/DEPHASE the phased flag. A byte row outside PHASE must sit at the section's running pc (the address column continues where the section left off, "a section's listed addresses start at 0 and are continuous", README G21); a break means the walk lost the section (a SECTION in a false IF branch, for one), and the listing is dropped ("expected $X, the listing has $Y; the listing cannot be followed"). A byte row is an item: its section, address, byte count, whether its first token is a Z80/Z80N mnemonic, and its source location (in Asm mode its own file and column; otherwise the current C_LINE or comment marker of its section). In CLine mode the walk also keeps every C_LINE operand (Z88dkListedScope): the LAST directive before a byte row owns that row, and the row's map value is the occurrence's. fill_listing_scopes() gives an 80cc function that table instead of the map's one __C_LINE_ symbol per (line, scope) (Z88ZB-12, Z88ZB-13).

  5. Anchors and the offset. A label row of the walk is an anchor when the map has an addr symbol of that name in this module, in the same section, whose map location is this very row (<header>:<line-number column>). The anchor gives offset = map value - listed address for its section. All anchors of one section piece must agree, or the listing is dropped ("this is not the listing of this build"). A piece with no anchor falls back to __<section>_head when tail - head equals the piece's byte count (p.pc, z88dk_lis.cpp:610-619). A smaller piece is placed by its bytes (5b below). A piece with none of these, and anything inside PHASE, cannot be placed; those rows are counted and reported as "N listed lines could not be placed". 5b. A label-less piece smaller than its section is placed by its bytes (design 9.5). Another module can put code in the same section: the banking driver shares code_crt_init with the CRT in the banked-CRT fixtures, so the CRT's own piece has no label in the map and is smaller than the section. place_z88dk_listing() (z88dk_lis.cpp:398) tries every start c from __<s>_head to __<s>_tail minus the piece's size and excludes it when, at any checked row, the section binary holds a byte other than the listing's first byte. A checked row is the first byte of a mnemonic row, outside PHASE, in a non-data section; the rest of an instruction is never compared, because the linker patches operands and z80asm never patches an opcode, so a listing of this build is never excluded at its true start. The byte at c + row address comes from view.byte_at(value, space), where place() gave the space; it is unknown (nullopt) when no section binary covers the byte, when two or more do (overlay sections at one ORG: bin_for(..., &more), z88dk_source_map.cpp:870, and the byte_at lambda, :942-948), and when place() fails (a ROM area: the memory is not a RAM page, so no byte can be read). The outcome is one of three:

    • no start survives (survivors, z88dk_lis.cpp:664; the search loop over survivors, z88dk_lis.cpp:621-671): the listing is dropped, with "section '': its label-less lines match no place in the section binary; this is not the listing of this build" (row Z88LIS-42);
    • exactly one survives and every checked byte was known: the piece starts there (Z88LIS-36 and -37 on the banked-CRT fixtures: the CRT piece is placed and the driver's bytes after it are left without a line; Z88LIS-38 with a patched defw and a PHASE row);
    • several survive, or the one left has an unknown byte: nothing is guessed. The piece's rows are not placed and are counted in the "could not be placed ... do not fit exactly one place in the section binary" note, while the listing's other pieces stay (Z88LIS-39, -40, -41, -45, -46; a data section has no checked rows, so both starts survive, Z88LIS-43).

      • The loop stops at the second survivor (survivors < 2). This rule replaced "the size must be equal", which left 17 lines of the CRT unplaced when the map and the listing disagreed by one byte (Z88LIS-19, re-specified).

    • Placement and the first-byte check. An item's map value is offset + address (a value above 0xFFFFFF drops the listing); place() supplies the memory and 16-bit address, or a reason that drops the listing. For a mnemonic row in a non-data section the section binary's byte at that value must equal the listing's first byte, else the listing is dropped ("holds $X in the section binary, the listing says $Y"): operands are module-relative in a listing, the opcode is not. The check abstains where the byte is unknown (no binary covers it, or two do): a labelled piece over two overlapping section binaries is kept (Z88LIS-47). An item with a location gets a SourceRange of [lo, min(lo + bytes, 8K window end)). One range per byte row, so the several rows of one line are adjacent ranges of the same line, which resolve() collapses into one start (7.2, "continuation").

    • Zero-width lines. A marker with no bytes of its own resolves through the next byte row of its section, as an alias. In Asm mode a marker is a label row with no bytes that the map names (an anchor); in the C modes a marker directly followed by bytes owns them (no alias), and one followed by more markers aliases the next byte row, except that when a function-entry label (one starting _) intervenes only the last marker before it does. One alias per (file, line).
    • The cross-check. Every map line record of this module is compared with the listing: a __C_LINE_ record with where the first C_LINE of the same operand string sits, an __ASM_LINE_ record with the first anchor label row at that header:line. It agrees when the section matches and position + offset == value. Disagreements do not drop the listing; they are counted and the first three named in one note ("the listings disagree with the map at N of M line records (first: ...); the listings were used").
    • Embedded text. Every row under a header ending .m4, with a line-number column from 1 to 1,000,000, is kept as that line of that file; lines[i] is line i + 1.

docs.title: Choosing listings: load_z88dk_source_map(..., Z88dkListings::Beside)
docs.text: The candidates are <map stem>.lis (the start-up code; it may be a listing of any module of the map) and <file>.lis for every source file named by the location of the map's module symbols and line records, path relative to the map. A candidate that is not a regular file is ignored without a word. One that fails source_file_problem() or parse_z88dk_listing(), or is dropped by a rule above, adds a note and the module keeps the map's records. A second listing of an already-listed module is ignored with a note. A module that does get a listing takes its lines from it: its map records are erased and the listing's ranges and aliases follow the map's. The notes are logged one Warn each, the listings counted in the attach line ("and N listings"), and carried to the frontends in SourceMapLoad::listing_note (hand load) or the log (sidecar); a map with no line record can still supply ranges from a listing.

docs.title: 5. Space and extent
docs.text: Space. The same as the map: z88dk_section_space(section, value, page_head) (7.4.3) on offset + address, through Z88dkMapView::place. Extent. The bytes of the row: [lo, lo + n), cut at the 8 KB window end. There is no guess, unlike a map record's extent.

docs.title: 6. Identity
docs.text: A listing carries none. Its ranges join the map's when the section binaries' identity is built, so they are byte-checked like the map's own (7.4.3).

docs.title: 7. What is skipped
docs.text: Rows inside a macro definition; the first-byte check of rows that do not start with a mnemonic (data) and of data sections; bytes inside PHASE; rows of a section piece with no offset (no anchor, no head fallback, and no single verified start by its bytes); and, per listing, every reason in rules 1-8 that drops it whole.

docs.title: 7.4.5 NextBuild Memory.txt
docs.text:
Memory.txt is the label list that the Boriel ZX Basic compiler can write and that NextBuild asks for on every build. It is the only thing from the BASIC toolchain that JNEXT reads. It has an address and a name per line and nothing else, so a program built this way has symbols and no source lines.

Boriel ZX Basic writes no SLD, and no tool in this chain writes the ||program.* identity records either. Where a BASIC project does have an SLD, some other tool produced it.

docs.title: 1. The producer
docs.text:
The Boriel ZX Basic compiler, zxbc, option -M FILE / --mmap FILE, "Generate label memory map" (boriel-basic/zxbasic, src/zxbc/args_parser.py:151, read on main at 29f0b2f0ce, 2026-11-01). NextBuild (em00k/NextBuild, read at 364b2d13c5) runs zxbc in-process from Scripts/nextbuild.py, after os.chdir() to the program's source folder (Scripts/nextbuild.py:70), with the argument pair '-M','Memory.txt' in each of its three compile calls: headerless (Scripts/nextbuild.py:400), tape (Scripts/nextbuild.py:404) and the default .bin (Scripts/nextbuild.py:406). The call that writes assembly ('-A', Scripts/nextbuild.py:409) has no -M. So the file lands as Memory.txt in the source folder, next to the .nex NextBuild goes on to make.

The URLs of both are in doc/REFERENCES.md.

docs.title: 2. The producer's writer
docs.text:
zxbc.main() writes the file at src/zxbc/zxbc.py:230-233: f.write(asmparse.MEMORY.memory_map). The property is src/zxbasm/memory.py:301-306:

return "\n".join(sorted("%04X: %s" % (x.value, x.name) for x in self.global_labels.values() if x.is_address))

The global labels that are addresses, HHHH: name, sorted as strings (so by address, since the hex is upper-case and four digits), joined with line feeds and no trailing one. The leading . of a name is how the assembler spells the root namespace; the compiler prefixes every user identifier with _.

docs.title: 3. The grammar
docs.text:
HHHH: <label>

HHHH is the 16-bit address in hex; <label> is the assembler label, such as ._Main, or a runtime label such as .core.__LABEL.

docs.title: 4. The parser's rules
docs.text:
SymbolTable::load_nextbuild_memory(path, why) in src/debug/symbol_table.cpp:

  1. source_file_problem() first (not a regular file, or over 64 MiB, returns -1 with why set and the table untouched); a file that does not open sets why to "could not open Memory.txt file". Only then is the table clear()ed.
  2. Per line: the text before the first : is the address, trimmed, and must be a whole field of hex digits that fits 16 bits (parse_hex16()); the rest, trimmed (blanks, CR and LF), is the raw label and must not be empty. Any other line is skipped.
  3. The shown name drops a leading ., and then one leading _ if the next character is not _: ._Main is shown as Main. A name that begins __ keeps its underscores (.core.__LABEL is shown as core.__LABEL). A name that is empty after that is skipped.
  4. add_label(display, addr, nullopt): an unpaged label (first wins, by address and apart by name), then add_name() for the raw text and for the raw text without its leading ., so Main, ._Main and _Main all resolve to the address. The return value counts the lines accepted.

The count is what load_program_sidecars() logs: Loaded N NextBuild symbols from '<file>'. The same loader serves MapFormat::NextBuild (Debugger::load_map()).

docs.title: 5. Space and extent
docs.text: None. A label from Memory.txt is unpaged and names its address in every memory. The file carries no page, so a BASIC program in a banked page needs its SLD (if there is one) or a reader that knows the bank. There is no extent: this file feeds only the symbol store.

docs.title: 6. Identity
docs.text: None.

docs.title: 7. What is skipped
docs.text: Lines with no :, an address field that is not entirely hex digits or whose value does not fit 16 bits, an empty label, and a label that is empty once its leading . is dropped.

docs.title: 8. Excerpt
docs.text:
Synthetic. There is no committed Memory.txt produced by zxbc, and no Boriel install on the development machine to make one. The format above is read from the producer's code, and the tests use hand-written files in that format:

write_text() at test/debug/source_debug_test.cpp:486, beside a game.nex:

and printf at test/00regression/scripts/nextbuild-symbols-func.sh:24, which writes the file for the functional row:

docs.title: 7.4.6 The annotations project file (.jdp) and the user's labels
docs.text: The user's own labels and comments are the one input of chapter 7 that no toolchain writes. JNEXT defines the file itself: plain UTF-8 text, extension .jdp, opened and saved by the user and never attached beside a program. It fills a third store, UserAnnotations, which sits beside the toolchain's SymbolTable and wins over it when the two disagree.

docs.title: 1. The producer
docs.text: JNEXT. The Qt Map menu opens and saves it (section 10); --annotations FILE loads one at start-up (main.cpp stores annotations_file at src/main.cpp:881 and copies it to the configuration at src/main.cpp:2194, and ScriptHost::start() loads it (annotations_file, src/script/script_host.cpp:201-215), after --map and before the scripts, so a script's @name of the file resolves). replace_annotations() is the primitive an import builds on.

docs.title: 2. The producer's writer
docs.text:
write_annotations(), src/debug/annotations_file.cpp:69-77: the header line jnext-annotations 1, then, for each entry in UserAnnotations::entries() order, the label record and then the comment record. A memory is space_tag() (src/debug/long_address.h, 7.1); an address is $ and four upper-case hex digits (hex4()); a comment is escaped by escape() (src/debug/annotations_file.cpp:22-30): \ becomes \\ and a line feed \n. LF is the only line end written, and no # line, so a Save does not keep a user's own # lines.

The order is the key's: AnnotationKey::operator< (AnnotationKey, src/debug/user_annotations.h:33-37) compares the memory kind (the MemSpace::Kind enumerator order: Page, Rom, BootRom, ... DivMmcRam...), then the index, then the address, so the file diffs well in a repository.

docs.title: 3. The grammar
docs.text:
jnext-annotations 1
label   <SPACE> $<ADDR> <NAME>
comment <SPACE> $<ADDR> <TEXT>

One space between fields. <NAME> is one token (below), <TEXT> is the rest of the line and is never empty. At most one label and one comment per key, and a name at one key only.

docs.title: 4. The parser's rules
docs.text:
read_annotations(), src/debug/annotations_file.cpp:79, validates the whole file into a scratch store and assigns out only when it is all good; every error is line N: reason.

  1. Skipped: a UTF-8 BOM at byte 0 of line 1 only (the "\xEF\xBB\xBF" compare, src/debug/annotations_file.cpp:90), a trailing CR (CRLF), a line whose first character is #, a blank line.
  2. The header is the first other line and must be exactly jnext-annotations 1 (kHeader, src/debug/annotations_file.cpp:94); jnext-annotations N for another canonical N reads version N: this jnext reads version 1 (the "version " message, :100); anything else is not a jnext annotations file.
  3. A record with an unknown kind is refused (the "unknown record '" message, src/debug/annotations_file.cpp:117; forward compatibility is a version bump, not skipping). <SPACE> goes through parse_space_tag() (case-insensitive, strict digits, the hardware's ranges) or the file is refused ("unknown memory '", :122); CPU is refused ("memory CPU:", :124), since a user entry names a memory. <ADDR> is $ and exactly four hex digits, either case (parse_addr(), :46; "bad address '", :127). A label has exactly four fields ("a label record has exactly", :130). A second label or comment for a key is refused ("a second label", :132; "a second comment", :141), a CR inside a text is refused ("a carriage return", :143), and unescape() (:33) accepts only \\ and \n (a final lone \ is refused, "lone backslash", :37).
  4. Names and text are checked by the store, not the adapter, so the API and the file cannot disagree: UserAnnotations::valid_label_name() (src/debug/user_annotations.cpp:29: components [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]* joined by single dots, exactly what the DSL's @name lexes, lex_symbol(), src/script/lexer.cpp:243-261), valid_utf8() (src/debug/user_annotations.cpp:39: no overlong form, no surrogate, nothing past U+10FFFF) and the uniqueness of a name (set_label(), src/debug/user_annotations.cpp:62-80).
  5. A key the file can name. nameable() (src/debug/user_annotations.cpp:15) refuses any memory with parse_space_tag(space_tag(s)) != s (page 0xE0, ROM 4, DivMMC bank 16 ...), so Save never writes a file that Load then refuses whole. The rule is the parser's own; there is no second range table. set_comment() (:92) applies the same checks, turns CRLF and a lone CR into LF and treats empty text as "remove".

docs.title: 5. Space and extent
docs.text: Every entry is keyed by a MemSpace and a 16-bit logical address, the key of the page-aware symbol table (7.4, "The symbol table the formats fill"). It is always paged: the user's entry is shown only while that memory supplies the address, exactly as a paged SLD label is (7.1). An entry whose address its memory can never supply (ROM0 $5000) is legal and never shows. There is no extent: a label names one address.

docs.title: 6. Identity
docs.text: None. The file is not tied to a program, which is why it is never attached automatically.

docs.title: 7. What is skipped
docs.text: The BOM, CR, # lines and blank lines above. Nothing else: an unknown record, tag, version or escape refuses the file.

docs.title: 8. Excerpt
docs.text:
From the writer's row JDP-01 (test/debug/source_map_test.cpp:1344-1350), the bytes of a store inserted in a shuffled order:

jnext-annotations 1
label P04 $8000 Start
comment P04 $8000 Entry\npoint \\ here
label ROM0 $0010 rst_print
comment DIVRAM3 $2000 x

The functional row writes the same shape with printf (test/00regression/scripts/annotations-func.sh:25-27).

docs.title: 9. How the store reaches a reader
docs.text:
Impl keeps three tables (src/debug/debugger_impl.h): toolchain_symbols, the loaded layer (7.3); annotations, the user's store; and names, their composition. recompose_names() (src/debug/debugger_annotations.cpp:30-36) adds the user labels first and then merge()s the toolchain table, so by address and by name the user wins, and the C-name rule of 7.4.3 holds inside the one table. symbols(), lookup() and lookup_name() return names, so every consumer reads both layers with no code of its own. names is assigned in place, so the const SymbolTable* the Disassembly, Call Stack and Breakpoints panels hold (set_symbol_table(&dbg_.symbols())) stays valid.

recompose_names() is called after every change of either layer: the toolchain writers (recompose_names at src/debug/debugger.cpp:270 in load_map and :284 in clear_symbols; in src/debug/debugger_source.cpp at :409 the deferred-check drop, :547 and :554 the hand SLD's labels, :797 the program-load attach and its bind, :961 drop_sidecars, :1064 and :1070 the ring landing) and every verb that changes a label (recompose_names at src/debug/debugger_annotations.cpp:71 in set_user_label, :80 in remove_user_label, :116 in replace_annotations; set_user_comment() changes no name and does not). The attachment cache copies toolchain_symbols, never names (src/debug/debugger_source.cpp:912), so a ring landing cannot bring back a user label that was removed, nor drop one that was added.

The name rule against the toolchain layer is in set_user_label() (the toolchain_symbols.find_name() test, src/debug/debugger_annotations.cpp:53-61): a name the loaded symbols give another address, or another paged memory, is refused; the same address (pinning an unpaged name to its page) is allowed. A project file is not refused for it, and a toolchain loaded later is not either: the user layer then wins by name.

save_annotations() (src/debug/debugger_annotations.cpp:141-162) writes PATH.part and renames it over PATH; load_annotations() (src/debug/debugger_annotations.cpp:121) checks source_file_problem() first (not a regular file, over 64 MiB). The verbs touch no machine state, so they are allowed while the machine runs, take no load generation and leave .jns, the rewind ring and the attachment cache alone; each success bumps state_revision() (3.9.1). A verb that changes nothing (a rename to the same name, an identical or already-normalised comment, clearing a comment that is not there, replacing or loading the same store) bumps neither revision: the early return Result::Ok of set_user_label() (Ok, src/debug/debugger_annotations.cpp:69), of set_user_comment() (Ok, :96) and of replace_annotations() (Ok, :113), pinned by SRCDBG-UANN-21, so an unchanged dialog never raises the unsaved-changes question.

docs.title: 10. The Qt debugger
docs.text:
The same two views edit the store and draw it; nothing here changes what the store holds.

  • One menu builder. add_annotation_actions() (src/debugger/annotation_menu.cpp:77) appends, behind a separator, Add Label… / Rename Label…, Remove Label and Add Comment… / Edit Comment… to a code view's context menu. The Disassembly calls it with the one place of the line, its address and the entry.space it was drawn with (in DisasmPanel::contextMenuEvent(), add_annotation_actions is called at src/debugger/disasm_panel.cpp:986); the Source tab calls it with the line's st.starts (in SourcePanel::fill_context_menu(), add_annotation_actions is called at src/debugger/source_panel.cpp:1369), so a line that compiled to several places gets a submenu per entry, a place not mapped now stays editable (the key does not depend on the mapping), and a line with no code has the entries disabled with the tab's no code at tooltip. Both views therefore offer the same words in the same order (QANN-11).
  • What the entries do. edit_label() (annotation_menu.cpp:35) is a QInputDialog::getText that calls Debugger::set_user_label(); edit_comment() (:53) is a QInputDialog::getMultiLineText that calls set_user_comment() (empty text removes); remove_label() (:70) calls remove_user_label(). A refused name or text is a QMessageBox::warning with the backend's reason and changes nothing (QANN-09). Rename on a toolchain label creates a user label that shadows it; Remove acts on user labels only, so on a toolchain-only label it is disabled and its tooltip names the file the toolchain layer was loaded from (toolchain_symbols().loaded_file() in add_annotation_actions(), toolchain_note, annotation_menu.cpp:95-98; state_of(), :24, only says whether a label is there). The panels hold a const Debugger* for reading; the writes go through the non-const pointer DebuggerManager hands them with set_annotation_backend() (src/debugger/debugger_manager.cpp:392 and :396), and each panel's annotations_changed() signal makes the manager refresh the panels.
  • The Disassembly draws it. label_column_shown() (disasm_panel.cpp:1016) is true while the symbol table (the composed reader, section 9) holds any label; then the Label column sits between the BP column and the mnemonic and every x after it moves by label_width() (16 characters). The columns run Mem, Addr, BP column, [Label], mnemonic, opcode bytes, ; comment; breakpoint_x() (:1023) is the BP column's left edge, mnemonic_x() (:1025) the mnemonic's (breakpoint_x() + 20 + 4, plus label_width() with a label), mnemonic_width() (:1030) the mnemonic column's 20 characters, and bytes_x(line) (:1035) where that line's bytes start: after the column, or after the mnemonic itself plus a gap when that mnemonic is wider, so a long line pushes only its own bytes. The comment sits 100 px (BYTES_WIDTH) after the bytes. The painter and the tests read these accessors (QDCOL-01, QDCOL-03, QDCOL-04; with no label the mnemonic is at 172, QANN-01). line_label() (:1056) is the name the reader gives the line's own address in its own memory, shortened with ...; line_comment() (:1066) is ; and the comment's first line, plus ... when it has more. Both are what the painter draws and what the tests read. The copy formats do not include them (QANN-04). The Source tab does not draw comments (it shows the user's own file).
  • The Map menu. DebuggerWindow adds Open Annotations…, Save Annotations and Save Annotations As… (connect, src/debugger/debugger_window.cpp:899-903), connected to DebuggerManager::on_open_annotations() (debugger_manager.cpp:784), on_save_annotations() (:760) and on_save_annotations_as() (:750); Save with no current file is Save As, which appends .jdp to a name without a suffix. Failures are warnings with the backend's why (an Open names the line).
  • Unsaved changes (D11). DebuggerManager keeps saved_revision_ (debugger_manager.h), the backend's annotations_revision() at the last Open, Save or --annotations; annotations_unsaved() compares them. confirm_discard_annotations() (debugger_manager.cpp:766) asks Save / Discard / Cancel when they differ, and is asked by on_open_annotations() before it opens and by MainWindow::closeEvent() (confirm_discard_annotations, src/gui/main_window.cpp:3880) before anything else, which ignores the event on Cancel or a failed Save (File ▸ Quit goes through close(), which then returns false). An unattended close (unattended_, the delayed automatic exit and SIGINT/SIGTERM, tested at src/gui/main_window.cpp:3877) asks nothing: it logs that the unsaved changes were discarded and quits (QG-ANN-05). With nothing changed there is no dialog. set_annotations_file() (debugger_manager.cpp:731), called by QtApp for --annotations (set_annotations_file, src/gui/qt_app.cpp:395), makes that file the Save target and the starting point of "unsaved".
  • Settings. None: the store has no Preferences field, so config_keys.cpp has no row; the CLI is --annotations FILE.

docs.title: 11. The rows that pin it
docs.text:
• source_map_test: UANN-01 to UANN-13 (the store: keys, grammar, name rule, comment text, order, unnameable memories) and JDP-01 to JDP-09 (the file's bytes, the leniencies, every refusal with its line, atomicity, the round trip).
  • source_debug_test: SRCDBG-UANN-01 to -21 (the two layers and the one reader by page, the name rule, the file through the backend, no lifetime across sidecars, hand loads, resets, state loads and ring landings, purity with its control, the state revision).
  • gdb_rsp_test GDB-ANN-01, script_events_test SCRIPT-ANN-01, cli_options_test CLI-ANN-01, debugger_verbs_test QMAP-10 (the four Load MAP boxes count the loaded file only), and the functional row annotations-func (headless, Qt and SDL).
  • The Qt side: debugger_panels_test QANN-01 to -04 and -06 (the column, the comment, the copies, the address field), debugger_verbs_test QANN-05 (Call Stack and Breakpoints), QANN-12 and -13 (the Map menu, the unsaved question), debugger_source_panel_test QANN-07 to -11 (the menus, per place, the dialogs, a refused name, parity), debugger_quit_gate_test QG-ANN-01/-02 and quit_cleanup_test QG-ANN-03 (the quit question) (SRCDBG-UANN-21: a no-op verb bumps nothing, in the backend list above).

docs.title: 7.4.7 The skoolkit and Ghidra exports and imports
docs.text: The other pages of 7.4 are inputs. This one is the reverse direction: Debugger::export_skoolkit() and export_ghidra() write what the disassembly shows, and for skoolkit the code/data map that --coverage recorded, into a directory, as the files the two reverse-engineering tools read; import_skoolkit() and import_ghidra() (stage B) read such files back into the user's labels and comments (7.4.6). The decisions are in section 11.2 of doc/design/SOURCE-LEVEL-DEBUGGING.md; this page is the code and the formats.

docs.title: 1. The consumers
docs.text:
• SkoolKit 10.1, sna2skool.py and the control-file parser. A comment line starts with #, % or ; and anything else must be a directive (skoolkit/ctlparser.py:254-255), so the first line of every file, # jnext space <TAG>, is inert. A bad line is only a warning (skoolkit/ctlparser.py:119, "Ignoring line"). An address is decimal, $hex or %bin, never 0x (get_int_param(), skoolkit/__init__.py:88-98). With no -c, sna2skool.py reads every <input-stem>*.ctl (skoolkit/sna2skool.py:34); a -c that names a directory reads sorted(glob(DIR/*.ctl)) (skoolkit/sna2skool.py:39-40), so the file names must sort in address order. skoolkit is Z80-only and drops, with no warning, a label that is not at the start of a line it writes.
  • Ghidra 12.2, Ghidra/Extensions/Jython/ghidra_scripts/ImportSymbolsScript.py (the Jython extension; the release bundles it, since 12.1 it is not installed by default). askFile() (ImportSymbolsScript.py:35; headless: the file is the script's argument), line.split() (ImportSymbolsScript.py:38), toAddr() (ImportSymbolsScript.py:41), createFunction() (ImportSymbolsScript.py:57) for f and createLabel() (ImportSymbolsScript.py:62) for anything else. A line whose address space the program lacks makes toAddr() return nothing and the script dies on it, losing every later line while analyzeHeadless still exits 0. Both tools are test-time only and provisioned by make skoolkit and make ghidra (section 6).

docs.title: 2. The writers
docs.text:
Both are pure (std, mem_space.h, long_address.h, disasm.h); their inputs and outputs are the plain structs of src/debug/reexport.h.

  • The classifier, classify() (skoolkit_ctl.cpp:34). Over a space's whole store: an X byte starts an instruction whose extent is instruction_length(), clipped at the store end and at the next X start; a byte is code inside an extent, else data (R or W), else unknown. A store with no mark is one code run.
  • The files, build() (skoolkit_ctl.cpp:196): one <WWWW>-<TAG>.ctl and .bin per window of each space, named by file_name() (skoolkit_ctl.cpp:87), and 0000-0CPU.ctl for the unpaged labels. The windows are those holding the space's keys; with none, the one that maps the space now (Input::mapped_window), else home_window() (skoolkit_ctl.cpp:19). The text of a window is written by render_window() (skoolkit_ctl.cpp:142): the header, @ start / @ org, the block directives (block_letter() (skoolkit_ctl.cpp:137)), the labels, the B/C sub-blocks and the closing i. A Z80N instruction or a clipped one is a B sub-block, and so is each piece of an instruction a key falls in.
  • One name, one key. z88dk's module-local labels repeat across routines (end_x at $80CA and $8103 in asm_zx_cls_wc_attr / asm_zx_cls_wc_pix); skool2asm.py refuses a label defined twice, and both importers (and UserAnnotations, one key per name) refuse a name at two keys. So unique_names() (reexport.cpp) runs first in build() of each writer: of the exportable labels sharing a name at different (memory, address) keys it keeps the first by (unpaged, memory kind and index, address) and notes each other (label 'N' at P04:$8103 skipped: the name is already used at P04:$80CA (one name, one address)). The rule is global across one export, since an import reads several files into one store; the Ghidra view.ghidra.txt is its own import, so it is made unique among its own lines. The alternatives were rejected: qualifying a name with its module (the label would come back under a name nobody typed, and the module is not in the label) and refusing the export (the common z88dk newlib program would export nothing). Rows SKCTL-18, GHSYM-07; the foreign readers run it on skool2asm.py, skool2ctl.py and the importers (skoolkit-foreign-func A5, ghidra-foreign-func).
  • Window sizes and homes. window_size() (skoolkit_ctl.cpp:17) is the size of the space's store: 8 KB, or 16 KB for Rom, AltRom and Config. A space with neither keys nor a current mapping goes to home_window() (skoolkit_ctl.cpp:19): the 128K bank positions for a RAM page ($4000/$6000 for pages 0x0A/0x0B, $8000/$A000 for 0x04/0x05, $C000 plus (n & 1) * $2000 for any other), $0000 for ROM, $2000 for a DivMMC bank. The home exists because coverage is keyed by (memory, offset) and records no logical address: nothing says where a page was mapped when it ran.
  • Where the identity lives. A control file describes one 64 KB view and skoolkit's only bank notion is the @bank directive, which names neither the Next's 224 8 KB pages nor ROM and the overlays. So the identity is the file name and the first line, written as the string "# jnext space " (skoolkit_ctl.cpp:186) (a control-file comment skoolkit ignores). The same prefix is how a later export recognises its own files: kCtlHeader (debugger_reinterop.cpp:33).
  • File order. out.files (skoolkit_ctl.cpp:288) puts the unpaged file first; it is named 0000-0CPU.ctl, not 0000-CPU.ctl, because the 0 sorts before the letter every 0000-<TAG> starts with (0000-ALTROM0, 0000-BOOT and 0000-CFG00 would otherwise sort ahead of it). All files are then ordered by name with stable_sort() (skoolkit_ctl.cpp:290), which is address order. Two files that disagree at a shared boundary address are applied in command-line order, and sna2skool.py -c DIR reads sorted(glob(DIR/*.ctl)), so a paged label wins over an unpaged one at the same address, as in the disassembly.
  • The .bin. build() writes it beside each control file with the out.files push (out.files at skoolkit_ctl.cpp:266; file_name() only names it), from the bytes the export read with peek() (debugger_reinterop.cpp:200) now. skoolkit reads no NEX, so a Next page's control file is useless without them, and sna2skool.py -o 0xWWWW WWWW-TAG.bin finds exactly that .ctl by default pickup, which happens only when no -c is given.
  • No map for what cannot be read. The identity-only memories (boot ROM, Multiface, DivMMC ROM, alternate ROM, Layer 2, config, floating) are refused by peek(), so they have no instruction lengths and get no code/data map; the report says so with the note space_tag() (debugger_reinterop.cpp:208) (SRCDBG-REX-07). With coverage off the report says that too, behind mem_coverage_enabled() (debugger_reinterop.cpp:184).
  • Unpaged labels are also label-less keys of every window written that covers their address, added by the loop over by_window (skoolkit_ctl.cpp:253), so the same splits keep them from being dropped by sna2skool (SKCTL-08d).
  • Ghidra, build() (ghidra_symbols.cpp:39): one file per space; the <TAG>: prefix is set in prefix_of (ghidra_symbols.cpp:55); CPU.ghidra.txt and view.ghidra.txt (the labels the disassembly shows now).
  • The line formats. render() (ghidra_symbols.cpp:29) writes NAME <TAG>:0xHHHH l for a space's file and NAME 0xHHHH l for CPU.ghidra.txt and view.ghidra.txt, sorted by address then name (the line is built by the format string " l\n" (ghidra_symbols.cpp:33)), with no header, comment or blank line, and only when the file has a line, as render() (ghidra_symbols.cpp:68) shows. view.ghidra.txt exists because on a 48K or 128K machine every RAM label is paged, so the per-space files alone would need one overlay per page to import a 48K program into flat memory.
  • The Z80N table, kZ80nEd (disasm.cpp:362), is read by z80n_ed_length() (disasm.cpp:371), by instruction_length() and by is_z80n_extension() (disasm.cpp:813).

docs.title: 3. The verbs and the directory
docs.text:
All in debugger_reinterop.cpp. gather_labels() (debugger_reinterop.cpp:75) takes one entry per key of symbols() named by lookup(). Debugger::export_skoolkit (debugger_reinterop.cpp:176) adds the stores (peek() and mem_coverage(), a note for coverage it cannot read) and Debugger::export_ghidra (debugger_reinterop.cpp:225) the view.

write_directory() (debugger_reinterop.cpp:93) checks every file in the way before writing (Unsupported), writes <name>.part (part (debugger_reinterop.cpp:127)) and renames it with fs::rename (debugger_reinterop.cpp:137). Then it removes a previous export's files that this one did not write: a *.ctl whose first line is # jnext space (has_jnext_header() (debugger_reinterop.cpp:151)) and the .bin of its WWWW-TAG stem (is_ctl_stem() (debugger_reinterop.cpp:59), applied at is_ctl_stem() (debugger_reinterop.cpp:158)), or the Ghidra names (is_ghidra_export_name() (debugger_reinterop.cpp:49)). Anything else in the directory is never touched. A path that is a regular file (refuse() (debugger_reinterop.cpp:98)) or a directory that cannot be created (refuse() (debugger_reinterop.cpp:100)) is RefusedUnavailable; a .ctl or .bin in the way that is not jnext's is Unsupported and nothing is written (refuse() (debugger_reinterop.cpp:113)).

Names are exported as lookup() shows them (lookup() (debugger_reinterop.cpp:84)), so a z88dk C symbol goes out under its C name. The verbs are reads: they call only peek(), mem_coverage(), mem_coverage_enabled(), mem_coverage_spaces(), symbols(), lookup() and source_page(), so no machine state changes and no generation moves (SRCDBG-REX-03, with REX-04 as its control).

docs.title: Import
docs.text:
Debugger::import_skoolkit (debugger_reinterop.cpp:254) and Debugger::import_ghidra (debugger_reinterop.cpp:300) read ALL their files into a scratch copy of annotations() and apply it with one replace_annotations(), so a refusal anywhere changes nothing and a success is one revision bump (SRCDBG-REX-12, -13). The readers are pure, in the writers' files:

  • skoolkit, parse_ctl() (skoolkit_ctl.cpp:475). It mirrors the grammar of _parse_ctl_line() (skoolkit/ctlparser.py:208) but is strict where skoolkit only warns (skoolkit/ctlparser.py:119, "Ignoring line"). The parameters go through parse_params() (skoolkit_ctl.cpp:447), a port of skoolkit's own parse_params() (skoolkit/ctlparser.py:39): base letters, : sublengths, *N repeats, characters like "A", and the L loop rules; the numbers are read by get_int_param() (skoolkit_ctl.cpp:349), skoolkit's own get_int_param() (skoolkit/__init__.py:88) without its 0x form, in py_int() (skoolkit_ctl.cpp:318) which also refuses a value past 2^40, far beyond any address or length. A line skoolkit would drop (a bad integer, extra parameters on a lowercase block, L without a length or count, an unknown directive, a blank directive before any block, a bad @ignoreua suffix) refuses the file with line N: reason, as do an address outside 0..65535 (and, in a length, a number past 2^40), a label name outside UserAnnotations::valid_label_name(), one name at two addresses and text that is not UTF-8 (SKCTL-12, SKCTL-15, SKCTL-17; measured against sna2skool 10.1). It takes @ ADDR label=NAME (a leading * dropped; two labels at one address keep the last, as skoolkit applies it) and the text of a B C S T W or blank-lead sub-block with its . / : continuation lines, joined with line feeds, as the comment at that address. An @ line leaves a comment open, as in skoolkit (SKCTL-16). Block titles (a lowercase directive with text, or the first . line after one without), D descriptions and the other directives are counted in Imported (reexport.h:71) and not imported; no store holds a code/data map.
  • Ghidra, parse_symbols() (ghidra_symbols.cpp:85), the script's grammar (line.split(), ImportSymbolsScript.py:38; toAddr(), ImportSymbolsScript.py:41): whitespace split, name, address, then anything; blank lines skipped. The address is 0xHHHH or TAG:0xHHHH (CPU: is untagged); a prefix that is no jnext memory tag (ram:0x8000), an expression, a # line and a bad name refuse; two labels at one address keep the first (Ghidra's primary is the first created).
  • Which memory. A control file's memory is its # jnext space TAG line (only before the first directive), else its name (TAG.ctl, WWWW-TAG.ctl), else none; none and CPU are untagged, and each untagged entry takes source_page(addr) when the file is read through source_page (debugger_reinterop.cpp:276), the identity the disassembly looks labels up with. A command-line import runs in ScriptHost::start (script_host.cpp:171), in import_all() (script_host.cpp:218), after --annotations and before --load, so an untagged file is placed by the mapping at start.
  • Export carries comments. export_skoolkit() passes annotations().entries() with a comment as Input::comments from the loop over annotations (debugger_reinterop.cpp:180), and symbols() is the composed table, so a user label already shadows the toolchain's in both exports (SRCDBG-REX-14).

docs.title: Qt: Map ▸ Import and Export
docs.text:
The Qt debugger offers the four verbs in its Map menu, after the annotation entries of 7.4.6: import_menu (debugger_window.cpp:919) and export_menu (debugger_window.cpp:924), each with &skoolkit Control Files... and &Ghidra Symbols... (I and E are free in the Map popup, S and G are unique in each submenu; DACC-05 pins the new popups and mnemonics). The slots are on_import_skoolkit (debugger_manager.cpp:858), on_import_ghidra (debugger_manager.cpp:859), on_export_skoolkit (debugger_manager.cpp:860) and on_export_ghidra (debugger_manager.cpp:861), which share import_re_files (debugger_manager.cpp:818) and export_re_files (debugger_manager.cpp:841):

  • Import asks for one or more files with QFileDialog::getOpenFileNames (*.ctl or *.txt), calls the backend verb once with all of them, and shows the report (counts, then each note) in an Import Done box, or an Import Failed warning with the verb's why (the file and the line) and nothing changed. A success refreshes the panels, so the Disassembly's Label column shows the new names at once; the verb's one revision bump is what makes the quit question of 7.4.6 ask about unsaved annotations.
  • Export asks for a directory with QFileDialog::getExistingDirectory, calls the verb and shows the report in an Export Done box, or an Export Failed warning with why.
  • Tests: QREX-01..04 in debugger_verbs_test drive the real file dialogs through Modals (a quoted file list or a directory typed into the dialog's name field) and compare the exported files with what the verb writes.

docs.title: 4. The frontends
docs.text: write_re_exports_at_exit() (re_export_at_exit.h:39) is called from the three loop owners' shutdown(): write_re_exports_at_exit() (headless_app.cpp:1075), write_re_exports_at_exit() (sdl_app.cpp:822) and write_re_exports_at_exit() (qt_app.cpp:533). A failure logs and sets the exit code to 1. --export-skoolkit, --export-ghidra, --import-skoolkit and --import-ghidra are in src/core/cli_options.h.

docs.title: 5. A real excerpt
docs.text:
The F1 fixture of reexport_test (SKCTL-03) writes C000-P10.ctl as below; skoolkit 10.1 reads it with no warning and skool2asm.py emits banked:, table: and smc:.

# jnext space P10
@ $C000 start
@ $C000 org
c $C000
@ $C000 label=banked
b $C003
@ $C003 label=table
B $C003
. two
. lines
u $C004
c $C010
B $C010,1 Load the first byte
@ $C011 label=smc
B $C011,2
b $C014
u $C015
c $C020
B $C020,4
u $C025
i $E000

docs.title: 6. Tests and the foreign readers
docs.text: reexport_test (SKCTL, GHSYM and SRCDBG-REX rows) proves the formats and the verbs; cli_options_test CLI-REX-01 the options. The writers are proved by the tools themselves, never by a reader of ours: skoolkit-foreign-func runs sna2skool.py and skool2asm.py (a 48K snapshot with -c DIR, a Next page by default pickup, the Qt and SDL owners, a failing export) and ghidra-foreign-func runs analyzeHeadless with ImportSymbolsScript.py (and pins the abort above as its control). make skoolkit (test/provision-skoolkit.sh, SkoolKit 10.1's PyPI sdist, 1.3 MB) and make ghidra (test/provision-ghidra.sh, Ghidra 12.2 with its Jython extension, 570 MB download, 954 MB on disk, a JDK 25 to run it: java-25-openjdk-devel is in the CI dnf list) are sha256-pinned, verified before unpacking, and prerequisites of regression, regression-rows and regression-confirm; the rows are os=linux. HS-100 and HS-101 prove a wrong checksum is refused.

docs.title: 7.4 File formats and records
docs.text:
Six inputs feed the stores. Each gets a page, laid out the same way so that a reader can compare formats and a maintainer adding one (7.8) knows what to write.

Page Input Produced by Fills 7.4.1 sjasmplus SLD --sld file, version 1 sjasmplus source map, labels, identity (by convention) 7.4.2 sjasmplus --sym / --exp NAME: EQU 0x0000ABCD lines sjasmplus labels 7.4.3 The z88dk map <stem>.map, with -debug line records z88dk (z80asm) labels and source map, identity from section binaries 7.4.4 z88dk listings <file>.lis z88dk (z80asm --list) source map (replaces a module's map records), embedded texts 7.4.5 NextBuild Memory.txt 8000: ._Main lines Boriel ZX Basic zxbc -M, via NextBuild labels 7.4.6 The annotations file .jdp: label and comment records the user, in JNEXT the user's labels and comments (a third store)

The reverse direction, the skoolkit control files and Ghidra symbol files jnext writes, is 7.4.7.

Boriel ZX Basic writes no SLD. Its only output jnext reads is Memory.txt (7.4.5), a list of labels with no source positions, so a BASIC program built with NextBuild has symbols and no source lines unless an SLD is produced by some other tool.

docs.title: The symbol table the formats fill
docs.text:
There is one SymbolTable (src/debug/symbol_table.*), owned by the backend. The Qt panels, the DSL's @name, the GDB server's monitor sym and --map all read it, so a symbol loaded by one client shows in every other. How the formats differ is only in what they put in it.

  • Keyed by memory and address. add_label(name, addr, space, bind_at_load, c_symbol) stores a label that is paged (assembled for one FetchSource such as Page{20}, naming the address only while that memory supplies it) or unpaged (naming it in every memory: the sjasmplus EQU, Simple and NextBuild loaders make these). There is no address-only lookup: lookup(space, addr) finds the paged label with exactly that key, else the unpaged one at addr (MemSpace::cpu() is "no memory known" and reaches unpaged labels only). The backend's lookup(addr) asks with source_page(addr), the same identity the source map and the gutter use (7.1), so every consumer (the Disassembly, the Call Stack, the Breakpoints, monitor sym ADDR) names an address by what is mapped there now; disasm_text::symbol_namer() is that rule as a function for the panels. The first label of a key wins and, apart, the first of a name.
  • A name resolves to an address and, through find_name() and resolve_key(), to the memory it was assembled for; the breakpoint dialogs keep that page. SymbolTable::resolve() turns an address field's text into an address: hex first (4000, $4000, 0x4000), else a symbol; @name always means the symbol, so a program variable named FE is still reachable.
  • Name-only values. add_value() stores a size, an offset or a section bound: find_name() and lookup_name() resolve it, but it never names an address, so a constant is never shown in a disassembly (a z88dk ; const line, an SLD +struct_def record).
  • Binding at load. A z88dk symbol of a section that names no page is stored with bind_at_load and no memory; SymbolTable::bind(space_of) gives it the RAM page space_of(addr) names (ROM, DivMMC and the other overlays leave it unpaged; an empty function unbinds it). The backend binds with the one function the source half uses, emu.predict_fetch: at load_map() (every success), at the sidecar <stem>.map (a tape included, at the attach), and for the user's store at every program load (7.4.3, rule 4).
  • Combining. SymbolTable::merge(other) is the one way to combine two tables: it adds the other's labels whose key is still free, its names and name-only values not yet taken, so the first table wins throughout (row SYMPG-12). The sidecar store is assembled with it (7.3).
  • C names. A z88dk C symbol also has its C name (c_name_to_key_, shown_name(), lookup_assembler(); 7.4.3); merge() carries the C names for the labels the receiving table does not own, and clear() empties them (rows Z88CN-01 to -16).
  • Rows. SYMPG-* and SLDL-* (source_map_test: pages, SLD labels), Z88SYM-01 to -09 and SRCDBG-SYM-18 to -22 (the z88dk placement), SYM-19 to -32 (debugger_backend_test: the EQU and --map loaders).

docs.title: The layout of a format page
docs.text:
1. The producer, its version and the command.
  2. The producer's writer, cited by tree and file:line, so a change in the tool can be checked against it.
  3. The grammar of a record.
  4. The parser's rules, each with the jnext function that applies it.
  5. Space and extent: which memory a record belongs to and how many bytes it covers. These two decide whether a format can be supported at all.
  6. Identity, if the format can carry a program identity.
  7. What is skipped, and why.
  8. A real excerpt from a committed fixture, with its path. The fixtures are normalised (install paths, temporary names and compile dates are replaced: test/fixtures/z88dk/README.md, "Normalisation and trimming"). Where no public producer writes a record and no fixture exists, the excerpt is labelled synthetic and says which test it comes from.
  9. The rows that pin it.

docs.title: Which citations are where
docs.text:
Producer sources are cited as <tree> <path>:<line>:

  • sjasmplus is ~/src/spectrum/sjasmplus at v1.23.1, commit 46aae3f.
  • z88dk 2.4 is ~/src/spectrum/z88dk-original-2.4 at 4d530b6eb7 (v2.4) and z88dk master is ~/src/spectrum/z88dk-original-97731e4e29 at 97731e4e29 (v2.4-2883-g97731e4e29), master before the debug-record fixes of 2026-11-04 and -05, which ~/src/spectrum/z88dk-original-latest (0f0a1cf70e) has. These are the installs the z88dk fixtures were made with (test/fixtures/z88dk/*/PROVENANCE files).
  • Boriel ZX Basic and NextBuild are read on GitHub: boriel-basic/zxbasic at 29f0b2f0ce and em00k/NextBuild at 364b2d13c5, both on 2026-11-01. The URLs are in doc/REFERENCES.md.

docs.title: 7.5 Breakpoints, steps, history and call frames
docs.text:
Everything on this page answers "where in the source" with machinery that already existed for "where in memory": the Execute event, the debugger's Step, the trace, and the call-stack tracker. None of it adds a new way to stop the machine. It adds a way to name where, and a loop that ends on a source boundary. 3.9.4 owns the step modes, the gates and rewind; this page does not restate them.

Left: a file:line breakpoint is a group of Execute subscriptions that share one predicate. Middle: a forward source step is a loop of the debugger's own Step. Right: Back and Reverse Continue pick a trace entry and hand a count to step_back().

docs.title: A line breakpoint is a group of Execute subscriptions
docs.text:
Debugger::subscribe_source_line(by, "file:line", like) (debugger_events.cpp):

  1. like must be an Execute subscription, or the verb is refused; so is a departed client.
  2. source_map().resolve(file_line) (7.2) gives the line's starts. No start refuses the verb (RefusedUnavailable).
  3. A new GroupId is taken, and for each start (space, address) a copy of like is added with filter.lo = filter.hi = address, filter.page = PAGE_ANY and filter.space = space, all in that group.

The qualifier is the canonical one (7.1): the memory the location was compiled for. A line compiled into two places is two subscriptions in one group, each matching only its own memory. The group verbs (unsubscribe_group(), set_group_enabled()) act on all members, and refuse a group the caller does not own with the same answer an unknown one gets. The Qt Breakpoints panel shows a group as one row (Row::group in breakpoint_model.h).

Debugger::run_to_source_line(by, "file:line") (debugger_control.cpp) is Run To for a line: it checks the execute gate and resolves the line before it pauses anything, so a refusal leaves a running machine running; then it builds a transient Stop Execute and calls subscribe_source_line() with it, run_to_subscribed() and arm_target(RunTo, by, starts.front().address, ...), remembering every start in armed_targets. A transient subscription is removed at the next stop that the backend caused (Impl::apply_stop()).

docs.title: One predicate
docs.text:
All of this relies on a single decision about whether an Execute event matches a filter, EventFilter::matches(ev) (event_table.cpp: kind, range, legacy page, then space). It has three callers, and they differ only in where the Event comes from:

Caller The Event Used for EventTable::filter_matches(), from Impl::deliver_to_subscribers() built by Impl::execute_gate(pc): phys_page is the effective page, space is predict_fetch(pc) the live gate, before an instruction runs, and a source step's delivery below Debugger::probe_execute(pc) the same event, built without recording a hit the pure "what is armed here" query history_stop_at() (debugger_source.cpp) built from a TraceEntry: pc, phys_page = te.mmu[te.pc >> 13], space = te.fetch_space() Reverse Continue

The first two use the prediction, the third the record (7.1). history_stop_at() honours only what does not depend on the machine of then: a live (Entry::live: enabled, and on for its client), non-transient, unconditional Stop with no handler, which has not already fired its once. A breakpoint with a condition or a handler cannot be re-evaluated against a machine that is not there.

docs.title: source_step()
docs.text: Debugger::source_step(by, kind) (debugger_source.cpp), with SourceStep = Into, Over, Out, Back, ReverseContinue. It is refused inside a delivery, and with RefusedUnavailable when there is no live source map (recheck() runs first, 7.6).

docs.title: The forward steps
docs.text:
Into, Over and Out are a loop over Emulator::debugger_step(), the debugger's own single Step, so a source step is exactly a run of Steps that stops on a source boundary. First execute_gate() (the same refusals a Step has), then the pause ownership and stop evidence exactly as step_into() sets them.

  • The start. start is a copy of source_location() (a handler may load a map mid-step and invalidate the pointer), and start_depth is call_stack().frames().size(). With no location under the PC, or Out with no tracked frame, the step is one instruction: that is how an unmapped stretch is left.

  • The boundary. reached() re-reads the location and the depth after each Step:

    Kind Reached when Into the position moved (same_position() is false: file, line or column) Over the position moved and depth <= start_depth Out there is a location and depth < start_depth

    Over and Out measure depth with the call-stack tracker, so they need it on (set_call_stack_enabled, a per-client request; with a C variable store and a non-observer client attached it is on by itself, 7.10).

  • The loop, per iteration: debugger_step(), then pause(); stop if an event stop is latched, or the magic or watch stop fired; stop if reached(); stop at a HALT with interrupts disabled (Warn: "Source step stopped at a HALT with interrupts disabled"), because each Step there would spend two frames learning that only an NMI or a reset ends it; stop when the machine clock has advanced by SOURCE_STEP_FRAME_LIMIT frames (100, SOURCE_STEP_FRAME_LIMIT, debugger.h:1464) since the start (Warn); then the delivery below.

  • The limit. After SOURCE_STEP_LIMIT instructions (1,000,000, SOURCE_STEP_LIMIT, debugger.h:1460) the step ends with a Warn.
  • The delivery. debugger_step() delivers no Execute event, because run_frame() does that before each instruction and a Step does not run through it. So between instructions the loop gives the next PC run_frame()'s treatment itself, in its order: DebugState::should_break(pc) (the legacy PC breakpoint), then, when execute_events_armed(), run_execute_gate(pc) under a GuestExecutionScope. Handlers run, and a Stop records its hit and its once. If a handler moved the PC, the new address gets no delivery of its own (as in a run, the redirect target simply runs next) but the loop checks whether it is already the boundary.

A step ends the way a Step does: finish() pauses, and an event's own stop becomes the reason in place of Step.

docs.title: Back and Reverse Continue
docs.text:
These search the retained trace; they do not run the machine. They need the trace on (else the rewind refusal "the instruction trace is off") and they hand the result to step_back(by, n), so they inherit its refusals. Candidates are the entries before the machine's current cycle (a Frame Back or a slider jump leaves newer entries in the trace) and in the machine's current load generation (generation_of_seq(), 7.6): Back never crosses a landing into the history of the machine before it.

For each entry, newest first, at_entry() asks the map with the entry's recorded identity, source_map.lookup(te.fetch_space(), te.pc); an entry whose fetch space is cpu() ("none recorded") has no location. An entry with no location is skipped by both kinds.

  • Back takes the newest earlier entry whose position differs from the current one (same_position(); a loop on one line, or several records for one statement, count as one step), then walks older entries (passing unmapped ones) while they are at that same position, and lands on the oldest: the first instruction of the previous statement, the inverse of Into.
  • ReverseContinue takes the newest mapped entry for which history_stop_at() is true or the legacy store has a PC breakpoint at its address (breakpoints().has_pc()).

step_back(by, size - target) lands on trace[size - n]'s PC. When no entry qualifies the verb refuses with "no earlier mapped source position in the retained trace" or "no earlier source breakpoint in the retained trace".

docs.title: The call stack the steps lean on
docs.text:
CallStack (debug/call_stack.h) is a debug-only shadow of the machine's calls. It is told about each instruction by Emulator::step_one_instruction() (on_instruction_pre() with the opcode and its predicted memory, then on_instruction_post() with the new SP and PC and the recorded fetch) and about an accepted INT or NMI by on_interrupt(). Frames are oldest first, up to MAX_DEPTH = 256. A frame is a CALL, an RST, an INT or an NMI (CallType), with caller_pc, target_pc, sp_at_call and the two memories of 7.1.

What ends a frame. Not just the stack pointer. CallStack::return_to(): a taken RET that lands on the newest frame's own return point ends exactly that frame: for a CALL, caller_pc + 3; for an INT or NMI, caller_pc (or caller_pc + 1 when the interrupt ended a HALT, which the CPU had stepped past). Any other RET, and every RST frame (whose inline DEFW operands make the return point vary), ends frames by the stack pointer: those whose sp_at_call is below the new SP are popped (pop_frames_to_sp()). The reason is that SP alone is wrong for a routine that moves its own return address:

  • sccz80's l_debug_push_frame (every -debug function) re-pushes the return address two bytes lower, so the frame would survive its RET by the SP rule;
  • a __z88dk_callee routine moves it up, so the RET of a call it makes (or of an ISR that interrupted it) would pop its frame.

The price is stated in the code: a routine that drops its return address and leaves by a direct JP nn keeps its frame until a RET ends it by SP. (A routine that leaves by an indirect jump has its frame ended: below.)

A return with no RET. Some sccz80 runtime helpers return by an indirect jump, and some routines jump indirectly without returning. CallStack::indirect_jump_to() (call_stack.cpp:96) judges a JP (HL), JP (IX) or JP (IY) when the newest frame is a CALL frame; the frame ends in two cases:

  • A. The jump lands on the frame's return point (caller_pc + 3), whatever SP is. The l_gintspsp family (l_gcharspsp, l_g2intspsp, l_g2charspsp, l_glong2sp: sccz80's loads of an int/char stack variable) swaps a value into the slot with EX (SP),HL and jumps with SP at the slot or one PUSH below it. l_long_sub, l_long_and, l_long_or, l_long_xor, l_long_eq and l_long_ne (long arithmetic and comparisons) POP IX the return address, pop their arguments and JP (IX) with SP above the slot. Nothing but a return jumps to the return point.
  • B. SP is above the frame's slot and the frame has no live stored copy of its return address. l_case, l_long_case and l_i64_case (switch) POP HL the "return address" as the inline case table, walk it and JP (HL) to a case label (or the default continuation) in the caller: they store nothing back, so they have left.

A stored copy is what tells a routine that has left from one that has only moved its return address up. A __z88dk_callee routine pops its return address and its arguments and pushes the return address back (POP r; POP args; PUSH r, or ...; EX (SP),r), so SP is above its CALL's slot for the whole body, and its internal jumps are not returns. CallStack::note_stack_store_() (call_stack.cpp:59) records, in CallFrame::ret_stored_at, the address where a PUSH qq, PUSH IX, PUSH IY, Z80N PUSH nn or EX (SP),HL/IX/IY put caller_pc + 3 above the slot of the newest CALL frame; the latest store wins. The copy is live (CallStack::ret_copy_live_(), call_stack.cpp:69) while it sits at or above SP and still holds that value. The words are read through a stack reader that Emulator::Emulator() (emulator.cpp:43) installs over Mmu::peek() (mmu.h:367), which has no watchpoint or latch side effect. Without a reader (the bare tracker rows) nothing is recorded and clause B is "SP above the slot".

Then pop_frames_to_sp() ends the older frames whose slot is below SP. Only the newest frame is judged and recorded, so recursion (every deeper call is a newer frame at a lower SP) and an interrupt routine (its INT frame is the newest) cannot end an outer frame. Kept, on purpose:

  • bit_beep_raw_callee (POP AF; POP HL; POP DE; PUSH AF; JP asm_bit_beep_raw, which loops by JP (IX) with SP four bytes above the slot) and any hand-written __z88dk_callee routine: the copy is live.
  • The classic retrofit callee shims (_clga_callee, _draw_callee, ...: LD HL,retaddr; EX (SP),HL; LD (save),HL; JP (HL)): SP is AT the slot, which clause B never ends.
  • banked_call: it POPs its return address but enters the target with CALL l_jphl; the JP (HL) is in l_jphl's own frame, at its slot, to a function (rows SRCDBG-CS-21, SRCSTEP-01 to -03, -08).

The residuals, stated plainly. A routine that moves its return address above its slot by anything but PUSH/EX (SP) (LD (IX+n),r, LDIR) or holds it in a register, then jumps internally with SP above the slot, loses its frame early. A routine that drops its return address with SP left at or below its slot and jumps elsewhere keeps a stale frame until a RET ends it by SP (rex's saveRegAlloc; no z80 target), and so does one that pushes a value equal to caller_pc + 3 that is not its return address. None of these occurs in either install's z80 libraries.

The survey: every JP (HL), JP (IX) and JP (IY) in both installs' libsrc (491 lines, 242 distinct code windows; EX (SP) and POP r families included). G1, return by jump: clause A (l_gintspsp family, l_long_*, l_i64_*, l_command_line_parse, the math48 and mbf helpers, asm_im2_push_registers, the sdcc 64-bit callees and others). G2, return slot consumed with a jump into the caller: clause B (l_case, l_long_case, l_i64_case). G3, trampolines reached by CALL (l_jphl, l_jpix, l_dcal): SP at their own slot, kept. G4, call emulation (push a return label, jump to a function: FZX, cpm, call_extrom): SP below the slot, kept. G5, tail jumps to a function or state: kept, including after a callee prologue (the copy is live). G6, jumps within a routine's own body (asm_bit_beep_raw, beeper, SP1): kept, including with SP above the slot after a callee prologue. G7, other CPUs (Rabbit, GBZ80, 8080/8085): not applicable. Rows SRCDBG-CS-16 to -27, SRCSTEP-14 to -48 on the intarg, longsw and calleejp z88dk fixtures and the sjasmcallee SLD fixture (test/fixtures/z88dk/*/*-intarg, *-longsw, *-calleejp; test/fixtures/sjasmcallee), QCSP-04 to -06 for the panel. There is no 80cc calleejp build: master's -compiler=80cc does not honour __z88dk_callee on an extern declaration.

CallStack::on_slot_without_fetch() handles the esxDOS shim, which returns from the RST $08 it serviced: that frame ends, and only that one.

These rules are why Out and Over cross banked_call and l_debug_push_frame correctly, which v2.4/sccz80-banked-run and master/sdcc-banked-run (test/fixtures/z88dk/README.md, finding Z3) exist to prove on a running program.

docs.title: Where it is tested
docs.text:
• source_debug_test: SRCBP-* (line breakpoints and groups), SRCRUN-* (run to line), SRCSTEP-* and SRCDBG-STEP-* (the forward steps), SRCDBG-BACK-*, SRCDBG-HIST-* and SRCDBG-GATE-* (Back, Reverse Continue and the generation filter), SRCDBG-CS-* (the call stack's frame identities; SRCDBG-CS-08 to -15 pin the frame-ending rule above: the esxDOS shim, a RET used as a jump, __z88dk_callee, RETI/RETN, an RST frame, an INT that ended a HALT; SRCDBG-CS-16 to -27 pin the jump rule).
  • step_out_test (the Step Out RET predicate, check_step_out()) and rewind_call_stack_test (the tracker restored across a rewind).
  • script_events_test: the DSL's on execute FILE:LINE.
  • mmu_integration_test: FSRC-* for the identities the steps and breakpoints use.

docs.title: 7.6 Lifetime: resets, snapshots, rewind and tapes
docs.text:
The stores describe a program. When the machine is replaced, whether by a reset, a snapshot, a state load, a rewind or the arrival of a tape's program, they may describe a program that is no longer there. This page is the set of rules that decides, for each store and each kind of replacement, between keep, drop and stale. (The user's labels and comments are not among the stores that follow these rules: that store is kept across every replacement, 7.4.6.) The C variable store (7.9) is not a fourth store: it is part of the SourceMap it was read from, so these rules apply to it with no code of its own. All the rules run in one place, Impl::recheck() (src/debug/debugger_source.cpp).

A landing only marks the new generation. recheck() judges it, run first by every reader and writer. A rewind inside the ring restores what was attached there; any other landing keeps a map only if its identity matches memory now; a tape's program is judged where the CPU first runs it.

docs.title: The load generation
docs.text:
A load generation is a counter that says which machine's history a store and a trace entry belong to. Impl::generation_counter is the source, and DebugState::load_generation() publishes the current value. It lives in the backend, not in the Emulator, because a cold boot rebuilds the emulator and a counter it owned would restart and collide with the cache keys. It is host-side state: it is not saved in a state file.

A new generation begins in two places (Impl::begin_generation()):

  • load_program_sidecars(): the sidecars about to be attached belong to the program loaded now;
  • Impl::machine_replaced(), for any landing that is not a rewind-ring restore.

Each rewind slot records the generation it was taken in (RewindBuffer::Slot::generation), and RewindBuffer::restore_nearest() sets it as the current one before loading the state, so the hook that fires inside the load already sees the landing's generation, and sets DebugState::restoring_from_rewind() for the duration (RingRestore).

docs.title: The hook only marks; recheck() judges
docs.text:
Emulator::init() and Emulator::load_state() end by calling debug_after_machine_transition_(), which calls the machine-replaced hook the Debugger installed (DebugState::notify_machine_replaced()). The hook (Impl::machine_replaced()) resets the backend's own stop evidence with arm(None) and then sets one of two flags: ring_pending for a ring restore (and notes the restored generation), or, for any other landing, begins a generation and sets landing_pending. It does nothing else, because the machine may still be half-built when the hook fires (inside init(), or a warm start).

Impl::recheck() does the work, when somebody looks. Every reader runs it first (source_map(), source_map_status(), variables(), source_location(), lookup(), lookup_name(), symbols(), executed_source_lines(), source_step()), and so does every writer (load_map(), clear_symbols(), load_source_map(), clear_source_map(), load_program_sidecars()), so a pending landing is judged before the writer's change and cannot undo it later. Debugger::pump() runs it too, so a landing is announced to listeners even if nobody reads. It returns at once when nothing is pending. Transitions are collected in pending_log and announced to listeners at Info after the flags are cleared, so a listener that reads back sees a settled backend.

docs.title: Tier 1: a rewind-ring restore
docs.text:
When recheck() finds ring_pending, and the landing's generation g differs from the one the stores are attached for (attach_gen), it puts back the attachment of that generation:

  • The record comes from the attachment cache, Impl::attach_cache: one Attachment per generation, holding the sidecar SourceMap and SymbolTable (shared, immutable), the reason text, and the sidecar identity checks still to make. It keeps the last ATTACH_CACHE_MAX = 4 (ATTACH_CACHE_MAX, debugger_impl.h:204); when a fifth is added the oldest record is evicted. cache_push_current() erases a generation's existing record and appends the new one, so a replaced record becomes the newest and is the last to be evicted.
  • A restored store is assigned into the existing objects, so the Qt panels' &symbols() stays valid.
  • With no record, the sidecar stores are cleared with "this point of the history is before the program was loaded".
  • The user's symbols never change with lifetime. The user's source map is re-verified only if it was last judged in another generation, and not at all while it is still waiting for a tape's program.

Log lines say what happened ("Restored the program's ... of this point in the history", "Dropped the program's ... before the program was loaded").

docs.title: Tier 2: any other landing
docs.text:
A reset, a snapshot load, a state loaded from outside the ring, an RZX playback start, or a program loaded by hand: fresh is true (landing_pending and the generation is the newest one), and the stores are judged by identity (7.2).

  • The program's sidecars are kept only if the source map carries an identity and verify_identity(source_map) (over Mmu::peek() and Debugger::peek(Page{n})) matches memory now. Then the generation moves (attach_gen = g) and the attachment is cached. A mismatch, or a map with no identity, drops the sidecars with the reason "its binary identity does not match the program now in memory", or "the machine was reset or replaced and it has no binary identity to check". Sidecar symbols with no source map beside them have nothing to check, so they are dropped at such a landing too. The attachment is dropped from the stores but its cached record stays: a rewind into the generation before the landing brings it back.
  • A kept map is checked again. A reset's ROM may clear RAM only later, so a kept map sets pause_verify_sidecar (or pause_verify_user) and the clock; at the next time the machine is paused with the clock moved, recheck() verifies it again and drops the map if it no longer matches. A run that is never paused does not get this second look.
  • The user's source map is judged the same way (verify_user()) and, on a mismatch or no identity, goes stale, not away: source_map() and source_location() answer empty, source_map_status() says Stale with the file and the reason, and loading it again by hand makes it live.
  • A program the guest loads for itself (the NextZXOS browser, LOAD "") is invisible to the backend: it sees no landing, so its predecessor's sidecars stay until a reset or a load. Loading the same program again (a rebuild) attaches the new build's map (SRCLIFE-17); a map loaded by hand across such a load stays the user's, stale without an identity and live when the new build matches it (SRCLIFE-18).

Back and Reverse Continue count a trace entry only if it belongs to the current generation (TraceLog::recorded() plus the markers): Impl::trace_gens holds (first trace sequence number, generation) markers, kept in step with the trace's retained window (note_generation(), generation_of_seq()) and cleared when a cold boot makes a new TraceLog.

docs.title: A tape's program: the verify window
docs.text:
A tape's program is not in memory when load_program_sidecars() returns, so a map that carries an identity (an SLD's hash, z88dk byte checks) cannot be judged yet. It attaches at once and pending (SidecarLoad::sources_pending, SourceMapStatus::pending; for a hand load, load_source_map(path, accept, verify_at_first_execution)), and the attach line ends (identity check pending: the program loads from tape). Rule-4 sections bind at the attach, since that is where the loader puts the bytes.

  • The check. Impl::add_check() stores a DeferredCheck: a copy of the map (the live store may be replaced under it), the units still to judge and their SourceMap::verify_spans(), and which stores answer for the verdict: guards_sources (the live source store, the user's or a sidecar's) and guards_symbols (the sidecar symbols that came with the map, so they go with a map of another build even when the user's source map is the one kept). At most one check per owner.
  • The trigger. DebugState has a one-shot verify window: a range of PCs set by Impl::sync_verify_window() to [min lo, max hi) over the pending spans of all checks (set_verify_window()). While it is set the machine is armed (verify_hold_ is an armed() contributor of its own, with magic_hold_, in refresh_gates_() and SuspendScope). The emulator asks verify_window_hit(pc), two compares, first in run_frame()'s armed block (verify_window_hit, emulator.cpp:10423), before consume_step_off(), the legacy breakpoint test and the execute gate, and in step_frame_slot() for a debugger Step (verify_window_hit, emulator.cpp:12110).
  • The verdict is recorded, not applied. On a hit, Impl::verify_hook(pc) takes predict_fetch(pc), finds the spans of each check that contain pc in that exact memory, judges each unit now with verify_identity_unit() (through Debugger::peek, so it reads page 20 while it is unmapped and touches no watchpoint, latch or ring), removes the unit and its spans, and sets verify_due. A mismatch sets mismatch. The hook never pauses, and does nothing in replay_mode().
  • Applying it. Impl::apply_deferred() is the first thing recheck() does when verify_due, so a reader, or a stop on the very instruction that triggered the check, already sees the map judged. It logs one Info line per memory judged (Verified ... in page 20; N memory spaces still to check), Verified ... the program loaded from tape matches its binary identity when the last matches, and on a mismatch drops the sidecar map with its symbols through drop_sidecars(), or the user's map to None (not Stale: it was refused, as a mismatch at load refuses it), at error level with Rejected ... does not match its binary identity. The window stays set for the units not run yet, and is cleared when none remains.
  • Landings meanwhile.
