A landing that is not a ring restore judges a pending map whole, as it does any carried map: a match clears the check; a mismatch, or a reset before the program arrived, drops a sidecar map, while a user's map goes stale (verify_user()), unlike the verify-window verdict above, which takes it to None; a ring restore brings back the generation's Attachment::checks, updated at every judged space, so a rewind keeps what was verified. A user's pending map is carried into the next program's load, and across rewinds, still pending.
  • --source-map with a tape. The loop owner polls source_map_status() once per tick; a map dropped by the check exits 1 (7.3).

docs.title: A dot command's map: judged at its entry
docs.text:
A z88dk dot command is not a program the emulator loads. NextZXOS copies the file into a DivMMC RAM bank when the command is typed and runs it from $2000 there, so at the moment the map is attached nothing says whether the right command is in memory, and a landing says nothing about it either. The map therefore has its own rule, on top of the tape machinery above. SourceMap::dot() (source_map.h:199) is set by the z88dk adapter (7.4.3, rule 5).

  • Always deferred. load_source_map() defers a dot map whatever verify_at_first_execution says (verify_at_first_execution, debugger_source.cpp:502), when it has any byte check. add_check() marks the check dot only if one of its units is the DivMMC bank, dot_entry_unit() = DivmmcRam{kNextZxosDotBank} (bank 2, kNextZxosDotBank, z88dk_space.h:46); a dot map with no byte check of the DivMMC part has no entry to judge and takes the tape rule (add_check(), debugger_source.cpp:161-176).
  • The state. dot_reset() (debugger_source.cpp:183) puts the check back to "waiting for the entry": every unit is to judge again, but only the entry (the DivMMC unit) is armed: the spans of every other unit (a dotx's main part, in main RAM) are moved to held, not armed. dot_match() (debugger_source.cpp:200) is the entry matching: the DivMMC unit is done, entry_ok is set and the held spans are armed, which from then on follow the tape rule (judged where the CPU first runs them).
  • The trigger. sync_verify_window() always includes kDotEntry ($2000, kDotEntry, debugger_source.cpp:114) in the window of a dot check (kDotEntry, debugger_source.cpp:299-302). verify_hook(pc) (debugger_source.cpp:315) judges when pc == kDotEntry and predict_fetch(pc) is the entry unit: a match records the verdict Verified and calls dot_match() once; a mismatch is another dot command: if the entry had matched it goes back to dot_reset(), the event is NotTheOne, and nothing is dropped. apply_deferred() (debugger_source.cpp:372) tells each verdict once ("The dot command started in <space> is not the one source map '<file>' describes; it stays pending"; Verified ... the dot command in <space> matches its binary identity) and keeps the check: it is never finished (checks.push_back at debugger_source.cpp:430), so a later entry that does not match puts the map back to pending.
  • A landing does not judge it. recheck() (debugger_source.cpp:976): for a user's map that is a dot map, verify_user() returns at once, keeping the map live and not stale (verify_user, debugger_source.cpp:990-999); the checks are re-derived by dot_landing(fresh) (debugger_source.cpp:233). A fresh landing (reset, state load, program load, cold boot) sends the user's dot checks (dot_landing() skips the others) to dot_reset(): pending until the next entry. A ring restore reads back what the original run showed at the landed cycle.
  • The history. dot_record() (debugger_source.cpp:213) appends a snapshot {generation, cycle, entry_ok, units, spans, held} to DeferredCheck::history at every judgement and every change of the check, replacing the records of the same generation from that cycle on (a re-run replaces what the first run recorded from there), and keeping at most kDotHistoryMax = 256 (kDotHistoryMax, debugger_impl.h:167; the oldest go, and a landing older than the oldest reads pending). dot_landing(false) picks the last record of the landed generation strictly before the landed cycle (a verdict at cycle C applies to the instruction about to run at C, which a landing at C has not run); none means pending. Records of earlier generations are kept, so a rewind back across a reset reads them.
  • A hand load made while the command already runs. load_source_map() calls dot_adopt() (debugger_source.cpp:256) for a dot map: if predict_fetch(PC) is the entry unit and the bank holds this command, it judges like a landing and is verified at once (dot_match()); the result is no longer pending and its note is the ordinary identity note (dot_adopt(), debugger_source.cpp:522-528).
  • RZX. An RZX playback start is a landing like any other (above), and --source-map with a replay accepts only a dot map (7.3): the map attaches pending at start-up and the verify hook does not distinguish a replayed session from a live one (replay_mode() is the rewind replay's flag, emulator.h:1254, not RZX's). What the row z88dk-dot-source-rzx-func pins is the attach and the refusal, not a verdict reached during playback.
  • Where it shows. SourceMapStatus::dot (debugger.h:1214, set at SourceMapStatus::dot, debugger_source.cpp:603) tells the Source tab to word its pending note ...when the dot command runs (7.7).

docs.title: What the backend cannot see
docs.text: Only landings it is told about and loads that go through it. A program the guest loads itself (LOAD "", the NextZXOS browser) is invisible, which is why its predecessor's sidecars stay until a reset or a load. And an identity is a snapshot of the image as it was right after the load: a program may legitimately change variables inside its own image afterwards, which is why a hand load can accept a known mismatch (accept_identity_mismatch).

docs.title: Where it is tested
docs.text: source_debug_test: SRCLIFE-* (ring restores, the attachment cache and its eviction, state and snapshot landings, RZX start, the stale user map, rewind past a load, a rebuild), SRCDBG-TAPE-* (the verify window and the deferred checks, per memory) and SRCDBG-OWN-* (ownership). source_debug_posix_test holds the rows whose sidecars are POSIX file types (a looping link, a FIFO), which wine cannot create.

docs.title: 7.7 The frontends
docs.text:
Every frontend reaches the stores through the backend facade (src/debug/debugger.h) and nothing else; none holds a SourceMap or a SymbolTable. This page says what each one reads, and describes in full the only one with a source view: the Qt debugger's Source tab. For the verbs themselves see 3.9.1; for a user's steps see chapter 10 of the user guide, Source-level debugging.

The facade at the top is the whole interface. The Qt window is the only frontend that draws source text; GDB, ZRCP and scripts print or subscribe; DZRP has no source surface and no C variable surface at all.

Frontend Reads Adds Page Qt debugger source_location(), source_map(), source_map_status(), source_page(), lookup(), the breakpoint groups, executed_source_lines(), c_frames(), c_locals(), c_globals(), c_children(), read_c_value(), c_variables_status() The Source tab, the Variables tab, the Breakpoints rows, the Call Stack column, symbol names, the long address below, and 3.10.2 GDB RSP source_location(), symbols(), mmu_slots(), c_frames(), c_locals(), c_globals(), read_c_value(), c_variables_status() monitor src, monitor sym, monitor mmu, monitor locals, monitor globals, monitor print 3.10.4 ZRCP load(), mmu_slots(), read_c_value() (through the DSL) smartload reaches the sidecars; get-memory-pages names the memory; CVAR(path) in evaluate and in conditions 3.10.5 DZRP Nothing None: no source and no C variable surface 3.10.3 Scripts source_map().resolve(), load_map(), read_c_value() on execute FILE:LINE, --map, the cvar(PATH) atom 3.10.6 Loop owners (headless, SDL, Qt) load_source_map(), source_map_status() --source-map 7.3

docs.title: The Qt Source tab
docs.text: SourcePanel (src/debugger/source_panel.*) shows the line of the PC from the backend's source map and carries the source-step buttons. It holds no copy of the map. What it keeps is presentation: the file shown (shown_file_), the text loaded and its modification time (loaded_source_, loaded_mtime_), whether the view was placed (placed_), the Disassembly's selection (disasm_range_), the address being browsed (browse_addr_) or the file being browsed (browse_file_, exclusive with it), the File list's cached items (combo_files_) and the reason report_sidecars() gave it.

docs.title: What one refresh does
docs.text:
SourcePanel::refresh_() (source_panel.cpp:615) runs while the machine is paused, whenever the window's paused stamp changed (3.10.2: the stamp carries a flag for "the loaded file changed on disk", DebuggerManager::paused_stamp(), debugger_manager.cpp:969; the flag is SourcePanel::file_changed_on_disk(), source_panel.cpp:574). In order:

  1. update_buttons(paused) (source_panel.cpp:516): the forward steps need a paused machine and a non-empty map; Back and Reverse Continue also need rewind_blocked() empty and the trace on. It emits steps_available(forward, backward), so the Debug > Source menu items and the buttons share one predicate.
  2. Running: show_running() says "Running", drops the highlight and the browse.
  3. source_map_status() says Stale or None: a message and nothing else (show_message()). A pending status appends a note to whatever is shown: Source map not verified yet: it is checked when the program first runs its code, or for a dot command ...when the dot command runs (status.dot, source_panel.cpp:650).
  4. The location is source_location(pc), or, while browsing, source_location(browse_addr_) (the browse ends if that address has no line now, or another map is loaded, source_panel.cpp:658-676). A file browse (browse_file_) skips the location altogether and goes to refresh_file_browse_() (see Opening another file below); it ends when another map is loaded or the map no longer names the file. The memory shown in the label is memtext::text(dbg_, style_, source_page(addr), addr) (source_panel.cpp:684).
  5. The text, loaded by one helper for every path, SourcePanel::load_text_() (the PC's line, an address browse and a file browse differ only in the wording of their two messages). A file the map carries as embedded text (SourceMap::embedded_text(), the m4 output of the CRT from prog.lis, 7.2) is shown from the map and labelled (m4 output, from <listing>). Otherwise a z88dk record in a .m4 file with no embedded text gets a message of its own, decided before any file is read (z88dk counts the m4 output, which the build does not keep). Otherwise source_search::resolve() finds the file (below); no file gives "source file not found" and enables Locate File. A file is reloaded when its modification time changes, so an edit-and-rebuild never highlights a line of the old text (lastModified(), source_panel.cpp:821). A line past the end of the file found gives "has only N lines; it is not the text the build used" (file_lines, source_panel.cpp:707-709; the line count ignores the final newline, file_line_count(), source_panel.cpp:63). The label's tooltip is the path found.
  6. The label ends with SourcePanel::also_text() (source_panel.cpp:600): lookup_all() for the address, minus the primary and any entry with the same file:line, as also: f:l, ...; then the browse text (browsing; the PC is at f:l, $addr); then the pending note.
  7. The extra selections, in this order so a later one wins on its own line: memory coverage (executed_source_lines(), tint coverage_line), the Disassembly's linked lines (linked_lines_(), tint linked_line), the PC's line (the editor's Highlight, only when the file shown is the PC's file).
  8. Placement. The cursor moves and the view centres only when something moved: the line, the address, placed_ cleared or place_now_ set (place_now_, source_panel.cpp:762-777). A browse centres only a line that is out of view. A user who scrolled away on a paused tick stays put.

follow_pc() (source_panel.cpp:580) clears placed_ and the browse and refreshes at once. It changes what the tab shows without moving the machine, so the paused stamp cannot see it; DebuggerWindow::activate_follow_pc() (debugger_window.cpp:1617) calls it, and apply_pause_state(true) runs that at every stop and step, so a stop at the very PC and line already shown still puts the view back.

docs.title: Finding the file
docs.text: source_search::resolve(recorded, map_file, dirs) (src/debug/source_search.h, Qt-free so the SDL-only and Windows trees test it): an absolute name; then the map's directory and each of its parents; then the search directories; tried suffix-major, the longest trailing part of the normalised name first, then the directories in order; a leading .. is dropped. DebuggerManager owns the list: set_source_dirs() (debugger_manager.cpp:311) takes the configured one (MainWindow::push_source_dirs(), main_window.cpp:3178, fed by apply_startup_config(), :2949: the saved list with the command line's --source-dir or paths.source_dirs value over it), and Locate File... (SourcePanel::locate_file(), source_panel.cpp:459) adds to a second, session-only list through DebuggerManager::on_source_dir_located() (debugger_manager.cpp:323). The effective list (configured, then located, duplicates dropped) is pushed to the panel by DebuggerManager::push_source_dirs() (debugger_manager.cpp:303) on every change and again in ensure_window(), since the window is created lazily. Locate derives the directory with source_search::root_for(), refuses a file of another name, and asks whether to save it; source_dir_save_requested is MainWindow's, which appends to [paths] source_dirs and refuses a directory that holds the list separator, as Preferences and --source-dir do: it would load back as two (it stays searched for the session). The session-only list is kept when the configured list changes (set_source_dirs() touches only the configured one). The manager announces each change (source_dirs_changed, because src/debugger/ names no logger) and MainWindow logs Source search path: ....

docs.title: Loading a map by hand
docs.text: The Source tab's Load Source Map... button and the Debug > Source > Load Source Map... item are one slot, DebuggerManager::on_load_sld() (debugger_manager.cpp:863). Its file dialog offers *.sld, *.sld.txt and *.map; the backend tells the format by content (7.3), so a z88dk map loads as source lines only, and the mismatch box and the failure title name no format. The Map menu's Load MAP File items load symbols through load_map(); they append the backend's reason to their failure box when a file was refused rather than unreadable. The sidecar report is DebuggerManager::report_sidecars() (:905): the log, and the main window's status bar for ten seconds.

docs.title: Colouring
docs.text:
SourceHighlighter (source_highlighter.*, a QSyntaxHighlighter that exists only in jnext_debugger).

  • The language. source_language_for(file, text) (source_highlighter.cpp:409): the extension, lower-cased, with a trailing .m4 dropped (zxn_crt.asm.m4 is assembly): c and h are C; asm, s, z80 and inc are assembly; bas is Boriel. Otherwise the first 200 lines vote: a line counts for a language when its first word is in that language's set alone (a column-0 label is skipped); the winner needs three votes and strictly more than the others (kMinVotes, source_highlighter.cpp:463); else Plain.
  • The word tables. The Z80/Z80N mnemonics and register words are not listed anywhere: they are enumerated once from disasm_one() over the seven opcode pages, so a new Z80N opcode is coloured the day the disassembler names it. The directive, C and Boriel tables are committed with the upstream file and commit they were read from (z80asm scan_def.h and keyword.def, sjasmplus directives.cpp, ISO C11 6.4.1, Boriel keywords.py).
  • The scanners are hand-written, linear per line, and carry multi-line comments and embedded assembly in the block state. The classes are the owner's ten (Role: Text, Keyword, Instruction, Preprocessor, Label, String, Char, Integer, Float, Comment); Text is the editor palette's text colour and never a format. Punctuation and operators (kKeywordPunct, source_highlighter.cpp:280) are Keyword, tested at each scanner's fall-through point after comment, string, char, number and word detection, so those win; Qt merges adjacent equal formats, so -> or <<= is one Keyword range. A sign is part of a number only inside an exponent (-5 is a Keyword and an Integer). C and Boriel numbers have their own scanners: Float is a point or an exponent, including the C hex-float p exponent; Boriel's t_HEXA, t_OCTAL and t_BIN are tried before t_NUMBER, and a $ or % suffix belongs to its identifier. The scanners are allocation-free per word. Formats set the foreground colour and nothing else, so the line geometry and the gutter alignment equal Plain's.
  • Entering a text. SourcePanel::set_source_text() (source_panel.cpp:537) is the one way: the language first, then the text, so a load is highlighted once with its own language.
  • Schemes. SourceScheme (platform/source_scheme.h) is the order of the words of the source.colour_scheme key: Auto, Light, Dark, Borland (static_asserts in app_config.cpp and source_highlighter.cpp:470). scheme_colours() (:587) holds one table per concrete scheme: background, text, the current-line bar's two colours, the coverage and linked-line tints, and a colour per class. Dark is derived, not kept: palette_tint::ink() of each Light colour over a fixed dark palette (#242424 and #F0F0F0, make_dark(), :531), so it does not depend on the application's own dark palette. Every scheme meets one legibility rule, which row QSRC-195 checks: text and classes 4.5:1 against the background (WCAG 1.4.3), bar text 4.5:1, bar against background 3:1, and any two colours at least CIE76 12 apart unless the scheme declares them shared (Borland's owner-given groups).
  • Applying one. SourcePanel::apply_scheme_() (source_panel.cpp:548) takes the panel's palette (the application's, never the editor's) in, resolves Auto against it (resolve_scheme()), hands the classes to the highlighter (apply_palette() rehighlights only when a class colour changed, never on a paused tick or a repeat) and puts the background, text and bar colours on the editor's palette (Base, Text, Highlight, HighlightedText). The background is a palette role, not a format, so it fills the whole viewport. set_colour_scheme() (source_panel.cpp:565) applies at once (Preferences Apply while the machine runs) and refreshes, because the tints are selections refresh_() builds and a paused tick redraws only when the machine moved. The setting is held by DebuggerManager::set_source_scheme() (debugger_manager.cpp:317) and pushed by ensure_window(), fed by MainWindow::apply_startup_config().
  • What a scheme does not reach. The gutter and its header paint from the panel's palette, so a scheme never colours them, and the breakpoint marks stay as they are. The current-line marker is an ExtraSelection reading the editor's Highlight; Qt draws a selection's colours over the layout's formats, so no syntax colour shows on that line.

docs.title: The gutter and breakpoints
docs.text:
The editor is a private QPlainTextEdit subclass, SourceEdit (source_panel.cpp:99), with a gutter widget in a left viewport margin and a header strip above it (setViewportMargins; objects source_gutter and source_gutter_header), because the visible blocks' geometry is protected.

  • Columns. BP | Line: the number is blockNumber() + 1 (paint_gutter(), source_panel.cpp:158).
  • The mark of a line is computed at paint time, for the visible lines only (SourcePanel::line_mark(), source_panel.cpp:1131, over line_state(), source_panel.cpp:1086), so it is never stale and needs no cache. line_state() derives, for line L of the file shown: starts (where the map says L begins, from resolve(file:line), so an alias line is marked), placed (those starts the memory mapped now supplies), drawn (this GUI's Execute breakpoints, from BreakpointModel::pc_breakpoints(), that the Disassembly would draw: a logical one, or one tied to source_page(addr), sitting on a placed start or on any instruction whose primary line is L), hidden (breakpoints tied to exactly a start whose memory is not mapped now) and armed (starts carrying one of this GUI's Execute breakpoints, mapped now or not). Every start armed is the full glyph, some the left half; a line is drawn at all only while a breakpoint is drawn on it. breakpoint_glyph.h paints the glyph for both panels.
  • The PC wedge: paint_pc_marker() (breakpoint_glyph.h:46), the amber wedge paint_gutter() draws on highlighted_line() only, in the 5-px strip after the number cell (x in [width-6, width-2], which no pinned pixel reading uses); the colour goes through palette_tint::ink(), and the text highlight stays the palette's own.
  • A click calls SourcePanel::toggle_breakpoint_at_line() (source_panel.cpp:1174), the one toggle: it removes what the line shows plus a hidden group tied to an unmapped memory, else add_source_line() (not idempotent, hence the check). The context menu calls the same function. A line with no code shows the store's reason as a tooltip.
  • In the model. BreakpointModel lists an Execute subscription with a fetch-source qualifier as the GUI's own row (Row::space). A file:line is one backend group (subscribe_source_line()) armed at every place it compiled to, and the model folds the group into ONE row with its location count (Row::group, Row::locations; the Symbol / Source cell reads main.bas:11 (2 locations)). Remove, the Enabled cell and Edit act on the whole group, and the row is enabled only while every location is. The Add and Edit dialogs and Breakpoints > Add Execute Breakpoint share that rule and show the store's reason ("no code at main.bas:5"). The gutter draws a location only while its FetchSource supplies the address (pc_marked(addr, space)), and a click on its dot removes that location, not the group. The Call Stack's last column looks up each frame's caller with its recorded FetchSource (CallFrame::caller_space).

docs.title: The context menu
docs.text:
SourcePanel::fill_context_menu() (source_panel.cpp:1289, called from the editor's and the gutter's contextMenuEvent) offers the Disassembly's actions on the source line: Copy, Copy with Addresses, Select All; Toggle Breakpoint; Run to Here (run_to_line_requested, which DebuggerManager runs as Debugger::run_to_source_line behind its corruption gate; Enter in the editor and the bindable Run to Cursor, while the tab has the focus, are the same request); Show in Disassembly (show_address_requested, DisasmPanel::show_address()); and the watch and data-breakpoint entries. Those entries come from operand_menu.{h,cpp} (add_operand_actions()), shared with the Disassembly's own menu so the two cannot differ. The Source tab fills a MenuOperands from the labels at the line's places and the word under the pointer. A word is classified as a register in parentheses, a number or a name, and a name goes through SourcePanel::symbol_for_word() (source_panel.cpp:1199), the single seam for the C names (resolve_key("@" + word); @ forces a symbol).

After the Show in Disassembly entry the menu carries the user-annotation entries: Add / Rename Label…, Remove Label and Add / Edit Comment…, from add_annotation_actions() (src/debugger/annotation_menu.cpp:77), once per place the line compiled to (SourcePanel::fill_context_menu() calls add_annotation_actions, src/debugger/source_panel.cpp:1369). The Disassembly shows the labels and comments; the Source tab does not. How they are stored, saved and drawn is 7.4.6, section 10.

docs.title: Selection sync with the Disassembly
docs.text:
DebuggerWindow::create_panels() wires the two panels with four connect() calls (connect(), debugger_window.cpp:1496-1510), and nothing else couples them. Each carries only what the user did in its sender, so no move echoes.

  • Source to Disassembly. SourcePanel::source_lines_selected(file, first, last, reveal) is emitted by emit_lines_() (source_panel.cpp:1021), only when the file or the lines changed (lines_file_, lines_first_, lines_last_; a message and Running emit an empty file, and none = true says the text stays but nothing of it is selected). The lines are selected_blocks_()'s, the same rule as Copy with Addresses (a selection ending at a block start does not take that block). The editor's cursorPositionChanged / selectionChanged slot passes reveal = true (selectionChanged, source_panel.cpp:430-435); a move the panel makes itself (the PC placement of refresh_(), a text load, set_disasm_selection()) runs under a SyncScope (syncing_), so that slot stays silent, and ends with emit_lines_(false, ...), so a stop tints the PC statement's other instructions without scrolling. DisasmPanel::set_source_lines() (disasm_panel.cpp:438) stores the range; a row is linked (source_linked(), linked_at_(), :425-433) when lookup_all() in its own space has a location on a selected line of that file, the primary or not. paintEvent fills a linked row with source_sync_colors::linked() before the PC row, the selection and the coverage bar. With reveal and no linked row in view, the view centres on the first start of resolve(file:line) that is mapped now; otherwise it never moves.
  • Disassembly to Source. DisasmPanel::selection_changed(lo, hi, caret) comes from the user paths only (notify_selection_(), disasm_panel.cpp:413: a press, a drag, a navigation key, Select All, the menu's collapse), when the triple differs from the last one sent. show_address() and a refresh do not emit; set_source_lines() forgets the last triple, so the next click on the same lines is a change again. SourcePanel::set_disasm_selection() (source_panel.cpp:976) is ignored while running or without a map, stores the range (disasm_range_, dropped when the machine runs, so a stop shows no tint of it), and sets browse_addr_ unless the caret's primary line is the PC's own statement. refresh_() then describes browse_addr_ instead of the PC. The lines of the instructions in the range (linked_lines_(), :1040, walking instruction_length over memory_reader()) get an ExtraSelection in the scheme's linked_line, after the coverage tints and before the PC's. There is no cache of those lines: a full 64K range cost about 3.5 ms when measured at design time (not re-measured since), and it is paid at each refresh(), which runs only when the paused stamp changed, not on every tick.
  • Show in Source. DisasmPanel::show_source_requested(addr), from a menu item present only while a map is loaded and enabled only where lookup() finds a line. The window raises the Source tab and calls SourcePanel::show_address() (source_panel.cpp:996).

Browsing ends at follow_pc() (every stop), show_running(), the map going away (the None and Stale branches of refresh_()), another loaded map (browse_map_), an address with no line now, a file the map no longer names, and Go to PC Line (go_to_pc_line(), source_panel.cpp:1002). A message about the browsed line itself (file not found, a .m4 line without a listing) does not end it, so the message and Locate File... stay usable, and Go to PC Line stays enabled. Every accepted Disassembly selection places the cursor on the caret's line (place_now_, cleared by the placement itself, so the next ticks leave the cursor and scroll alone). A Source move made while the machine runs announces nothing. The gutter, the menu, Copy with Addresses and Run to Cursor act on shown_file_, so they act on the file browsed. Rows QSRC-176 to QSRC-189 and QSRC-201 to QSRC-208 pin the behaviour; source_sync_colors.h is the one definition of the linked colour for both views; the Source tab keeps one per scheme (SchemeColours::linked_line), tested for legibility like the coverage tint (row QSRC-189).

docs.title: Opening another file
docs.text:
The File list (source_file_combo, a QComboBox in a row of its own under the loads row) is the only way to show a file without an address. Its items are SourceMap::files() (every file the map names, zero-width and alias files included, normalised, in byte order), rebuilt by sync_file_list_() from refresh() only when that set differs from the cached combo_files_: comparing the contents, not loaded_file(), because a reload of the same path may name other files, and an idle paused tick must redraw nothing. Its current item is the file browsed, else the file shown, under a QSignalBlocker; it is enabled by update_buttons() from the forward-steps predicate (paused and a non-empty map), and the Debug > Source > Open Source File... item follows the same steps_available signal; that item raises the tab and calls SourcePanel::choose_file() (focus and popup).

A pick (activated, so only the user's) calls SourcePanel::open_file(), which ignores a name the map does not have. The PC's own file is go_to_pc_line() (a click on the PC's statement is not browsing); the file already shown while browsing changes nothing; otherwise browse_addr_ is dropped, browse_file_ and browse_map_ set and the view placed at line 1 (placed_, place_now_) by refresh_file_browse_(). That path shares load_text_() and add_tints_() (coverage and the Disassembly's lines, keyed on the file shown) with the PC path, has no line to range-check, draws the PC bar only when the PC is in the file browsed (possible without a stop when a client sets the PC while paused), and labels the view file (browsing; the PC is at f:l, $addr) with no address of its own. A file the tab cannot find keeps the browse, so Locate File... still works. A Disassembly selection that has a source line (set_disasm_selection()) clears browse_file_. Rows QSRC-210 to QSRC-223 and SRCFILES-01 pin it.

docs.title: The Qt Variables tab
docs.text:
VariablesPanel (src/debugger/variables_panel.*) is a tab of the bottom-right tab widget, between Watches and Breakpoints (the window has no docks: its layout is fixed). It shows the C variables of one call frame and the globals and statics as a QTreeWidget (Name, Type, Value, Address). Like every CAP-SRC reader it holds no copy of a store, and it formats nothing: every value, type, refusal and note is the facade's text (c_locals(), c_globals(), c_children(), 7.10); the panel only joins a row's notes onto its value ((note; note), also the tooltip) and spells its address.

  • Paused only. refresh() returns at once unless set_paused(true) (DebuggerManager::set_panels_paused()), like the Call Stack. DebuggerWindow::refresh_panels() calls it after the Call Stack's own refresh.
  • Frames. A frame selector lists c_frames(): <function> at <file>:<line>, or <not C code> $XXXX, frame 0 suffixed (current). A refresh at a new master cycle (a new stop) selects frame 0; one at the same cycle (an idle tick, an input redraw, a style switch) keeps the choice, so a frame picked in an older caller survives everything but moving the machine.
  • One mapping. The Call Stack panel lists the tracked CALLs newest first, with no row for frame 0 or for a frame found through the saved-frame-pointer chain; c_frames() takes frame k's PC from the CALL tracked[n-k], so Call Stack row i is C frame i + 1. That is written once, in VariablesPanel::call_stack_row() (variables_panel.cpp:117) and frame_of_call_row(). CallStackPanel::call_selected(row) (emitted only for the user's choice: a refresh and select_row() set a guard) goes to select_frame(row + 1), and frame_changed(k) goes back to select_row(call_stack_row()), which emits nothing, so there is no loop. After each refresh the window re-selects the row the chosen frame maps to (-1 clears it), because a refresh may have rebuilt the Call Stack's rows.
  • Lazy children. An item that is an aggregate or a pointer to something (not void *) has the child indicator and no children. Expanding it calls c_children(frame, path, 0, 100); when total exceeds 100 the children are range items [0..99], [100..199], ..., each read with its own first. A refused expansion (null pointer, an unreadable pointer) is one placeholder item with the facade's reason. The panel never decodes a type.
  • Rows act on themselves. A row that another visible variable of its name shadows, and a Globals row whose function::name is shared by two block statics, has an internal handle as its path (#<n>, never typed or shown). Edit and expand go through write_c_value_row() and c_children_row() with that path, so they act on the variable the row shows and not on the innermost one the name reaches; the keys are prefix + path, so the two rows have two keys. A message about such a row names the variable (t (shadowed, in f), f::n (static)), built from the row's root label (RoleRootLabel, inherited by its children). Watch is a name expression: it uses CValueRow::name_path, and where that is empty (a shadowed row) or ambiguous (a shared static path, also in Locals) the action is disabled and its tooltip says why. itemFromIndex() is protected in Qt5, so the delegate reaches it through VarTree::item_of().
  • In-place refresh. Every item has a key (a path, a range, a file group, prefixed by the section and, for Locals, the function). sync() compares a parent's children with the new rows by key: unchanged keys are updated in place, so the selection, the scroll position and the expansion stay; changed keys rebuild that parent and re-open the items whose key the user had open (expanded_). Only open items are re-read; a closed item's children are dropped, to be read when it opens.
  • Addresses. A global's where is a page address (long_address(addr, space, style, next_layout)); a stack slot or a followed pointer is a CPU address, spelled with the memory mapped there NOW (memtext::now_of(mmu_slots(), addr): what a read reaches); a register local shows its register names. Debug > Physical Addresses reaches the panel through apply_address_style() like every other.
  • Editing. The Value cell of an item whose facade row is ok and not an aggregate is editable (Node::editable: a pointer is, its value is its address): a double-click on the cell, or the context menu's Edit Value, calls edit_item() while paused. The editor is the ValueDelegate's line edit, which holds RoleEditText (the first space-separated word of the facade's value: string slicing, so the panel still formats no number) and fills it once per editor (a keystroke is host input, so the manager's next paused tick redraws the row and the view offers the editor its data again: a refill would put the old text back over what is being typed, QVARW-09), and never writes the model: setModelData() hands the text to commit_edit(), which writes nothing when it equals the edit text and otherwise calls write_c_value(client_, frame_, path, text). On success nothing else happens: the write bumped the revision, so the manager's next paused tick redraws every panel (paused_stamp()), this one with the value read back. On a refusal variables_message shows <path>: <why> (cleared by the next success or a new stop) and the cell keeps its value, because the model was never written. client_ is the window's, set by DebuggerManager::set_panels_client() like the Memory panel's, so the MUTATE line names it. No new setting, so no CLI flag. The Watches C rows stay read-only.

docs.title: C watches in the Watches tab
docs.text:
A WatchEntry has a kind, Memory (the address watch) or CVariable (CVarWatch: the facade path, the function and CDB module of a parameter or local, empty for a global, a file static or a static local). VariablesPanel::watch_item() (the right-click menu's one action, refused while the machine runs: the tab shows the last stop, and a binding taken from the live machine would not be what the user pointed at) builds it and emits watch_requested; the window connects that to WatchPanel::add_c_watch(), and the current tab does not change.

  • Binding. A Locals item is bound to the frame's function: at each paused refresh refresh_c_row() reads it with read_c_value(k, path), k the NEWEST c_frames() frame whose function has that name and module (not a frame index: it would go out of scope at every new call of the same function), and when there is none the Value is out of scope: <function> is not on the call stack with Address and Memory empty. A Globals item (its path is file::name) and a static local (pinned from Locals as function::name, with the file before it, a.c::init::done, when the function name is not unique, exactly as c_globals() spells it: find_var() prefers the CURRENT frame's function for a bare fn::, which could be another module's) are unbound and read in frame 0 by a path no local can shadow.
  • Paused only. DebuggerManager::set_panels_paused() tells the Watch panel; a running machine does not read a C row, which keeps the text of the last stop (kept in the entry, so an Add or Remove that rebuilds the table shows it again). Memory rows are unchanged.
  • No store. Every C row shows c_variables_status().why, and binds again when a store with that function and path is attached.
  • Columns. Address is the 16-bit address or the register names; Label the path plus (in function); Type and Value the facade's text (a refusal is placeholder-coloured text); Memory the space the value is in (memtext::text(), a stack slot or pointee by what is mapped now).
  • Edit does nothing on a C row; Remove works on both kinds. C watches are not saved (no watch of any kind is).
  • While running, a frame chosen in the Variables selector or the Call Stack is ignored by select_frame(), and both go back to the frame the tree shows.

Rows QVAR-01 to -32 (debugger_variables_panel_test) pin the tab; CVCH-* and SRCDBG-CVCH-* the children.

docs.title: Which memory a view names
docs.text:
Every Qt view names the memory behind an address through debug/long_address.h (7.1) and nowhere else. The Qt-side wrapper is src/debugger/memory_text.h: memtext::text(dbg, style, space, addr) (memory_text.h:25) and memtext::next_layout(dbg) (:20), which is true only for the Next machine type (MachineType::ZXN_ISSUE2); any other machine prints the Friendly tag whatever the style.

DebuggerWindow holds one AddressStyle and hands it to each panel (set_address_style(), apply_address_style()) and to the BreakpointModel, whose rows are spelled in it; a toggle refreshes them all. The style is the setting debugger.physical_addresses (Debug > Physical Addresses, --set, a run override like debugger.attached).

Which space a view prints is a rule per view (design 10.3):

  • The line at PC and the Source tab show the fetch prediction (source_page()).
  • The other Disassembly lines, the MMU panel, the Memory panel's CPU view, Watches and Stack show the live data route of the address's slot (SlotInfo::now), the memory the bytes beside the tag came from.
  • The Memory panel's Slot and Page views show the space shown; a slot paged to nothing (NR >= 0xE0) is FLOAT, never a page the tag grammar refuses.
  • The Call Stack and the Breakpoints list show the recorded identity.
  • Where a qualifier was already printed the tag replaces it in place; elsewhere a column was added (Disassembly Mem, MMU Memory, Watches and Stack Memory, Call Stack Caller and Target memory). The Memory panel paints its tag as the item after the ASCII column, so dump_row() and the coverage underline never move. The legacy page qualifier of another client keeps its @NN, which is a different thing (7.1).

The instruction at the PC is read as the CPU will fetch it, not as a data read. Debugger::memory_reader() (debugger_inspect.cpp:838) takes the bytes of that one instruction (at most four) from Emulator::predict_instruction_bytes() and every other address from Mmu::peek(); at a DivMMC instant entry the M1 itself maps DivMMC, so a peek at the PC would show other bytes than the ones that execute. The Disassembly, step_over() (debugger_control.cpp:175: is_call_like() at :184 and instruction_length() at :190 read through it) and ZRCP cpu-step-over (ZrcpServer::cmd_cpu_step_over) all use it (rows LADDR-17 to LADDR-20).

docs.title: GDB, ZRCP, DZRP, scripts
docs.text:
GDB RSP (src/remote/gdb/rsp_server.cpp). monitor src [ADDR] (monitor_src(), :1063) prints $8CB8 main.c:19 P04 or $8CB8 unmapped P28: source_location() and the tag of source_page(addr). monitor sym (monitor_sym(), rsp_server.cpp:1026) prints the tag of the memory the lookup used; a name prints its tag when it is paged. monitor mmu (monitor_mmu(), rsp_server.cpp:923) prints each slot's now tag and, on the Next, the physical text of the slot's first byte. The server's own symbol and source verbs are described in 3.10.4.

The C variables are three more verbs over the facade of 7.10, read-only; the write is a fourth, monitor set var [FRAME] PATH = VALUE (monitor_set_var(), rsp_server.cpp:1215), over write_c_value(): OK and the value read back, or refused: <why> and E01. monitor_locals() (rsp_server.cpp:1107) prints the header of frame N (frame 0: main at main.c:21, fp $FF51 (prologue), from c_frames()), then one (type) name = value line per c_locals() row, and a [note] line under a row that has notes. monitor_globals() (rsp_server.cpp:1156) prints one line per c_globals() row named by its name_path (the typed path, never an internal handle), so a name pastes into print, and marks (ambiguous path) the entries whose path names more than one static (print refuses those), with the memory the variable lives in ($903E P04). monitor_print() (rsp_server.cpp:1179) takes the raw rest of the line, not the split words, because a C path may hold spaces (p -> y); a leading decimal word is the frame (a C path cannot start with a digit). A refusal (no C variables, an unknown name, no such frame) is text and OK, as monitor src does; a wrong argument is E01. They exist for any RSP client and for what z88dk-gdb gets wrong on its own: it resolves a file static by name across modules, prints the 48-bit float as <> 0.000000, shows an array with the wrong count and reads every global through the 16-bit view. Only the client of z88dk's master has monitor, so v2.4 cannot reach them.

ZRCP. CVAR(path) is jnext's one extension of ZEsarUX's condition dialect: evaluate does not hand its text to the DSL, it first translates it (translate_condition(), zrcp_condition.cpp), and cvar(...) was Error parsing. The tokeniser takes CVAR( followed by the raw path up to the first ) as one Tok::CVar operand (tokenise(), zrcp_condition.cpp:155); a (, a ", a missing ) and an empty path do not tokenise. The translator turns it into the DSL's cvar(path) and the canonical text echoes CVAR(path) with the path's case kept. Conditions compile through the same translation, so a breakpoint may carry it (PC=8D3EH AND CVAR(a)=2); a read that fails is ZEsarUX's Error evaluating parsed string, with no reason. A condition with no PC= first term is checked at every instruction, and a CVAR in it builds the C frames each time: put a PC= term first. The write is set-register CVAR(path)=value (cmd_set_register(), zrcp_server.cpp:1190): the command table's census pins ZEsarUX's ls, so no command can be added, and the extension is a branch of the one assignment verb. It takes the path up to the first ), then =, and the trimmed rest as the value (a value ZRCP's parse_number() reads, decimal or nnnnH, is converted to decimal text; anything else, -5, a fraction, 'A', 0x10, goes as typed) and calls write_c_value() in frame 0. Success answers set-register's own register line; every failure is ZEsarUX's Error changing register, with no reason. smartload "file" (ZrcpServer::cmd_smartload, zrcp_server.cpp:2652) calls Debugger::load() (debugger_reconstruct.cpp:465), which calls load_program_sidecars() after a successful load (load_program_sidecars(), debugger_reconstruct.cpp:528-532), so a program loaded over ZRCP gets its symbols and source map like --load, and a refused sidecar is logged to every client as a Warn line. get-memory-pages (memory_pages(), zrcp_format.cpp) names the eight slots of a Next from what each reads now (SlotInfo::now): RO the boot ROM, O<n> the 8 KB ROM page 2*image + half, A<n> RAM, SR<n> config-mode SRAM, DIV DivMMC; the overlays ZEsarUX has no spelling for print the slot's own mapping. On the other machines segment 0 is DIV while DivMMC is paged in.

DZRP. No source surface and no C variable surface: grep finds no source_* call and no c_* or read_c_value() call in src/remote/dzrp, and the protocol has no command that could carry a variable. DeZog reads the SLD or the map itself and evaluates its own breakpoint conditions (jnext arms a conditional DZRP breakpoint unconditionally). So a DeZog user gets no C variables from jnext. What DZRP shares with this chapter is the legacy bank+1 qualifier (7.1). CMD_GET_REGISTERS reports 0xFF for every ROM slot (is_rom, dzrp_server.cpp:549-553), because DeZog has no bank for the ROM values 0xE0-0xFE.

Scripts. on execute FILE:LINE resolves through source_map().resolve() at load time (source_map().resolve(), script_engine.cpp:330) and subscribes one Execute per start, each with the space its place was compiled for (space, script_engine.cpp:346); an unknown line is a diagnostic that names the reason. --map loads symbols with MapFormat::Z88dkOrSjasmplus (script_host.cpp:187, 7.3). Held scripts and the rest of the language are in 3.10.6.

cvar(PATH) is the one atom that reads a C variable: eval_int() (evaluator.cpp:276) calls read_c_value(0, path) (frame 0, where the CPU is) and c_int32_scalar() (7.10) and returns the int32. The store is looked up at each evaluation, so a script compiled before the program loaded works once the sidecars attach, and every refusal is an EvalError, never a 0. set cvar(PATH) = v is the write: parse_lvalue() makes it an ExprKind::CVar target and the Set action of script_engine.cpp calls write_c_value() in frame 0 with the int32 as CNewValue::From::Int32; a refusal is fail() with the facade's reason.

Reading C variables inside a delivery. A predicate runs inside the loops over the event table, and cvar() is the first reader there that runs recheck() (c_frames() and read_c_value() do): the first cvar() after a verdict the verify hook recorded in guest execution (verify_due, a tape program running its code) runs apply_deferred() and sync_call_stack() in the middle of a delivery, and announces pending_log to the listeners. That is safe, and the reasons are checkable: nothing reachable from recheck() reads or writes the event table (EventTable is touched in debugger_source.cpp only by history_stop_at(), which reads it), the log listeners are no-ops or printers (ScriptEngine::on_log()), so none can subscribe() under the Execute gate's range-for over the table, and a map dropped there only makes the reader say so. Row EVAL-CVAR-09 runs it on the tape fixture, both ways: right bytes (the map is verified inside the predicate, which then reads) and one wrong byte (the map is dropped inside the predicate, which is false with the facade's reason).

Headless, SDL, Qt loops. --source-map is attached by emulator_attach_cli_source_map() after the first successful --load (or at start-up for a dot command or an RZX replay, 7.3) and watched per tick by emulator_poll_cli_source_map() (source_map_watch_ in HeadlessApp, SdlApp and QtApp); a map dropped by the identity check sets exit code 1.

docs.title: 7.8 Tests, fixtures and adding a producer
docs.text:
Source-level debugging reads files other people's tools write, so its tests have a second job beyond checking the code: the expected values must come from the tools' real output, not from the code under test. This page lists the suites, explains where the fixtures come from and how they stay honest, and gives the checklist for supporting another toolchain.

The test counts are not written here, on purpose. test/unit-tests.conf is the only source (4.2), and a number copied into prose goes stale on the next branch. The process for writing rows, with the VHDL as the oracle where hardware is involved, is in doc/testing/UNIT-TEST-PLAN-EXECUTION.md.

docs.title: The suites
docs.text:
Suite What it covers source_map_test The std-only layer, with no emulator: SourceMap (SRCRNG-*, SRCMAP-*, SRCPATH-*, SRCTXT-01, SRCVAR-01), the SLD adapter (SLD-*, SLDL-*), the symbol table's pages (SYMPG-*), the NextBuild adapter (NBSYM-*), and the fixture manifest (Z88FIX-01, Z88FIX-02) z88dk_map_test The z88dk map: the source half (Z88MAP-*), the symbol half and binding (Z88SYM-*), C names (Z88CN-*), dot commands (Z88DOT-*, 7.4.3 rule 5), the C variable store (Z88CDB-*, 7.9) and the extents and frame helpers (Z88CDB-41..-50, 7.10), and the size cap and BOM of the symbol loaders (MAPCAP-*, MAPBOM-*) z88dk_lis_test The listing adapter (Z88LIS-*), including the placement of a label-less piece by its bytes (Z88LIS-36 to -47, 7.4.4 rule 5b) and the BOM (Z88LIS-35, -44) c_value_test The pure C value layer (c_value.cpp, 7.10): the 48-bit and IEEE floats, integers, pointers, arrays, structs, bitfields, the struct type lookup and type text, the path grammar and its evaluation, visible locals, register locals (CVALF-*), the children of an object (CVCH-*), the encoder of a written value (CVW-*), and the int32 rule of the script atom and ZRCP (CVINT-*) cdb_record_test The z88dk C debug records (__CDBINFO__, cdb_decode() in src/debug/cdb_record.cpp): un-escaping (cdb_unescape()), the scope split at the last ., the type chain, storage, T: members, what views hide (CdbHidden), refusals with their reasons, and every record of every committed map (CDB-*). Records measured from the z88dk master install are quoted in the rows with the probe and command source_debug_test The backend on a real machine: identity of fetches (SRCDBG-ID-*), sidecars and ownership (SRCDBG-SIDE-*, -OWN-*), symbols (SRCDBG-SYM-*), z88dk (SRCDBG-Z88-*, -LIS-*), tapes (SRCDBG-TAPE-*), the variable store's lifetime (SRCDBG-VAR-*), the tracker policy and the C frames (SRCDBG-CVAL-*, 7.10), writing a C variable (SRCDBG-CVW-*), the children of a C variable on a running machine (SRCDBG-CVCH-*), lifetime (SRCLIFE-*), dot commands (SRCDOT-*, 7.6), breakpoints (SRCBP-*), run to line (SRCRUN-*), steps (SRCSTEP-*, SRCDBG-STEP-*, -BACK-*, -HIST-*), call stack (SRCDBG-CS-*), coverage (SRCDBG-COV-*), the long address through a machine (LADDR-17 to -20; the pure formatter's LADDR-01 to -16 are in debugger_backend_test) source_debug_posix_test The rows whose fixtures are POSIX file types (a looping link, a FIFO); gated by OS mmu_test, mmu_integration_test The arbiter against the VHDL's memory map (FSRC-*) step_out_test, rewind_call_stack_test Step Out's RET predicate, and the call-stack tracker restored across a rewind (the frame-ending rule itself is SRCDBG-CS-08 to -15 in source_debug_test) debugger_backend_test Symbols across formats (SYM-*), and the pure long-address formatter (LADDR-01 to -16) gdb_rsp_test, zrcp_adapter_test, dzrp_adapter_test monitor src and monitor sym (GDB-MON-*); monitor locals, globals and print on the cvars fixtures (GDB-CVAR-*); ZRCP CVAR(path) in evaluate and conditions (ZRCP-CVAR-*); the C writes monitor set var (GDB-CVW-*) and set-register CVAR(path)=value (ZRCP-CVW-*); ZRCP get-memory-pages names and cpu-step-over at a DivMMC entry (LADDR-21, -22); DZRP's 0xFF for a ROM slot (DZRP-REG-08) script_events_test The DSL's on execute FILE:LINE and --map debugger_variables_panel_test The Qt Variables tab on a real Next running the z88dk fixtures: frames, locals, globals, lazy expansion, the Call Stack selection both ways, addresses, refresh, idle (QVAR-*, and editing a value QVARW-*, the C rows of the Watches tab included, 7.7); gated on Qt and the debugger script_eval_test The DSL evaluator; its EVAL-CVAR-* rows are the cvar(PATH) atom over a real Next machine and the committed cvars fixtures (scalars, members, elements, qualified names, banked globals, every refusal, no C variables, interpolation, a when, and a tape program's verdict applied inside a delivery) debugger_source_panel_test, debugger_verbs_test, debugger_panels_test, debugger_disasm_copy_test, debugger_menu_test The Qt Source tab (QSRC-*: the highlighter and schemes QSRC-190 to -200, the selection sync QSRC-176 to -189 and -201 to -208, the dot command's tab QDOT-*), the Map menu, and the long address in every panel (QLADDR-*); gated on Qt and the debugger

A suite marked ? in test/unit-tests.conf is gated; the harness checks that its absence matches the gate for the build (4.2).

Functional rows (test/00regression/functional_tests.conf):

Row Covers sld-labels-func An SLD sidecar's labels reach the symbol table a remote client reads, by page source-map-func A <stem>.sld beside a program attaches as its source map in every frontend; one whose identity does not match is rejected, with the reason z88dk-source-map-func A z88dk -debug map attaches as symbols and source lines, from beside the program and from --source-map, in every frontend z88dk-source-func The remote and script surface of the source map: on execute main.c:19 rules against the committed z88dk fixture z88dk-tape-source-func A z88dk map attaches to a tape program at once and its identity is judged where the CPU first runs the code gdb-z88dk-func The real z88dk-gdb client against the GDB server, with a program and its map nextbuild-symbols-func Memory.txt in headless, Qt and SDL script-map-pipe-func --map <(cmd), read once z88dk-dot-source-func A z88dk dot command's map with --source-map and no --load: attached pending, judged at the command's entry; any other map refused (exit 1) z88dk-dot-source-rzx-func --source-map with an RZX replay (--rzx-play, --load R.rzx): a dot command's map attaches, any other is refused naming the RZX coverage-frontends-func --coverage starts memory coverage in every loop owner (headless, Qt, SDL)

docs.title: Fixtures
docs.text:
test/fixtures/z88dk/ is what the two z88dk installs actually produce for one small program, committed so that CI, which has no z88dk, can check the adapters against ground truth. Its README.md is the reference: the two installs and their commits, the build matrix (one row per fixture directory with its flags and what it covers), the numbered findings (G1...G24, Z1...Z4) that rows cite, and the rules that normalise and trim the output.

  • Regenerate with bash test/fixtures/z88dk/generate.sh. Overrides: Z88DK_24, Z88DK_MASTER, Z88DK_FIXED and Z88DK_NIGHTLY (the install roots; defaults ~/src/spectrum/z88dk-original-2.4, ...-97731e4e29, ...-latest and ...-965fd0e628). The output is deterministic: git diff --stat must be empty unless an install changed. When one did, commit the new outputs and MANIFEST.sha256 together and say which rows' values moved.
  • The script exits non-zero when a build that should succeed fails, and when one recorded as not producible starts to build (EXPECT_FAIL=1). The failures are recorded too: v2.4/sdcc-debug and v2.4/classic-debug keep only a build.log.
  • MANIFEST.sha256 lists every file the rows hash: sources, the script, the outputs (not README.md). Z88FIX-01 checks every entry's hash; Z88FIX-02 checks the manifest lists exactly the files present.
  • Never hand-edit a fixture. A normalisation or trim that is wrong is fixed in generate.sh ("widen the rule") and the fixtures regenerated. The generated files are normalised so they do not depend on the machine: install paths become z88dk/, temporary names tmpXXXXXXXX, the compile date (normalised).
  • Why committed. CI has no z88dk, and the values are the oracle: every expected address, line and section in a z88dk row comes from these files, never from the code under test.

The dot-command builds are dot:<subtype> lines in generate.sh, compiled from dot.c dutil.c with -subtype=dot, dotx or dotn instead of nex: v2.4/sccz80-dot, sccz80-dotx, sdcc-dot, v2.4-dotn/sccz80 and master/sccz80-dot, sccz80-dotx, sdcc-dot, 80cc-dot. The dotn lives in its own directory so that Z88CN-10's walk over v2.4/ and master/ (every map shows a C name) is not tripped by its refused C symbols. The banked-CRT builds (sccz80-banked-crt, both trees) are the fixtures of the placement by bytes.

test/fixtures/sjasmequ/ is made by hand with an exact command, sjasmplus commit and sha256 per file (its README.md): equlabels.asm is ours, and equlabels.sym, equlabels.exp, equlabels-win.sym (a MinGW build run under wine), equlabels-v1.17.sym (a build of the v1.17.0 tag) and equlabels.sld are what sjasmplus writes for it, byte for byte.

test/fixtures/zdebugmap/ is the trimmed 2.4 maps (debug.map, nodebug.map) of a small program, kept for the symbol rows SYM-14..SYM-18; its README records the trimming.

There is no committed fixture for a Memory.txt or for the SLD identity records; 7.4.5 and 7.4.1 say so and label those excerpts synthetic.

docs.title: Adding a producer
docs.text:
A "producer" is a tool whose output could feed the stores: another assembler, a compiler, a linker. Support is a contract, and the contract is doc/design/SOURCE-LEVEL-DEBUGGING.md section 9.1: "A new format is therefore supported only once this section states its extent and space rules". The checklist, with the file each step touches:

  1. Commit ground truth first. Real output from the real tool, with its version and commit, the exact command, a README and sha256 sums, as test/fixtures/sjasmequ/ does; or a generator script under the rules of test/fixtures/z88dk/ (generate.sh, a manifest, deterministic output). If the tool cannot be run on a CI machine, the output is committed and a manifest row guards it.
  2. State the two rules before writing code. The extent rule: how many bytes a record covers. The space rule: which memory a record belongs to. Write them as the first two parts of a new 7.4 page, with the producer's code cited by tree and line, and quote the grammar from that code.
  3. Emit only qualified ranges. Every SourceRange carries a FetchSource; parse the whole input before anything is replaced; replace a store only on success (7.3). A source half is strict and a symbol half lenient.
  4. Look before you open. Call source_file_problem() (7.3) on every file the adapter opens, unless it must read a pipe.
  5. Dispatch by content. Extend load_source_map() (looks_like_sld() and its neighbours in debugger_source.cpp) and/or MapFormat/Debugger::load_map() so the format is told apart by its contents, never by its extension.
  6. Add it to the sidecar search in load_program_sidecars() if the format sits beside a program, and decide its precedence against the others, in the order and with the owner rules of 7.3. A new extension for a program format goes in the table in source_file.cpp.
  7. Identity. If the format can carry or be given a program identity, decide its form (7.2) and what it does on a landing and for a tape (7.6).
  8. Rows. Literal IDs, in source_map_test for the std-only adapter and in source_debug_test for the backend, with expected values that come from the fixtures; a functional row if a frontend path is new; and the # expect: count updated in test/unit-tests.conf and functional_tests.conf. The IDs must be string literals (the harness refuses a built-up ID), and unique across suites (4.4).
  9. Documentation. The user guide's chapter 10 (the user's side), a new page in 7.4 with the nine parts, a row in the design document's section 9 (the contract), and, if a flag is added, the man page and make cli-check.

docs.title: 7.9 C variables: the variable store
docs.text: A z88dk -debug build puts the program's C debug information in the map as __CDBINFO__ symbols (7.4.3, section 7): one record per function, module, variable and type, in the three compilers' own spellings. The decoder turns one record into a CdbRecord (cdb_decode_symbol(), src/debug/cdb_record.h) and knows nothing else. This page is the layer above it: the variable store (VariableStore, src/debug/variable_store.h), which joins those records to the map's symbols, so that a later consumer can ask where a C variable lives, which function a local belongs to and which scope a code address is in. Reading a value, a frame or a type is not here (last section).

docs.title: What the store holds
docs.text:
VariableStore (class VariableStore, src/debug/variable_store.h:139) is immutable once built. Its five vectors:

Accessor Holds functions() One CFunction per F: record: the decoded record, its name, its module (the module of the entry symbol, never the record line's), entry (a CStorage), its scopes table, its trail (every C_LINE record of the extent, see "The scope table") and its compiler (CCompiler: Sccz80, Zsdcc, Cc80 or Unknown for a synthetic store) variables() One CVariable per S: record, hidden ones included (views hide, the store keeps): the module of its CDB line, the C name, function (an index into functions(), -1 for none) and storage types() Every T: record with its module; the lookup rules (own scope, then a unique tag) belong to the first consumer modules() Every M: record (zsdcc and 80cc only) refused() "<escaped symbol>: <reason>" of every record the decoder refused float_format(module) the float format the module records: the local constants __fp_mode, __fp_exponent_bias and __fp_mantissa_size that sccz80 and 80cc write into every C module they compile (z88dk master from 2026-11-06). A CFloatFormat (mode, exponent_bias, mantissa_size, and why when the module's symbols are unusable: an incomplete set, or two different values of one name); null when the module records none (zsdcc, assembly, z88dk 2.4 and older master) float_library() the fallback for a module with no float_format(): the float library the map names (math32, mbf32, ...: the first non-zero __code_fp_<lib>_size), empty when it names none

A CStorage is resolved or it says why not: a resolved one has the page-aware address (SourceAddress, the same type as a line's start, so a banked variable is Page{20}:$C000) and the map symbol it was joined to. Only E-space records are resolved (data symbols and function entries); stack (B), register (R), code (C), literal (D), port (I) and struct-member (Z) records are kept as they are, and so is a record with an empty type: sccz80 and 80cc write both an enumerator and an I/O port as ({0}) at E,0,0, and neither has memory there, so such a record is never given a storage.

docs.title: Where it lives, and why
docs.text:
The store is a member of the SourceMap it was read from (SourceMap::variables(), src/debug/source_map.h:113), held by a shared_ptr to an immutable object, exactly like the embedded texts of 7.2. SourceMap::replace() takes it as its last argument and stores it (variables_, src/debug/source_map.cpp:127); every replace() without one drops the previous store, and clear() resets it (variables_, src/debug/source_map.cpp:347).

That placement is the design. Debugger::Impl::source_map is assigned, moved, copied or cleared at about ten places (the owner, the stale flag, drop_sidecars(), the tape DeferredCheck, the attachment cache, the ring restore). A store kept beside it would need an edit at each, and a missed one is a store that outlives or misses its map. Inside it, every rule of 7.6 applies with no code of its own: the store is attached with the map, dropped with it, made stale with it, cached and restored with it, and the copies share one object, so the cache costs nothing more.

The facade is Debugger::variables() (variables, src/debug/debugger_source.cpp:578): it runs recheck() first, like every reader, and returns the live source map's store, or null when there is no live map or it carries none (an SLD). A z88dk map with lines but no record carries an empty store, so "this program has no C information" is told from "there is no z88dk map". A map with no lines at all gets no store, because it replaces nothing. Load MAP (symbols only) never has one.

docs.title: How it is filled
docs.text: load_z88dk_source_map() reads the map once. Pass 1 keeps a const line that starts __CDBINFO__ in cdb_lines (src/debug/z88dk_source_map.cpp:732), and the parser gained Z88dkMapLine::is_public (the scope field). The line records of code sections are copied to scope_records right after they are placed and before a listing replaces its module's lines (scope_records, src/debug/z88dk_source_map.cpp:824): a listing's C_LINE keeps only the file, so the scope comes from the map; for an 80cc function the table is replaced by the listing's own occurrences (fill_listing_scopes(), S4a). Just before map.replace(), build_variable_store() (src/debug/z88dk_source_map.cpp:557) decodes each record, joins, and builds the store. A symbol is placed in its space by one lambda, place_symbol (src/debug/z88dk_source_map.cpp:1063), shared by the extent code and the store, so no rule is kept twice.

docs.title: The joins
docs.text:
The key is the module, not the file name (a wrong file name in some records, does not reach JNEXT). Index: (module, name) and public name, each to the placed symbols that carry it. Two or more matches is ambiguous and reported as such; the first is never taken.

Record Joined to Why S:G$x the PUBLIC _x, whatever its module (join_public(), src/debug/z88dk_source_map.cpp:242) A record's module column is its first emitter, not its definer. Measured on master/sdcc-extern (ext_use.c declares extern int g;, ext_def.c defines it): zsdcc writes S:G$g with ext_use_c while _g is public in ext_def_c; sccz80 writes it in ext_def_c. The same collapse makes F:G$other say vars_c while _other is in other_c (master/sccz80-cvars) S:F<file>$x, level 0 _x in the record's module (join_in_module(), src/debug/z88dk_source_map.cpp:232) _s_dup is one symbol in vars_c and another in other_c S:F<file>$st_<fn>_<x>, level > 0 _st_<fn>_<x> in the module; the local belongs to the module's function fn, its C name is x (static_local_function(), src/debug/z88dk_source_map.cpp:302) The writers: src/sccz80/declparse.c:1012, src/80cc/declparse.c:1099. Several candidate functions (a and a_b): left unattributed, with the raw name. 80cc's st_<fn>_<x>_<n> keeps _<n> in the C name, not distinguishable from a name that ends so S:L<scope>.<fn>$x$L_S$B, space E (a zsdcc static local) _<fn>_<x>_<L*10000+S>_<B> in the module (join_variable(), src/debug/z88dk_source_map.cpp:274) SDCC allocLocal(), z88dk/src/sdcc-build/src/SDCCmem.c:876 S:L..., any space function = the one CFunction of that name AND module (function_of(), src/debug/z88dk_source_map.cpp:289) A local exists only in its defining unit; util_inc of a header is two functions, one per module, each with its own v F:G$f the public _f; the function's module is that symbol's F:F<file>$f _f in the record's module

A record that cannot be joined stays, with storage.why (or function == -1). Nothing is dropped.

docs.title: Storage
docs.text: A joined symbol is placed by z88dk_section_space() on its section and value, the same rules as the lines (7.4.3): a numbered section is paged (_btable $14C000 in PAGE_20 is Page{20}:$C000), a dot command's CODE is DivMmcRam{2} (rule 5), and any other section binds to the RAM page the MMU maps there when the map loads (rule 4; outside RAM it is unresolved with the reason). A DIV section or an unplaceable 24-bit value is unresolved with the placement's reason.

docs.title: The scope table
docs.text:
Each function has a table of the scopes its code is in, built from the map's own C_LINE records (fill_scopes(), src/debug/z88dk_source_map.cpp:377). Records at one address are grouped, and the highest line owns the address (the rule the line ranges use). Equal-line owners that disagree make the entry unknown, so no order of the map can change the answer. The entry is filed under the function of the same module and section whose entry map VALUE is the greatest one at or below it (never by comparing spaces: a function that crosses an 8 KB slot lives in two, 7.10), with its offset from that entry.

The compilers write the scope differently:

  • sccz80 and 80cc: file::<func>::<level>::<block>:<line>. The level is the compiler's, the block is the last one opened, not the current one, and 80cc has level 0 everywhere and no block structure. Since z88dk master of 2026-11-04 80cc counts blocks per file in parse order (a __stdc function takes one more for its parameters), writes the open compounds plus the open for headers as the level and the innermost open compound as the block: a for raises the level and opens no block (D-for), and emit_op_cline() skips an op whose line equals the previous one's, so a line holding code of two blocks carries only the first block's scope (D-line). The named function must be the function at the address, or the entry is unknown. This is the line-44 gap: int main(void) is scoped sum::0::2 at _main, and the same address holds line 45 (main::0::3), which owns it; were line 44 alone there, the cross-check makes it unknown instead of giving main the block numbers of sum.
  • zsdcc: zcc's peephole rule writes C_LINE %2,"%1::x::%eval(%3 10000 * %4 +)::%5" (z88dk/lib/sdcc/sdcc_opt.1:313): the function is the literal x, and the number is level * 10000 + sub. A location is zsdcc's when its function field is x and (a TAB follows it, or the function at the address is not named x); then level = n / 10000, sub = n % 10000, and there is no function cross-check. The store decomposes it so both sides of a comparison with the CDB records (which are in (level, sub)) agree.

A location that names only a file and a line, with no scope, is unknown. Visibility is not decided here, but the table keeps what the decision needs:

  • The trail (CFunction::trail): every C_LINE record of the function's extent, not only the owner of each address, in (offset, line) order. A line with no code of its own (for (;;) {) shares its address with the next line and its record is the only one that names its block, so the owners alone are not enough (Z88ZB-02). scopes is unchanged.
  • The compiler of a function (CCompiler, fill_compilers()): from the map alone. 80cc writes M:<file> into its module, the file as its C_LINE records spell it (M:./m.c beside ./m.c::main::...); zsdcc writes M:<module> against the file <module>.c, so it never matches (since z88dk master of 2026-11-05 -debug writes M:m.c, which does match: the x form is what rules 80cc out); sccz80 writes no M: into the map. A module is 80cc iff an M: record names a file field of the module's own C_LINE records and none of them is zsdcc's x form (x with a TAB, or a level of 10000 or more: Z88ZB-10); no M: is sccz80; any other module is zsdcc. The name z80asm gives the module is not used: it prefixes X to a path that starts with ., / or a digit (X__xm_c). An M: name is free text: ( ) [ ] , are accepted; $ is still refused by the decoder.
  • The x placeholder. zsdcc writes the literal x where it names no function. Since z88dk master of 2026-11-05 drops the TAB that used to follow it, x is read as "no function" with or without the TAB (parse_location()), so the alias rule keeps asking later_function_entry() instead of comparing "x" with "x" (Z88ZB-09). A zsdcc function really named x is told by its level (level_raw >= 10000); an sccz80 function named x by its name.
  • Stale stamps. 80cc keeps one global emit location (ir_set_emit_loc(), src/80cc/ir_build.c:7931 once per statement, and src/80cc/ir_build.c:8397 for an if condition); code a construct emits after building its children, with no statement of its own, carries the location of the last statement built. H-a: an if/else closes the then-branch after the else part is built (src/80cc/ir_build.c:8415-8420), so the then-branch's last jump carries the else part's last statement, even when the then-branch has no braces. H-b: the fall-off-end ret (src/80cc/ir_build.c:8669-8673), the switch exit (src/80cc/ir_build.c:8352-8356) and a countdown step (src/80cc/ir_build.c:8258-8268) carry the last statement inside the construct. H-c: CSE and LICM insert a 1cse_<n> / 1licm_<n> declaration before the loop with the hoisted expression's scope (src/80cc/ast_opt.c:4116, src/80cc/ast_opt.c:4190, src/80cc/ast_opt.c:4615). No record excludes any of them for a given block, so an 80cc block local is never listed plain (design 14).
  • 80cc temporaries. 1cse_<n> and 1licm_<n> start with a digit, so no C name can be one: classify() hides a leading-digit name as Temporary (CDB-55), which keeps the level-0 1licm_0 out of the parameters.
  • The x placeholder, again. fill_compilers() also takes a level-0 x record as zsdcc's when the module has no function named x (sccz80 and 80cc write x only for a function really called x, which has an F: record): a zsdcc module whose functions have empty bodies has no TAB and no level above 0 (Z88ZB-15, Z88ZB-16). Undecidable, and left: a zsdcc module whose only function is named x and has an empty body.
  • Two F: records (zsdcc). A zsdcc function with a block static local gets its F: record twice, ...,C,0,-4,... and ...,C,0,0,... (97731e4e29 and 0f0a1cf70e; SDCC's cdbWriteFunction wrote it twice, and the records differ only in the number after the address space, which nothing reads). build_variable_store() keeps the first of records equal up to that number, so the function is one and its variables attach (Z88ZB-17); a record with another type stays a second function (Z88CDB-30).
  • Enum records (z88dk master from 2026-11-05). sccz80 and 80cc write an N: (the enum) and an E: (an enum-typed object) record; cdb_decode() returns them as CdbKind::Enum, checked for shape and dropped by build_variable_store(): the object's S: record is still written with the integer type, which is what the Variables tab reads, so a value shows as its number (CDB-53, Z88ZB-11).
  • Unsized arrays. The decoder classes every {-1}DA-1x record as hidden (sccz80 and 80cc write it first, then the sized one). build_variable_store() unhides one that has no sized twin of the same scope kind, scope name, function, name and module, deciding every record before applying any (Z88ZB-03); it is then listed and refused.

docs.title: Refusals are lenient
docs.text: A record the decoder refuses goes to refused() with its reason; one that cannot be joined stays with its reason. Neither refuses the lines: the strictness of 7.3 protects lines, and a new compiler spelling must not cost the user source-level debugging. Every __CDBINFO__ line of a map ends up in exactly one of functions(), variables(), types(), modules() and refused() (Z88CDB-01).

docs.title: Canonical order
docs.text: The vectors are sorted by the record's text (then module), and a function's scope table by offset, so the store is the same whatever order the map lists its lines in (Z88CDB-20). No map line number is kept. VariableStore's constructor (VariableStore::VariableStore(), src/debug/variable_store.cpp:20) sorts the functions and remaps each variable's function to the sorted index.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
• z80asm keeps the first of two identical symbols (symtab1.c:117), so a record that two modules both write is held once.
  • 80cc's second static of one name, st_<fn>_<x>_<n>, keeps _<n> in the C name.
  • The frame helpers (__debug_framepointer, l_debug_push_frame) are not stored: a hand-loaded z88dk map attaches no symbols, so the next stage adds them to this same pass.

docs.title: Not here
docs.text: Frames, the extents they stand on and the rule that keeps the tracker running are in 7.10. Values, the "location unknown" of sccz80's fastcall parameter, the text that says why no variables are shown, and the type lookup are in 7.10. The store gives them the records, the storage and the scopes.

docs.title: Rows
docs.text: (Z88CDB-41 to -50 and SRCDBG-CVAL-01 to -58: 7.10.) Z88CDB-01 to -26 in z88dk_map_test (the joins, scope tables, order, refusals, banked and dot storage, hidden records, listings), SRCVAR-01 in source_map_test (the member), and SRCDBG-VAR-01 to -12 in source_debug_test (the lifetime). Z88CDB-40 compares every function's scope table on 12 maps with a golden that test/fixtures/z88dk/derive-scopes.py derives from the raw map lines (its header holds the rules). The fixtures are the committed maps; the master/*-extern pair exists for the one case the others lack (7.8).

docs.title: 7.10 C frames and values
docs.text: 7.9 holds the records, the storage and the scopes. This page is what sits on them: the C frames at a stop (Debugger::c_frames()), and the rule that keeps the call-stack tracker running for them. Reading a value (the formatting layer, the type lookup, the C paths, the facade that returns rows) is the next stage of the epic and is not described here yet.

docs.title: The frame base
docs.text:
Every compiler keeps a frame base fp, the address of the saved frame pointer. Write E for the SP at the function's entry instruction (the address of the return address): then fp = E - 2, for all three compilers, and the B records of a variable are offsets from fp.

Compiler How fp is kept Evidence sccz80 (2.4 and master) call l_debug_push_frame at the entry stores E - 2 in __debug_framepointer; the caller's fp is at [fp] z88dk/libsrc/l/sccz80/8-8080/l_debug_push_frame.asm; the vars.c listing of master/sccz80-cvars zsdcc push ix; ld ix,0; add ix,sp (DD E5 DD 21 00 00 DD 39), so IX = E - 2; [IX] is the caller's IX the vars.c listing of master/sdcc-cvars 80cc per function: some use IX, some l_debug_push_frame master/80cc-cvars (sum and main IX, other push-frame) and master/80cc-fc banked banked_call pops its own return address and call l_jphls into the function, so E holds the return address into banked_call and the arguments sit above it z88dk/libsrc/target/zxn/far/zxn_banked_call.asm the epilogue after call l_debug_pop_frame the variable already holds the CALLER's fp; after pop ix IX is the caller's. SP is E only right after that instruction: a __z88dk_callee routine pops its arguments between it and the ret (fc listings of all three compilers), so from the next instruction on the base is not known without the tracker the same listings

The helpers (__debug_framepointer, l_debug_push_frame, l_debug_pop_frame) are joined by public name in CFrameHelpers (struct CFrameHelpers, variable_store.h:111), by the adapter (helpers.framepointer, z88dk_source_map.cpp:676), never from the symbol table: a hand-loaded map attaches no symbols. They are unresolved, with a reason, in a zsdcc map.

docs.title: Which function a PC is in
docs.text:
A function's extent is a list of pieces (CPiece, variable_store.h:57). fill_extents() (z88dk_source_map.cpp:328) bounds the extent above by the lowest map value, in the same section, of another function's entry, a symbol or line record of another module, or the section's __<section>_tail; then it splits [entry, bound) at the 8 KB logical boundaries and places each piece with the rule the symbols use. A function that crosses a slot lives in two spaces (a NEX code group is placed slot by slot: page 4 for $8000-$9FFF, page 5 for $A000-$BFFF). With no bound, pieces is empty and extent_why says so: the function then contains no PC.

VariableStore::locate() (variable_store.cpp:52) answers "which function, and how far into it" from a SourceAddress: the piece with the same space whose range holds the address. Nothing else is used, neither the nearest symbol nor a jump target. The scope tables follow the same rule (fill_scopes(), z88dk_source_map.cpp:377): a record is filed under the function of its module and section whose entry value is the greatest at or below the record's, and each CScope carries its offset from the entry, so tables compare across pieces. Comparing spaces would lose the tail of a function that crosses a slot (cross.c, in the *-cross fixtures).

docs.title: The frames
docs.text:
